Subject: Silent, hovering, 'triangular'-shaped objects 4/4

UFO Research List

 One of the last of the Lumberton people to be favored with a viewing
of the weird craft, Strickland was also treated to one of its most
spectacular, dramatic displays. Driving with his wife at 5:15 p.m.,
Sunday, April 6--the last day of the visitation--Strickland says he saw
the thing directly over the road ahead. The veteran lawman described a
spellbinding, sweeping, hawk-like dive toward a field only 100 yards
away.

 "I slowed down and my wife let out a gasp because she thought it was
going to hit a farmhouse," he said. "But the thing just disappeared
behind the farm buildings--without a sound."

 The first of the scores of reports came shortly after 1 a.m. on April
3 (of 1975). "We were swamped with calls from the public and 30 officers
reported seeing a strange object," submitted Lumberton sheriff's radio
dispatcher Ronn Thompson. Most of the callers-in said they had seen the
UFO over the north end of the rural hamlet.

 "I saw the object hovering about 50 feet over the town's water tank,"
said officer Phil Stanton, one of the policemen who received calls from
citizens who were, if not frightened, certainly very impressed at what
many thought was a drop-in from extragalactic beings.

  "It seemed to be triangular or vee-shaped. I could make out reddish
lights on one side of it and green or blue lights along the other. I
thought it was about the size of a Cadillac. The strange thing was that
there was no sound at all. It appeared to have a solid hull and one big
spotlight."

 Just as the mystified officer began to register that he was seeing
something that he couldn't do anything about-- and something that very
few others could expect ever to see--the strange object vanished,
hurtling away at almost unearthly speed. And then--"I heard on my patrol
car radio that it was spotted over St. Pauls just 90 seconds later. And
St. Pauls is 15 miles away," he said.

  Over in St. Pauls, security guard John McPherson and officer Tom
Hagens chased the triangular mystery in a patrol ear. Their first
glimpse of it came with a red flash "like an explosion," behind some
trees way back in the boondocks. The strange craft was moving low and
slow across an isolated country road and the officers saw their duty.

 "We took off after it, but lost it. Then we stopped the car and just
waited," reported McPherson. And then, as though playing an
interplanetary game of tag, "There it was again ... it seemed to be
triangular, maybe vee-shaped, with blue lights all around the edges and
a big pulsating ball of red light in the center. There were two big
beams like searchlights. The next thing I knew, it took off at terrific
speed--without a sound.

 If that isn't the same whatsis that Stanton saw four days later, it
must at least have been a sister ship.

 And suddenly, the same ship or one much like it turned up a few miles
away. When McPherson and Hagens last saw it in St. Pauls, it was racing
west. Soon it was picked up by Hoke County Deputy Sheriff George
McGuire. "It seemed to be travelling about the speed of a jet, but far
closer to the ground than I've ever seen a jet fly," he recalled.

 Reports of mysterious doings in the North Carolina skies kept pouring
in. The Lumberton radio dispatcher, Ronn Thompson, found that his
curiosity was whetted by all the reports he had received from presumably
sane and sober citizens. So off he went on his own UFO hunt when he got
off duty Friday night. Sure enough about 20 miles southwest of Lumberton
he really did spot it.

  "It appeared suddenly, less than 200 feet above my car," he told
reporters later. "I could see a beam shining out of the thing and
flashed my car lights. Incredibly, the beam flashed back at me in
response. I flashed my lights a second time and again I got a response.

 "Then the object took off at tremendous speed and vanished."

  There were more reports. A police chief, Gary Moore, of White Lakes,
N.C., said he spotted a similar triangular UFO with a pulsating red
light just about at dawn on Saturday, April 5. But the visit to
Lumberton was nearing an end. One more cop, State Trooper Marshall
McGee, was to make a sighting in the early hours of Sunday, April 6.
He saw something in the sky between Lumberton and St. Pauls and his
description was substantially the same as those submitted by many
others.

  Naturally, the Federal Aviation Administration was consulted and, as
happens so often, it was, officially, baffled. Authorities at the nearby
Fayetteville, N.C., Airport were notified almost as soon as the UFO was
first spotted. "We had a Piedmont Airlines Boeing 737 make a test flight
in the area," said an FAA spokesman "But the UFO reports continued after
it landed "

 And not only are the civilian flying folk stumped. An Air Force
official at the nearby Fort Bragg flying facility admitted, "We're
just as baffled as the FAA."
*E-O-F*
This is one of the earliest documented reports with clear
parallels to the silent, hovering 'triangular' objects of more
recent years.

A 'pulsating', central red light is a distinctive feature of such
accounts, many which are similarly, 'highway encounters'.


With little apparent leeway for mistaken identifications of
stars, or indeed any of the normal rational explanations, what
could be the origin of all these comparative reports?

Date: Sat, 8 Oct 1994 13:45:24 -0400From: Dennis Mercer

Subject: sightings

Excerpts from Aviation Week Oct 1, 1990 pg. 20:

MULTIPLE SIGHTINGS OF SECRET AIRCRAFT HINT AT NEW PROPULSION,
AIRFRAME DESIGNS

Multiple reports from well-qualified observers lend substantial
credence to the existence of numerous secret aircraft flying from
remote bases in the south-western U.S., regardless of the
political, funding or technical arguments against that
probability.

Over the past 13 months, large, triangular wing-shaped aircraft
characterized by a relatively quiet propulsion system have been
the objects of at least 11 sightings near Edwards, AFB, Calif.,
and one near Fresno, Calif. These are supported by additional
reports of similar vehicles seen and heard around remote central
Nevada communities near government ranges operated by the Energy
Dept. and the Air Force.

Possibly prototypes of concept demonstrators of the Air Force B-2
or Navy A-12, the fairly flat, triangular-shaped vehicles have a
rounded nose, rounded wingtips and probably no vertical tail
surfaces. The flying wings' trailing edges may be slightly
curved, but definitely are not sawtooth-shaped like those of the
Air Force's B-2 bomber, according to reports received so far. One
observer in Nevada described the shape as "like a manta ray."

Key sightings include:

* A daytime observation near the Tehachapi mountains (about 30
mi. northwest of Edwards AFB) in early May verified this craft's
triangular shape. Numerous earlier sightings had been at night,
although several were under a near-full moon that provided enough
illumination to identify a large, triangular planform. The
Tehachapi report noted that the aircraft was light-colored, but
had a dark area near the center of the trailing edge, presumed to
be the engine exhaust area.

* On the night of May 3, 1990, a quiet aircraft matching the
triangular description was reported by five different observers
over a 4-hr. period. One or more of the aircraft made multiple
passes over Tehachapi, Mojave, Lancaster and Palmdale, Calif.,
during this time.

* A triangular aircraft also has been seen flying with multiple-
ship Lockheed F-117A flights. Typically, the stealth fighters fly
alone, spaced about 8-10 min. apart - a general pattern that has
characterized F-117 operations since they were first observed in
California in mid-1989.

However, on several occasions, the larger, triangular aircraft
appeared on the same general flight path as the F-117As. It was
seen after about three or four of the stealth fighters had
passed, yet was ahead of another three or four. It has been
spotted repeatedly over the northern end of the Antelope Valley,
near Edwards AFB and Mojave, Calif., as well as in central
Nevada.

This vehicle is quieter that the F-117As - which already are
substantially quieter than an F-15 or F-16 - and definitely
larger. It normally displays a lighting pattern similar to that
of the F-117s - single amber lights under the wingtips and a red
beacon near the nose - but can be distinguished by its
characteristic hushed engine noise and larger planform.

All observer descriptions of the triangular aircraft correlated
closely, and the observer who reported seeing the vehicle before
sunset sketched a top view. That sketch matched descriptions of
similar vehicles supposedly seen in Nevada-based government
hangars several years ago and flying in military operating areas
nearby...

A totally separate, distinctly different type of aircraft seen
and heard in California and Nevada over the last year is
characterized by a loud, very deep, rumbling engine noise, At
times, the exhaust noise is punctuated by a slow-frequency (about
1 Hz.) pulsing sound, which has prompted observers to call this
aircraft the "pulsar." The aircraft also produces a sausage-link-
shaped smoke trail or vapour contrail when it is pulsing. This
vehicle is not the triangular-shaped aircraft discussed earlier,
and may be capable of hypersonic speeds.
At other times however, the aircraft exhibits a more continuous
noise without the pulsing characteristic. Observers are confident
it is the same type of aircraft, based on its distinctive deep,
loud roar.

There have been multiple reports of "pulsar" flights, including:

* The first, in July, 1989, at about 3 a.m. near Edwards AFB,
Calif. The vehicle was at medium altitude, flying very fast and
exhibiting the characteristic pulsing sound. The "pulsar's"
position was marked by a *white glow*, rather than a distinct
point of light.

* An early evening takeoff from Edwards AFB on Oct. 18, 1989.

* Multiple reports of an aircraft having a deep, pulsing roar
flying over central and eastern Nevada during the early morning
hours throughout the past year.

* Eight separate reports of an aircraft exhibiting the same
characteristics, always flying on a northerly heading near
Mojave, Calif., between midnight and about 5 a.m. It was
typically at lower altitude and slower speeds than when first
seen in July, often had a slower pulsing sound and displayed only
two position lights.

* Six reports of an extremely fast-moving vehicle in southern
California's skies, ranging from Santa Barbara on the Pacific
coastline to near George AFB at the eastern end of the Antelope
Valley. These aircraft typically were flying at very high
altitude, were seen as a *single bright light*, and seldom
changed direction. Speed changes have been observed, and, on
occasion, a pulsing red or white light was seen. Whether these
so-called fast movers also are the "pulsar" aircraft is not
known.

A Santa Barbara observer estimated the aircraft crossed "some 350
mi. of night sky off the Pacific Missile Range bases in about 6
min." (about 3450 mph!) One Aviation Week & Space Technology
editor estimated a similar aircraft - seen as a bright point of
white light - required less than 20 sec. to tranit [? - James]
about 70 deg. of sky...

On Oct. 18, 1989, the "pulsar" apparently took off from North
Base, an airfield at the north end of the Edwards AFB complex
primarily devoted to classified programs. The noise from that
takeoff was described as extremely loud, with a deep, throaty
rumble that shook houses 16 mi. away, drawing residents into the
street. One observer claimed the noise compared with that of
Saturn 5 rocket tests conducted at Edwards AFB in the 1960s and
1970s.

Although no lights were seen, the deep, vibrating roar continued
for about 5 min., and its source appeared to be climbing steeply
to the north. "Your eyes tended to follow the noise; something
was climbing at a very steep angle," one observer noted.
Residents of surrounding communities reported that the sound "was
like the sky ripping," and was unlike anything they had heard in
the Edwards area for years.

The same pulsing, very loud, rumbling type of engine noise has
been reported by multiple observers in central Nevada as well. It
typically was heard in the early morning hours and was described
as having a 1-2 Hz. pulse rate. One Nevada-based observer said
the same pulsing aircraft departed from the Groom Lake range and
flew over a nearby community as recently as Aug. 6. It was "the
loudest thing I've ever heard. It wasn't breaking the sound
barrier, but it was rattling the window!" *


An interesting note: one of the drawings accompanying the text
shows the object as a very rounded triangular shape glowing
orange!
[End]


The reported Edwards AFB sightings are intriguing. This is an
account I documented and although impossible to be sure, had no
reason to believe wasn't a sincere recollection, apparently
dating from sometime in 1995. Julia related:

"I swear this craft just appeared over my head. This was at about
10:00 a.m. on a bright, sunny day. There was one of those
skyquakes, then in a minute or two after that, (I was outside)
the atmosphere seemed to get "heavy" like it was pushing down on
me, and it got warm. I have dogs and they were growling and when
I looked up, suddenly this craft was over my head, fairly close
too. I felt it there before I actually saw it. I did not see it,
or hear it approach except for noticing the change in the
atmosphere, suddenly it was just there, as if becoming visible
for the first time.

It appeared to be gunmetal gray, almost black, but not quite. I'd
say the shape was - triangular, a regular triangle. It was
exactly like the craft - well, no, but very close to the craft in
the second episode of the X-Files.

I'm not sure how to describe how big this craft was. It was big,
but not giant. It was wider than a helicopter but not as wide as
the stealth fighter wing span, or maybe it was close to that. And
it was very close to me, so close that I had a hard time keeping
my eyes open because of the pressure it caused in the air. The
eerie part was the silence for a craft hovering so close. It
wasn't far above the roof of our kennel and looked close enough
to almost touch. I'm not a very good judge of measurements so I
can't say for sure how high above me it actually was, but it
seemed rather close, I'd guess about 25 feet.

I was almost directly below it, so I only saw the bottom. It had
lights around the edges of the triangle, but I couldn't say how
many and they didn't appear to be on. I can say for certain that
I saw lights at each one of the three corners of the craft and at
least one on each of the sides. I did see what appeared to be
either a large light or a window directly in the centre of the
triangle.

I can't say if the edges were round or flat as I couldn't really
focus on it for a long time because I couldn't keep my eyes open.
It was sort of like standing under helicopter blades - you have
to shield your eyes. I didn't hear any engines or whirring or
humming, and there was no real air movement to speak of, just
this pressurized feeling and the warmth.

It was there about a minute, give or take a few seconds, then it
disappeared from view - I did not see the craft move at all, it
just wasn't visible anymore. It disappeared just as suddenly as
it appeared and was gone again without any visible movement. It
was pretty creepy. I'm not unused to seeing things in the sky. I
don't live that far from Edwards Air Force Base, as the crow
flies and I'm used to seeing the stealth planes, even when they
denied the existence of them. Those looked like giant bats in the
distant sky. This triangular craft was the same color as the
stealth planes, which leads me to believe they are experimental
military planes.
[End]


Could be, however, why was a 'top secret' aircraft hovering so
close above Julia's place?

Did it 'decloak' with the wrong co-ordinates, just missing the
base and then quickly engage 'invisibility mode' again?

Nonsense, surely.

Yet, the 'Aviation Week' article implies there is substance to
the 'mysterious aircraft' sightings, which to the public would
presumably be 'UFOs'.

'Tis the proverbial 'hall of mirrors'!
James.

UFO Research List

For a list which claims to be dedicated to serious discussion of the UFO
subject I find it quite remarkable that so many half-baked accounts should
be used to support the moderators unsupported view that FTs are' alien
craft'.

Although I understand that researchers will drag out any sighting, whether
it has been checked and/or properly investigated (which hardly ever
happens, in the past or these days), to prove their untenable position, it
is odd that nobody that I - or anyone associated with research into black
projects OR who is actually involved in developing it - has ever said
anything about recovered alien technology or supported a view that FTs are
'alien craft'.

For those out there who fail to understand, delta planforms are evidence of
basic aerodynamics. If people had bothered to read my book ("UFO
Revelation" - check it out, just published and on the subject or aircraft
not UFOs)) they would have seen that in terms of FTs these have been on the
drawing boards since the 1930s and developed in earnest both in the US,
Germany and England from the 1940s onwards.

The US Navy has, since the early 1970s, and initially in conjunction with
the Aereon Corporation, sought to develop massive delta planforms for
reconnaissance. The Aereon Corporation boss William Miller Jr. believes
that the military 'borrowed' his ideas and translated them into hardware.
The large delta platform hybrid LTA craft would be made of something like
Kevlar, be able to operate in silence and/or produce a slight humming sound
(due to it's airship-like propulsion system) and yet, according to maverick
genius Michael Walden, also operate at high speeds with an ability to
accelerate away.

What concerns me about the sightings mentioned here is that, apart from
Hudson Valley and Belgium, they seem to conform to a set pattern of
'unusual' experiences followed by reporting that indicates an overactive
imagination.

I am getting to the point where I, and I'm not alone, am giving up on "UFO"
sightings at all because they're all the UFO community (that utterly
unscientific believer cult) has to offer. Even in terms of the Rendlesham
debate we are expected to believe stories from witnesses dredged up years
after the event and which might be explained easily, as Ripdath and co have
said. Instead of this we find a desperate grasping at straws in the hope
that we can prop up this case, or the subject, and somehow make it
credible.
In a recent newsletter circulated by former 'Strange Daze' editor Dave
Newton he suggested that people like me, and those interested in other
areas of study that may occasionally affect Ufology, go our separate ways
and engage in research into earth lights, secret military aircraft and so
on. This is now happening.

There has been an outright refusal by the UFO community, as evidenced by
some of the postings on this supposedly 'expert' list already, to accept
(or even look into the possibility) that the military does have things that
are so advanced as to shock even those within the military-industrial
complex. The amounts of money and scientific expertise given over to the
development of advanced aircraft and still-classified black projects over
the years has been huge and as I said in a previous post exotic propulsion
systems have been a possibility (and more likely a reality in more recent
years) since Brown and Biefeld came across their strange electrical effect
in 1929.

It might have come to the attention of at least some of you that Thomas
Townsend Brown, whose electrogravitics work was supported by Lockheed after
the war, was also a founder of NICAP. So was Hillenkoeter whose Navy discs
were annoying our forebears. This small example indicates that the
military-industrial complex is where the answers to these supposed
'problems' lie...

In terms of electrogravitics systems it is interesting to note very similar
configurations in terms of the circular wings they hoped to fly at Mach 3
and the 'Project Silver Bug' discs. Of course it's all still classified
(well most of it) and into the breach falls ever so much ill-informed
Ufological speculation.......I wonder whether we should take any witnesses
seriously anymore. In the last few weeks I've received over 100 calls from
UFO witnesses in West Lancashire and their descriptions of the same objects
(seen from different locations) are so widely varied as to make a mockery
of the claims that people 'know' what they're looking at - whether they're
supposed 'trained observers' (no such thing) or not!

No, flying triangles are military - and you take that to the bank.

Ufology? A bad and worsening joke. No wonder most of the best people leave.
Nobody wants to hear explanations......or so it seems.

Tim Matthews.

Mr Matthews,

I beg to differ. It is not so much your basic premise which is that UFOs could
very well be earth based technology - which after all, is a theory that I view
on equal terms as the ETH - it is the data one generally provides to merit this
theory.

First of all, deltawinged aircraft were on the drawing board as early as 1896,
even before, and not since the 1930's as you claim. Likewise, utopian scetches
of the first circular shaped aeroforms appeared around the 1880's, and around
1910 one was actually built.
Exotic propulsion systems and antigravity? In the USA an inventor started to
experiment with that as early as the 1870's, I have photo's of his huge device,
developed for a proposed earoform, that should be made of aluminium, 60 feet
diameter, ovalshaped and airtight, so that one `could travel with it to other
planets'. In 1895 someone drew up plans for an aeroform propelled on
electromagnetism, and in 1910 another such proposal was made in Russia. All of
the above is now matter of history and will be backed by proper references,
illustrations and verifiable data in my new book on this subject. This is but a
small part of what I have collected over the years.

So, what I want to say is, if there is a joke, it is more to be found in
incomplete research that is generally conducted on both sides, be they the ETH
or man-made scenario's, and I would suggest anyone to turn around and start
digging again.

Kind regards,

Theo Paijmans

I hear this all the time from Ufologists and given that the vast majority
of data is still classified by the US government/military how are we
supposed to make the kind of quick and easy progress - and therefore quick
and easy answers - that Ufologists want?

There are also situations where people contact me and where I cannot
divulge their information because they won't let me use their name, or
simply want to tell me what took place. Often that's as far as it goes.

Let me give you an example. A man with detailed knowledge of US Navy discs
projects that continued until around 1980/1 and which were developed at
China Lake in California, came forward and said that basically there had
been an unbroken line of development in terms of these aircraft since the
initial work on the V-173 and XF5U-1 from 1944. That jet-powered pancakes
existed is not in doubt although there were only a few models in the early
part of the postwar period. The later aircraft were to some extent stealthy
utilizing shrouded turbofans etc. Our man was prepared to go on the record
until he was visited by people from the ONI - Office for Naval
Intelligence.

He immediately clammed up......and threatened legal action if we took his
story further.

!!NOTE - the US Navy is by far the biggest operator of advanced military
aircraft!!

This is the reality of research. How can the military admit that they had
more than the 'Avrocar' or XF5U-1 without opening up a Pandora's Box of
wild speculation? Realistically how do they declassify tens of millions of
documents? There is still a great deal of secrecy surrounding these
projects - there are so many problems - although we can make a good case
for Man-Made UFOs with the material already in our possession.

If people aren't listening then that's not my problem....

In my first and recently published book "UFO Revelation - The Secret
Technology Exposed?" (Blandford 1999) much of the material I now have on
flying disc technologies was not available to me and will need to be
included in a second book. To some extent the cover-up, if there is one, is
entirely within the UFO community, perhaps encouraged by Doty-like figures
on the fringes; UFO Magazines will not publish this kind of material on a
regular basis and realize that they need to print rubbish about crashed
alien craft, animal mutilations and MJ-12 type conspiracies in order to
maintain the interest of a gullible public. Other publishers need
Santilli-type 'disclosures' to woo their readers and to wax lyrical about
'Cosmic Consciousness' and ET contact. None of these things are actually
based in reality but then the UFO audience is fed a diet of bullshit
largely by a small and exclusive group of seemingly well-funded researchers
who have been in the field for years AND who have promoted so many lies
that it is impossible for people to consider earthly realities any more.

I think that earthbound solutions are far more exciting but I'm in a
minority for sure!

I'm even afraid that many people reading this, on the 'expert' list, hope
that some of the above fantasies are true. I get this impression from some
of the posts. Perhaps people here just have higher standards or better
filters....?

The truth is that in terms of advanced discplanes the missions that these
a/c undertook REMAIN CLASSIFIED - we have been told this by the US military
via refusals to declassify material that we KNOW they have hidden away. In
addition I don't see why I should spend thousands of pounds on research
only for some Ufological half-wit to come along and plagiarize it!

In order to work with other researchers there has to be trust - and
precious little trust exists in within or outside this subject.....

I'm afraid that sightings do, at best, only hint at the wider scenario. My
main efforts now are much slower - in terms of results - because I feel
that I can no longer rely upon the UFO community to assist in this research
to any useful extent because it is not interested in the actual truth of
the matter.

David Windle said that when I published some results they would be attacked
by the people on this and other lists not because they were wrong but
because they threaten the ideological basis of UFO beliefs;

In other words; discs and triangles are entirely of military origin
therefore NO "ET technology" and NO "ET craft". Therefore psycho-social
theories seem a little shaky because obviously some reports relate to
actual structured classified technology - and not a flight of fancy.
Various other areas for research are still open - studies into
consciousness, altered states, hypnogogia etc. etc. and of course
'earthlights'. I think that these fields of study will explain almost all
of the so-called "UFO Mystery". Just because we cannot collectively explain
all cases means very little; it simply means that we have alot of bad data
that, in general, comes from questionable sources.

After all, the big threat here is to the UFO subject. What if there are no
'UFOs' and only objects, craft, lights etc. that are REPORTED as
'UFOs'....?
I will be doing my best to get further information about these aircraft but
until a few people in America buck their ideas up and offer assistance
little progress will be made because the answers lie there. It takes time
AND money to get to the bottom of this. If I lied about my views maybe I'd
do better and be richer but I'm not prepared to do that.

It's a shame because there are so many leads to follow up - even though the
EThers and skeptics have a 40 year head start!!

Other answers lie within the former Soviet Union. It should be remembered
that former E. German STASI head Dr. Michael Wolf admitted in an interview
for Union Pictures "Riddle of the Skies" documentary that the Soviets had
developed and flown discplanes. No wonder the American felt that they had
to develop similar aircraft and no wonder the interview never made it onto
our screens!!

Of course any research trip to the former USSR without armed guards would
be a bad move at this time!

But it's all still classified.....

Tim Matthews.

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 1999 17:39:52 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Re: Silent, hovering, 'triangular'-shaped objects

UFO Research List

The following summary account contains the testimony of a
gentlemen named Steven Suddell. I documented this over a period
of time and he confirmed the verbatim summary to be an accurate
record:


[Start]
The time, i.e. year, is now hard for me to remember but the
events remain as clear as though it was yesterday.

I was living in St. Brides Major, a small village near Bridgend,
South Wales. I was around 16 years old then and keen on
astronomy. This fixes the date somewhere between 1974 and 1976.
The exact dates I have recorded in a small log book. This book,
if I still have it, is buried in my attic somewhere.

I was sitting at my bedroom window with telescope in hand looking
out of the window for something to gaze at. The field of view
from this window was good. There was a large playing field and
single storey school to the right. Approximately 600 yards
directly ahead there was a row of houses, with trees beyond and
beyond that the Severn estuary, although this could not be seen.
To the left were the backs of a row of houses and the main
village road was the other side of them. It was Autumn/Winter as
there were no leaves on the trees.

I searched around the sky for something to look at and I caught
sight of a red star high to the right. I say star as I had a good
idea of where the planets currently were and there were none in
this area. I continued to look around and decided that the red
star was the best thing to look at. I sat myself on the window
ledge and raised my telescope. As I did so the star started to
move. Ah, I thought a satellite, but hang on, it couldn't
possibly be because it was stationary for some time.

It moved diagonally downwards from high right to right of
slightly ahead (when viewed from the window). The light, as I now
thought of it, remained a constant size and brightness. The light
got to tree level and levelled off to move horizontally, left to
right across my field of view but behind the distant trees. I
continued to catch glimpses of it and it started to move up and
down also. It seemed to be moving in an entirely random fashion.
At this point I called my father. I suggested to him that it was
a helicopter searching for someone/thing in the estuary. My
father thought it was probably moving a bit to quick for this.

As we both continued to watch, it started to come towards us. As
it got closer two more lights appeared, also red. It became
apparent that whatever it was, was going to pass directly over
our house and quite low at that. We both rushed outside, grabbing
my mother on the way. We stood in the garden and watched this
thing approach our house. As it got closer we could see that the
three lights, all red, were arranged in a triangular
configuration (i.e., at the corners of a would be equilateral
triangle). The lights illuminated the inside of the triangle but
not the outer. They appeared to shine inward, albeit that's how
it seemed. What was illuminated can only be described as
something metallic. It appeared to be a metallic surface that was
dull. It did not shine as there were no light reflections in it.
I say metallic because that what I felt at the time. The material
appeared to be a silvery-grey colour. However, bear in mind that
this was observed under red light. It was one piece, i.e. between
the lights, there appeared to be no joints, rivet lines, beams,
etc., just a flat, dull, metal surface.

The lights were constantly on, they did not flash or go out at
any time.

To be honest, I didn't really notice anything outside of the
triangle bounded by the lights because I was looking at the lit
area. I mean the craft could have been square, rectangular,
banana, or round shaped, I just did not see this, all I saw was
this image created by the effects of the lights that gave it the
appearance of being triangular in shape.

As to size, well, this depends on the height but I would say that
it had to be about 20-30 feet between the lights. And
irrespective of what height it was at I had the feeling that it
was a big craft.

As to how high it was, it's very hard to say. I had the feeling
at the time that it was quite low, a few hundred feet, but it was
very hard to judge. The feeling I got was that it was below 500
feet.

There were no other lights or distinguishing features _visible_
on the object.

We expected to hear the noise of rotor blades or something. There
was not a sound. It was a very still night so we should have
heard something. It moved almost directly over our house. If you
were to project the image of the craft down onto the ground, it
would have appeared about 20 feet from where we were standing.
It then abruptly moved to the left. It had made a right 90 degree
turn in a totally dumfounded way - like a ball bouncing off a
cushion in snooker. The lights remained in the exact
configuration and did not change. The whole thing was weird, it
was as though this craft was gliding at a very slow speed. It did
not pause or hover over the house, it went about this direction
change as one fluid movement. When the craft came towards us it
had the point to the front (1 light in front and two behind).
When it made the turn, it moved to the side and it did not
rotate.

This was the thing that really made me think it was something
odd, because things just couldn't move that way.

We continued to watch this craft as it disappeared off to what
would be the left of my window. We had no idea what it was.

My father was quite excited about it. What he saw struck him as
being odd also. Normally he is a realistic man and would have
said, "it's just a low flying aircraft or something", but he
didn't. He decided to phone the local airport - Roose, now called
Cardiff, Wales. They had nothing up at all and hadn't for some
time. He then called the local RAF base at St. Athen. He spoke to
a very nice man who told him that he was not aware of anything
flying, however he would call the tower - where they are on
constant radar vigil and call us back.

Shortly after the gent from the RAF called back. He informed us
that the tower had not picked up anything on their radar and they
also had nothing flying.

And that was it. We heard no more about it. I told a couple of
mates and discussed it with them. But no one else had seen it.
[End]


It was an unusual account of what _ may _ have been a triangular-
shaped object. At face value, it was an apparent object which
exhibited these silent, slow moving, low-altitude
characteristics.

Perhaps a 'blimp' of some kind?

The sudden, "fluid" change of direction, described as similar to
a ball bouncing off a snooker (or pool) table cushion, was
intriguing and any comparative reports would be of interest.


James.

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 1999 18:33:32 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Re: Silent, hovering, 'triangular'-shaped objects 1/2

UFO Research List

Another historical account from the UK and one which does feature
a triangular, or delta-shaped object, observed at close range:

[Start]
The following story is absolutely true and describes my only
"close encounter".

As a Chartered Accountant, I often have to oversee audit
assignments with a strict timetable. This leads to the need to
work long hours. In March 1978, I was working on such an
assignment in my home county of Lincolnshire, UK. One Thursday
night, I finished work at about 10.30pm and drove a colleague
home to the village of Alford. In general, the coastal areas of
Lincolnshire are very flat.

However, Alford lies on the edge of gently rolling countryside -
the Lincolnshire Wolds. My route home took me up a hill on the
A1104 towards Ulceby Cross. Part way up the hill, at around 11:00
p.m., I was dazzled by what I took to be the undipped headlights
of an oncoming car. I flashed my own headlights and slowed. To my
astonishment, the oncoming lights slowly "took off" from the road
and gracefully flew to my right. Excitedly, I stopped my car,
wound down the driver's side window and peered out. The sight
that greeted me will stay in my memory forever.

I saw that the lights were coming from a massive, beautiful
aircraft which had now turned, was flying at a height of about 50
feet and was now heading towards the coast directly over my car!
The craft was shaped like a delta, very similar to the Vulcan
bombers based in Lincolnshire at the time.

However, it was about four times the size of a Vulcan, flew
extremely slowly and was absolutely silent! All leading edges of
the delta were beautifully rounded - there were no sharp
protuberances such as a tailplane. The underside of the craft was
coloured sky blue. It just glided over me and headed towards the
coast - no noise, no smoke, no vibrations, no smell - just an
aircraft of sheer gargantuan beauty.

It was very real; from the A16 I was able to watch this craft
making its slow, majestic way south towards Boston until I lost
sight of it just past Spilsby. I'd love to know what it was. It
seemed too real to be extraterrestrial. However, its immense
size, its low speed and above all, the sheer silence made it
unlike any aircraft known to me!

Paul H Hanmer FCA



Asked if he would answer some questions about this encounter,
Paul was exceptionally helpful and elaborated further on a number
of points:

Do you recall the exact date of the incident?

At the time, we did keep diaries; but those diaries were
destroyed many years ago (they were used as a primary record of
time spent on our various clients.) Therefore, I have no accurate
existing aide memoire as to the exact date. It was in March 1978,
before Easter (the audit had to completed by Maundy Thursday- a
directors' meeting had been arranged for that day!) I would
expect (recalling our pattern of working) that the sighting would
have been on a Tuesday or Thursday night. The sighting was at
approximately 11pm.


What material would you describe the object as being made of?

Another question that's difficult to answer. The craft appeared
to be perfectly "solid", so it wasn't constructed of anything
flimsy. It didn't flex in its movement but remained rigid. I
would therefore assume that it was made of a metallic element. I
would not say that it was a hard, cold metal. It seemed to be
soft and warm - maybe like a cross between aluminium and
manganese.


Did it reflect any available light?

The area of the sighting is very rural - surrounded by
agricultural property. Although the village of Alford was behind
me, the village is small and quiet and does not emanate much
light. The only immediate light (other than that on the craft)
would have come from the headlights of my car and from another
car, which came down the hill towards me after I had stopped (see
later - witnesses.) However, I recall seeing the underside of the
craft in its entirety. I have already described it as being light
blue, but maybe it had a luminescent nature. Thinking about it,
there was nothing else, other than the crafts forward lights, to
reflect that amount of light. I saw it in the black of night and
yet my memory of the underside was as if I'd seen it in daylight.
What approximate height was it flying at and did it ever change
altitude?

When flying along the coast, its altitude was constant. It was
quite low; I would guess 50 feet or so. That would also have been
its altitude when it passed over my car. Although I do not have a
PPL, I have flown in a Cessna along that stretch of coast. The
coastline constitutes land reclaimed from the sea and is
uniformly flat.


Although it maintained a constant altitude, was that after it
"took off" from the road? When you first saw the lights, is it
possible to say if the object was perhaps stationary on the road,
i.e., that it had possibly landed. Given its size, would that
have been feasible without damaging any bushes or trees by the
roadside?

The road from Alford to Ulceby (A1104) goes uphill (quite unusual
for this part of Lincolnshire.) When I first saw the lights, I
was at the bottom of the hill and the lights were at the top. So,
my perception as the lights "left the road" was that they moved
to my right rather than upwards. In retrospect, I suppose that
the craft came over the hill towards me at just above tree height
and maintained that altitude rather than following the contour of
the land down the hill.


How wide and how deep was the object?

I will not try to give you dimensions in feet and inches (or
metres and centimetres.) Other than the craft itself, and a few
small trees, I had sight of no other structure by which I could
gauge it. However, I could compare it to the Vulcan bombers with
which I was familiar (the Vulcan squadron was based at RAF
Waddington, Lincoln at the time.) I would say that the area of
the delta was about four times that of the Vulcan. The depth of
the delta was about the same as the cabin section of a Boeing
747. As far as I can recall, the depth was the same throughout
the delta.


Continued...

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 1999 18:33:46 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Re: Silent, hovering, 'triangular'-shaped objects 2/2

UFO Research List

Were all three sides of the triangle of equal size?

Yes, they were; and perfectly dimensioned to boot. There were no
sharp edges. Even the tail angles of the delta were beautifully
and smoothly rounded.


You mentioned lights being visible. Can you describe them in
detail and say whether they were on at all times?

At first I thought the lights were car headlights and they
dazzled me. As the craft flew towards the side of my car it
became obvious that two distinct beams were emanating from the
"nose" of the delta and were aimed directly towards the ground
(i.e. they were not aimed at the ground in front of the craft but
came directly down at 90 degrees from the delta.) The two beams
remained on at all times I had sight of the craft and in fact, it
was these beams which enabled me to track the craft from my
vantage point on the A16. The beams seemed to have the same
intensity of white light throughout their entire length.
Strangely, the width of the beams was also the same throughout
their length. They did not splay out as would a spotlight or
searchlight beam.


Were there any noticeable features on the object? Please mention
absolutely anything which comes to mind, no matter how trivial it
may seem. How large were any visible features in relation to the
object?

Really, none whatsoever that I could see. However, the best view
I had of the craft was of its underside as it flew over my car.
There were no protrusions or attachments. More tellingly,
perhaps, neither were there any panels, rivets, joins or welds.
The whole thing seemed to be made of one single sheet of
material.


How fast would you describe it as moving?

I would expect that it moved at between 15 and 40 mph, although
it seemed to me that its speed was constant. It did not stop at
all, and neither did I perceive it to accelerate. I could see the
craft (after my initial encounter) as I drove towards Boston on
the A16. It did not pull away from me and occasionally I had to
slow down to keep it in sight.


Did it move in a straight line?

When it wasn't turning, it did fly in a perfectly straight line.
However, it did navigate a seemingly premeditated route. When I
first saw it on the A1104, it was moving towards Alford. As it
"left the road" it turned towards Louth and then turned back
towards the coast at Skegness directly over my car. It then
turned South towards Boston. Throughout all these turns, its
height remained constant. I cannot recall the craft "banking" in
any of these turns.


Were there any other noises, e.g., traffic, which might have
masked any noticeable sound?

No traffic other than my car and one other. As I have said, the
area is rural and is very quiet at night.


Did you notice any change in the atmosphere when the object was
present?

No. The air was clear, cold and absolutely still. (The stillness
may be seen as unusual because the area is renowned for being
windy.)


Were there any markings of any kind, even the smallest detail
like a different coloured section, which you can recall?

No markings at all. Just an even light blue underbody. No
roundels or numbers or logos!


Did you report your sighting?

When I got home, I was very excited and told the whole story to
my fiance (now my wife.) I also excitedly related the tale to my
work colleague the next day. However, I did not report the
sighting to any official authority. Firstly, because I had no
idea which authority to report to and secondly because I didn't
want to be seen as a crank!


Were there any other witnesses?
As I said above, another car had come towards me on the A1104 and
had stopped on the road. I remember pointing up towards the craft
to draw his attention to it (as if the other driver could miss
it!). After the craft had passed, he drove on. I didn't speak to
him; I've no idea what kind of car he was driving. I've related
this story in conversation locally, many times over the years. I
have yet to find anyone who saw the craft or who has had a
similar experience.


Were there any reports in the local press?

I read most local papers from cover to cover. I found nothing to
match my sighting. There were reports of cigar shaped objects
seen above the sea off Grimsby, but no reports of my delta.
[End]


James.

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 1999 18:34:38 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Re: Silent, hovering, 'triangular'-shaped objects

UFO Research List

A more recent, 1997, account that I haven't published before and
which, again at face value, seemingly lends credence to the
possibility of a delta-shaped aircraft being observed in this
case.

[Start]
I had an interesting experience a some months ago which I would
like to run past you:

I was driving home one evening, not too late, along the main road
that joins Oxford to Reading. About halfway home I noticed the
proverbial "lights in the sky" over one of the fields off to the
side of the road. This was odd as there are no airfields nearby.
A couple of other motorists had stopped in a nearby layby, and
were stood watching over the fence so I decided to join them. We
all watched these "lights" for about 5 minutes, dancing around in
the sky above the field, and then the source of this display came
a little closer to the road and slowly flew over us to the field
opposite, and then carried on maneuvering. After another 3 or 4
minutes or so, it turned south and set off at modest speed,
climbing at the same time, until it was out of sight. The whole
experience was far from frightening. In fact it was quite
mesmerising watching this craft dance around a few tens of feet
off the ground. Nobody suffered any burns, distress, nausea or
any weird shit, and we all just shrugged it off as "another
military toy" and went our own ways after that.

Unfortunately, it didn't occur to me at the time to take anyone's
names or numbers. There must have been 8 or 9 people accumulated
by the end of the "display."

The Object.

I can best describe it's shape as similar to the A12 flying wing
but with an extension to the rear edge, and somewhat smaller.
(see text-o-gram below) It seemed unpainted except for two black
patches, one on each of the rear two corners, and some markings
under what I assumed to be the engines. These were slung
underneath in a "pod" similar to the engines on the XB70
Valkyrie, the same sort of shape too. There were no navigation
lights that I could recognise, instead just 3 bright yellowish
white lights, one at each extreme of the craft. These were steady
lights, not blinking, pulsating or flashing or anything dramatic
like that. We never got a chance to see the top of it, obviously
because it was above us. There was very little noise from it, but
what there was was like that of a diesel generator that you might
find in a large train, but much quieter. As it passed over us, I
could feel the displacement of the air, and there was a slight
warmth to the exhaust (if that's what it was) but nothing like
what you'd expect from a jet exhaust for example. When I could
see the back of it, there was a dark orange glow from the rear
end of the engine "pod".

BTW: This is an honest account

sincerity.

Subject: Pilot Reports

UFO Research List

* This is NOT list only *

Dear list members,

I recently made enquiries on an Oregon 'birding' mailing list re
Kenneth Arnold's later sighting of those 20-something 'brass
coloured objects' which flew like ducks, although seemingly to
fast for birds.

Detailing Arnold's report, without mentioning his name or the
'flying saucers' aspect at all, I asked for any opinions on what
comparative birds the un-named pilot might have observed and been
describing.

I noted that the pilot mentioned (from Arnold's book 'The Coming
of the Saucers): "I began to let down over North Powder, Oregon in
preparation to land at La Grande when I noticed above me and about
ten miles to the right the Empire Airline's old Boeing, also
coming in to land at La Grande".

Contacting a 'birding' forum to try and place a 'UFO' sighting in
perspective, it was truly ironic to see the following posted in
reply:

"Hi - I grew up with Boeing, & still have bushels of unsorted
documents from the many times my father cleaned his desk @ the
Renton plant before Boeing sent him off to some Classified
location.
If there was a Boeing plane in the air within 50 miles of your
specified location, there is also a record of anything else that
was, or was presumed to be in that airspace. Boeing has a
historical / archives section, which you can probably find via a
Web search.

Boeing tried to document / photograph & assess every single item
that might affect the performance of their stuff - geese, clouds,
dust, everything. ( which is why I have thousands of photos of
bolts, rocks, twisted metal & so on) One of the reports that my
father filed - before missile technology really got going - was
about a cylindrical, shiney object that cruised alongside the
Boeing for a while, then veered off.

MOST of these reports were ID'd as birds, but that one wasn't, &
the report vanished from official Boeing records with remarkable
speed".


I can follow this up with the person who replied and maybe obtain
further details, plus put an approximate date of the reported
incident.

It led me to wondering if there is a publicly accessible archive
for Boeing and other airlines, where pilots reports of 'incidents'
might be available.

These would be an invaluable database - the explained 'UFOs' might
be consistent with other cases which are still regarded as
unexplained and perhaps the archives may even hold some unsolved
cases which have never come to light.

What about archives for UK and other European airlines - are they
all 'confidential'?

I thought this was worthy of passing on anyway and it would be
interesting to know what became of that report which 'disappeared'
- presumably it went straight to a military channel?


James.

our own. It has three planets orbiting a star that is 44 light
years away.

The discovery of a group of planets orbiting a sun like our own
will cause great excitement and raises the chances that there may
be other forms of life in the Universe.

'It is one of the most important astronomical discoveries for
decades,' Professor Geoff Marcy, one of the discoverers of the
system, told BBC News Online".

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 1999 23:05:27 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Pilot Reports

UFO Research List

UFO Research List

* This is NOT list only *

Dear list members,

To recap for some new subscribers, on 14 April, I wrote:

I recently made enquiries on an Oregon 'birding' mailing list re
Kenneth Arnold's later sighting of those 20-something 'brass
coloured objects' which flew like ducks, although seemingly to
fast for birds.

Detailing Arnold's report, without mentioning his name or the
'flying saucers' aspect at all, I asked for any opinions on what
comparative birds the un-named pilot might have observed and been
describing.

I noted that the pilot mentioned (from Arnold's book 'The Coming
of the Saucers): "I began to let down over North Powder, Oregon in
preparation to land at La Grande when I noticed above me and about
ten miles to the right the Empire Airline's old Boeing, also
coming in to land at La Grande".

Contacting a 'birding' forum to try and place a 'UFO' sighting in
perspective, it was truly ironic to see the following posted in
reply:

"Hi - I grew up with Boeing, & still have bushels of unsorted
documents from the many times my father cleaned his desk @ the
Renton plant before Boeing sent him off to some Classified
location.
If there was a Boeing plane in the air within 50 miles of your
specified location, there is also a record of anything else that
was, or was presumed to be in that airspace. Boeing has a
historical / archives section, which you can probably find via a
Web search.

Boeing tried to document / photograph & assess every single item
that might affect the performance of their stuff - geese, clouds,
dust, everything. ( which is why I have thousands of photos of
bolts, rocks, twisted metal & so on) One of the reports that my
father filed - before missile technology really got going - was
about a cylindrical, shiney object that cruised alongside the
Boeing for a while, then veered off.

MOST of these reports were ID'd as birds, but that one wasn't, &
the report vanished from official Boeing records with remarkable
speed".


I can follow this up with the person who replied and maybe obtain
further details, plus put an approximate date of the reported
incident.

[.]

[End]


This is turning out to be interesting.

The person who replied as above is Camille, from Dallas, Texas and she
has given permission to post her responses to my further enquiries.

Asked if this incident was ever publicised to her knowledge, she states,
"It was not publicised, quite the opposite".

On the question of whether some documentary evidence may exist in her
father's papers, that seems a possibility, Camille confirming, "I'm sure
that much of this information is here somewhere. I'll see what I can
find; however, his papers are not organised in any comprehensible way so
it won't be soon".

Although she didn't provide any date or location, perhaps not being
sure, I've raised this again. Camille did clarify that the aircraft was
"probably not a jet" and that the airline involved could have been 'Pan
Am'.

Asked if she could "recall any specific details, e.g., how the object
was described (you mention 'shiney'), it's size, apparent speed, etc.",
this has produced details which are intriguing, Camille writing that the
object was, "cigar shaped, bronze or gold as opposed to silvery,
shorter than the Boeing, matched speed to the Boeing".

Whilst it's extremely doubtful we could be so lucky, she added, "For all
I know there's a photo of this thing in the boxes of unsorted documents
& photos".


Most surprising, if accurate, is her recollection of how long the
incident lasted. We might have assumed the pilot's sighting was brief,
probably a few seconds or so, however, Camille believes the duration was
"more than 10 min, less than an hour".
If true and we can discount the pilot being completely mistaken, etc.,
that appears to rule out a missile and indeed most obvious explanations
other than a bird. As a bird had been discounted, it would leave us with
a considerable mystery.

Re the likelihood of a missile, Camille notes, "Nothing was officially
being tested, & I believe he could have found out, he worked on Gypsy
Moth, Minuteman etc".


All we can do is leave this with Camille and hope that somewhere within
those "thousands of photos" and presumably even more documents, is
evidence of this alleged 'close encounter'.

How would Camille's father know that "the report vanished from official
Boeing records with remarkable speed"? I've asked if she can say what
his exact role was and how he knew about this subsequent
'disappearance'.

No obvious reason to doubt Camille's sincerity. In the first place, I
had merely raised an ornithological query, mentioning that the un-named
pilot had noted a Boeing airplane nearby. This potentially significant
'UFO' account was a fortuitous digression she brought up.

Kenneth Arnold would, I'm sure, also appreciate the absolute irony!


James.

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 1999 21:08:21 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Re: 'Out of this world discovery'

UFO Research List

[List mail which was forwarded to myself]:
From: Ed Stewart <ufoindex@jps.net>
Subject: Re: 'Out of this world discovery'

Before anybody gets too excited:

What is _not_ being said is that at least one of these three planets
(jovian size) has an _elliptical_ orbit. Unfortunately, a jovian size
planet with an elliptical orbit would ultimately sweep all mass in its
area into itself. If the orbit area of the planet encroached into the
life bearing area parameters, it would destroy any chance for an earth
like planet to form in that life bearing area. What makes our solar
system unique so far is that the Sun's planets have circular orbits and
not elliptical orbits.

If Jupiter had an elliptical orbit around the Sun, we wouldn't have the
solar system that we enjoy and there probably wouldn't be any earthlike
planets inside of Jupiter's orbit, if elliptical.

Ed Stewart

the serious allusion to perceived UFO mythology.

Stealth technology originated!

Subject: The road to Domestos

UFO Research List

[List posting forwarded]

From: Chris Gibson <cgibson@skomer.u-net.com>
Subject: The road to Domestos
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 1999 23:16:29 +0000

I suspect I was invited onto this list due to my work in the
aviation field, I would have been quite happy to sit on the
sidelines and watch the proceedings. Unfortunately I've been in
the boonies for 6 weeks, so have the benefit of assessing the
input retrospectively. May I insert a control rod...

Initial impression is that Tim Matthews is punting his work as
the first analysis of UFOs as a technological feat, by mere
humans and this "revelation" is being purposely ignored by the
UFO press. Is this, I wonder, the same Tim Matthews who as a
wheel in the Lancashire UFO society, had numerous articles
published in the UFO mages over a two year period? Now we have a
conspiracy against Tim, with no journals willing to publish his
work. Perhaps (having dealt with Tim for a few years now) it is
his methods that these journals and societies don't like?
Perhaps the same will soon be true of the aviation societies. Are
these the same aviation people dismissed as bitter and cynical in
UFO Revelation? How many times has Tim been up the road to
Domestos?

I've always advocated playing the long game, having been hunting
my own Snark since 1989. Kicking in doors and demanding answers
won't work, neither will being profligate with or dismissive of
the hard work of other researchers.

So, that's that out of the way. To deal with Tim's points:

1) Unscientific - what branch of science is being "un-ed"?
Applied, Pure or Psuedo? I think some idea of what science is
would be required before you start throwing words like
unscientific about. If you want to be really scientific, that
requires inconveniences like peer review and open discussion.

A forum such as UFORL and the Skunkworks list does provide that.
Where the UFOlogists are guilty of being unscientific is in the
latter two areas. Peer review and open discussion have come to
mean nitpicking and off the cuff remarks like "mad man".
Referring to one's fellow researchers (ie the people on whom you
rely for input and ideas) by such dismissive terms is both
unprofessional and lends credence to the view that those involved
in such work are not worth talking to. Us aviation types may be
cynical and bitter, but we have respect for each others' work and
expertise, with none of the one-upmanship of the UFOlogists.

2) Why look at all triangle reports? Ah, there we go being
unscientific. If we do not include all these reports how can we
get any density of data? Without that we cannot hope to monitor
any trends or changes in the behaviour of the triangles. If you
have a lot of sample it is then possible to categorise them:
that's an airship type triangle, that's a hypersonic type
triangle etc etc.

By ignoring the sightings which don't suit us, there is a chance
of missing something important.

I dipped out of the Skunk Works list as it was generating too
much traffic on subsidiary subjects, but occasionally it came up
with items of interest TO ME. What must be remembered is that in
any forum such as UFORL, each member has their own area of
interest and expertise and will see (pardon the pun) a sighting
or remark from a different aspect. The list is not run to provide
information for one person's particular interest.

In short I'm saying if we want our work on this subject to get
anywhere, get a grip and stop the petty point scoring.

So, now that's out the way, I can get on with what I consider
these list groups are about.

Any-one know how to contact the chap involved in the UFO
retrieval at Upper Heyford?

Chris


[Note]
Chris was indeed invited to subscribe as I consider Chris's
research into those darned 'flying triangles' and his general

By way of a brief introduction for those who are not familiar

On the topic of triangular-shaped aircraft being observed in the

I don't believe that's beyond us.


James.

__________

I welcome any questions on my North Sea sighting, as I am of the
opinion that too much is taken at face value in the black aircraft
snark hunt. I think that the snark hunt has degenerated into an
exercise in regurgitating the same old stories with little or no new
research being done.

A bit about me. I work as a drilling technologist for a major oil
field service company. I hold an Honours degree in Geology, with some
engineering, geophysics and chemistry thrown in. I also did a post
graduate course in systems analysis. I was a member of the Royal
Observer Corps for 13 years and was a member of the ROC's aircraft
recognition team for 12 of those years. In this field I was considered
to be an expert and produced an aircraft recognition manual for the
ROC.

You obviously know the sighting story, but I'll fill you in on what
happened from my point of view. I was working in the Indefatigable
field on the jack-up rig "Galveston Key" in August 1989. My colleague,
Graeme Winton, went out on deck but returned immediately. He told me
to "Have a look at this". We went outside and Graeme pointed skywards.

I had been at university with Graeme and he knew of my interest in
aircraft. As far as Graeme was concerned it was a formation of
aircraft and he reckoned I'd be interested. I looked up, saw the
tanker and the F-111s, but was amazed to see the triangle.

I am trained in instant recognition, but this triangle had me stopped
dead. My first thought was that it was another F-111, but there was
no "gaps", it was too long and it didn't look like one (might sound
strange but after a while doing aircraft recognition you get a feel
for the shape of aircraft, what was called the "sit" in the past or
what bird watchers refer to as "jizz".) My next thought was that it
was an F-117, as the highly swept planform of the F-117 had just been
made public. Again the triangle was too long and had no gaps.

After considering and rejecting a Mirage IV, I was totally out of
ideas. Here was an aircraft, flying overhead, not too high and not
particularly fast. A recognition gift and I was clueless. This was a
new experience.
He asked me what was going on. I watched as the formation flew
overhead and told him that the big one was a KC-135 Stratotanker, the
two on the left were F-111 and that I didn't know what the fourth
aircraft was. Graeme said "I thought you were an expert?". I said "I
am". To which Graeme replied "Some expert". It was obvious to me that
this aircraft was something dodgy.

I watched the formation for a minute or two and went back inside with
Graeme. At the time I was writing the aircraft recognition manual and
had a Danish Luftmelderkorpset "Flykendingsbog" in my briefcase. This
is probably the best aircraft recognition book ever produced. I looked
through it, but nothing matched. I then sketched what I had seen.

I sent this sketch to Peter Edwards, who was a Group Officer in the
ROC and was also on the recognition team. We discussed what to do
about it but decided that if it was reported through official
channels, it would be at best rubbished, at worst lead to trouble.
Having signed the Official Secrets Act I didn't want to jeopardise my
position in the recognition team. So I kept my mouth shut. I told
other members of the recognition team in the hope that they could shed
some light on the subject.

On returning home I had a look through my book collection. The only
aircraft which came close to matching what I had seen was a Handley
Page HP115. It was not one of them.

Whether this aircraft was Aurora is debatable, my background precludes
jumping to conclusions based on single piece of evidence. I wrote to
Bill Sweetman after being sent an illustration from Janes Defence
weekly which matched what I had seen. as an aside, I wrote to two
other writers who did not reply. Bill reckons it was Aurora, AgentX
reckons it was the FB-119. I don't know what it was. It is the only
aircraft I have ever seen that I could not identify. Pete Edwards told
Bill Sweetman that if I didn't know what this aircraft was, it isn't
in any book.

I've been hunting this snark for almost 9 years now and have turned
up some interesting stuff, mainly through my own efforts, but also by
having looked in the most unusual places. Surfing websites might be
cool, but talking to the people involved is a necessity.

As I said before, I welcome the healthy scepticism, but at least give
me the opportunity to state my case.


Yours

Chris Gibson
[End]

Hi Tim,

Yes, Crackpot UFOlogy is useless and gripped with religious fanaticism.
However, there is a small coterie of dedicated UFO researchers who are
engaged in serious scientific investigation. You want scientific
reproducible results then please see me RB-47 case article in The UFO
Encyclopedia, 2nd Edition, ed. by Jerome Clark (Omnigraphics, Detroit, 1998)
for the world's first calibrated scientific proof for the existence of an
unexplained UFO phenomenon, based on the real-time accurate calibration of an
airborne UFO's radar-like microwave signal against a known air-defense ground
radar at Duncanville/Dallas, Texas. The 28-year investigation I began (see
Astronautics & Aeronautics, Dec 1971) has completely refuted Klass' seeming
persuasive explanations for the case except for a brief meteor sighting which
was confirmed and a radiant plotted in the Sagittarius constellation. The
RB-47 case is ongoing, there are extremely classified military records still
to be obtained, including the air-ground transcript, etc.

Also please keep abreast of the Trent/McMinnville stereo photographic case,
which will soon have publicly announced breakthroughs. There are daily
developments in the case and I'm actively leading the investigations, having
worked on it for 27 years since a challenge from Philip Klass.

Best regards,

Brad Sparks

> A bit about me. I work as a drilling technologist for a major oil
> field service company. I hold an Honours degree in Geology, with some
> engineering, geophysics and chemistry thrown in. I also did a post
> graduate course in systems analysis. I was a member of the Royal
> Observer Corps for 13 years and was a member of the ROC's aircraft
> recognition team for 12 of those years. In this field I was considered
> to be an expert and produced an aircraft recognition manual for the
> ROC.
>
> You obviously know the sighting story, but I'll fill you in on what
> happened from my point of view. I was working in the Indefatigable
> field on the jack-up rig "Galveston Key" in August 1989. My colleague,
> Graeme Winton, went out on deck but returned immediately. He told me
> to "Have a look at this". We went outside and Graeme pointed skywards.
>
> I had been at university with Graeme and he knew of my interest in
> aircraft. As far as Graeme was concerned it was a formation of
> aircraft and he reckoned I'd be interested. I looked up, saw the
> tanker and the F-111s, but was amazed to see the triangle.
>
> I am trained in instant recognition, but this triangle had me stopped
> dead. My first thought was that it was another F-111, but there was
> no "gaps", it was too long and it didn't look like one (might sound
> strange but after a while doing aircraft recognition you get a feel
> for the shape of aircraft, what was called the "sit" in the past or
> what bird watchers refer to as "jizz".) My next thought was that it
> was an F-117, as the highly swept planform of the F-117 had just been
> made public. Again the triangle was too long and had no gaps.
>
> After considering and rejecting a Mirage IV, I was totally out of
> ideas. Here was an aircraft, flying overhead, not too high and not
> particularly fast. A recognition gift and I was clueless. This was a
> new experience.
>
> He asked me what was going on. I watched as the formation flew
> overhead and told him that the big one was a KC-135 Stratotanker, the
> two on the left were F-111 and that I didn't know what the fourth
> aircraft was. Graeme said "I thought you were an expert?". I said "I
> am". To which Graeme replied "Some expert". It was obvious to me that
> this aircraft was something dodgy.
>
> I watched the formation for a minute or two and went back inside with
> Graeme. At the time I was writing the aircraft recognition manual and
> had a Danish Luftmelderkorpset "Flykendingsbog" in my briefcase. This
> is probably the best aircraft recognition book ever produced. I looked
> through it, but nothing matched. I then sketched what I had seen.
>
> I sent this sketch to Peter Edwards, who was a Group Officer in the
> ROC and was also on the recognition team. We discussed what to do
> about it but decided that if it was reported through official
> channels, it would be at best rubbished, at worst lead to trouble.
> Having signed the Official Secrets Act I didn't want to jeopardise my
> position in the recognition team. So I kept my mouth shut. I told
> other members of the recognition team in the hope that they could shed
> some light on the subject.
>
> On returning home I had a look through my book collection. The only
> aircraft which came close to matching what I had seen was a Handley
> Page HP115. It was not one of them.
>
> Whether this aircraft was Aurora is debatable, my background precludes
> jumping to conclusions based on single piece of evidence. I wrote to
> Bill Sweetman after being sent an illustration from Janes Defence
> weekly which matched what I had seen. as an aside, I wrote to two
> other writers who did not reply. Bill reckons it was Aurora, AgentX

From: Chris Gibson <cgibson@dmu.ac.uk>
Subject: Re: The road to Domestos

UFO Research List

On the contrary, while I may disagree with the aims of some of the other
researchers in the field, it is necessary to be aware of the state of the
game in the other fields. Belittling their work cannot be a wise
investment, that work may turn out to be the key. A blinkered attitude
will not produce any results. If kicking in doors is the preferred method,
so be it. Sow the wind.

Slipping in off the cuff remarks like "I know where these things are built
/ operated from" smacks of true UFOlogy. Perhaps a better idea would be to
firm up the theories, allow others to discretely (that means without
telling all and sundry) review the work and then publish.

I've never doubted the deltas and the saucers exist, I know too many
people who have seen them. Proving they exist is not the point. Their
development, funding, and operation would be much more interesting. That's
whatwe want to be looking at and some credible evidence is waht is
required. Somewhere in the blizzard of sightings and paperwork, which some
of us would like to ignore lies that evidence. Find it.

Chris

> > graduate course in systems analysis. I was a member of the Royal
> > Observer Corps for 13 years and was a member of the ROC's aircraft
> > recognition team for 12 of those years. In this field I was considered
> > to be an expert and produced an aircraft recognition manual for the
> > ROC.
>>
> > You obviously know the sighting story, but I'll fill you in on what
> > happened from my point of view. I was working in the Indefatigable
> > field on the jack-up rig "Galveston Key" in August 1989. My colleague,
> > Graeme Winton, went out on deck but returned immediately. He told me
> > to "Have a look at this". We went outside and Graeme pointed skywards.
>>
> > I had been at university with Graeme and he knew of my interest in
> > aircraft. As far as Graeme was concerned it was a formation of
> > aircraft and he reckoned I'd be interested. I looked up, saw the
> > tanker and the F-111s, but was amazed to see the triangle.
>>
> > I am trained in instant recognition, but this triangle had me stopped
> > dead. My first thought was that it was another F-111, but there was
> > no "gaps", it was too long and it didn't look like one (might sound
> > strange but after a while doing aircraft recognition you get a feel
> > for the shape of aircraft, what was called the "sit" in the past or
> > what bird watchers refer to as "jizz".) My next thought was that it
> > was an F-117, as the highly swept planform of the F-117 had just been
> > made public. Again the triangle was too long and had no gaps.
>>
> > After considering and rejecting a Mirage IV, I was totally out of
> > ideas. Here was an aircraft, flying overhead, not too high and not
> > particularly fast. A recognition gift and I was clueless. This was a
> > new experience.
>>
> > He asked me what was going on. I watched as the formation flew
> > overhead and told him that the big one was a KC-135 Stratotanker, the
> > two on the left were F-111 and that I didn't know what the fourth
> > aircraft was. Graeme said "I thought you were an expert?". I said "I
> > am". To which Graeme replied "Some expert". It was obvious to me that
> > this aircraft was something dodgy.
>>
> > I watched the formation for a minute or two and went back inside with
> > Graeme. At the time I was writing the aircraft recognition manual and
> > had a Danish Luftmelderkorpset "Flykendingsbog" in my briefcase. This
> > is probably the best aircraft recognition book ever produced. I looked
> > through it, but nothing matched. I then sketched what I had seen.
>>
> > I sent this sketch to Peter Edwards, who was a Group Officer in the
> > ROC and was also on the recognition team. We discussed what to do
> > about it but decided that if it was reported through official
> > channels, it would be at best rubbished, at worst lead to trouble.
> > Having signed the Official Secrets Act I didn't want to jeopardise my
> > position in the recognition team. So I kept my mouth shut. I told
> > other members of the recognition team in the hope that they could shed
> > some light on the subject.
>>
> > On returning home I had a look through my book collection. The only
> > aircraft which came close to matching what I had seen was a Handley
> > Page HP115. It was not one of them.
>>
> > Whether this aircraft was Aurora is debatable, my background precludes
> > jumping to conclusions based on single piece of evidence. I wrote to
> > Bill Sweetman after being sent an illustration from Janes Defence
> > weekly which matched what I had seen. as an aside, I wrote to two
> > other writers who did not reply. Bill reckons it was Aurora, AgentX
> > reckons it was the FB-119. I don't know what it was. It is the only
> > aircraft I have ever seen that I could not identify. Pete Edwards told
> > Bill Sweetman that if I didn't know what this aircraft was, it isn't
> > in any book.
>>
> > I've been hunting this snark for almost 9 years now and have turned
> > up some interesting stuff, mainly through my own efforts, but also by
> > having looked in the most unusual places. Surfing websites might be
> > cool, but talking to the people involved is a necessity.
>>
> > As I said before, I welcome the healthy scepticism, but at least give
> > me the opportunity to state my case.
>>
>>
> > Yours
>>
> > Chris Gibson
> > [End]
>>

From: HerbUFO@aol.com
Subject: Various itemsMessage-id: <e7495612.2454c6f7@aol.com>

UFO Research List

Greetings to the list:

Though this is my first posting to the UFO RESEARCH LIST, I hope that many
more will follow. Please note that I'm a member of the PROJECT-1947 list, so
this venue is not new to me. To date I've noticed that though postings to
this list have not been that plentiful, they often are rather provocative.
My interest in the UFO phenomenon goes back nearly fifty years, and where I
once was a strong proponent of the ET theory, I now regard myself as a
rational skeptic. I look with despair at a field littered with nonsense and
crap, those jerks who conjur it up, and perhaps most sadly, those damn fools
who believe it. For instance, I once viewed the Roswell Incident as most
likely being a genuine recovery of an alien spacecraft. Thanks to being
enlightened by the findings of Karl Pflock, Bob Todd, Kent Jeffrey, and dare
I say it, the U.S. Air Force, I now realize that the debris field found on
the Foster Ranch by foreman Bill "Mac" Brazel was caused by a Project Mogul
balloon array. All else re this event is pure myth. No impact site(s), no
craft, no bodies. Yet due to a dearth of critical thinking in this field,
this damn myth rolls on. The presence of certain fake documents only adds to
the problem. This non-event illustrates the idiocy that wracks this field.

What I regard as perhaps one of the most fascinatings aspects of the UFO
phenomenon is that category of reports known as
satellite-objects/cloud-cigars. I'm in the process of making a study of this
category of reports, and needed badly is data from other serious researchers.
 Therefore, I request that anyone on this list who have little known sighting
reports that fall into this category, please be kind enough to send them on
to me. My thanks in advance.

BTW, I've been following with considerable interest the discussion on this
list concerning the possibility that much of the UFO problem can be laid to
classified government aircraft of advanced design. While I don't dismiss
this possibility out of hand, needed badly is documentation of the claims
supporting this theory, if in fact such exist. Incidentally, how would this
theory account for the most impressive satellite-object/cloud-cigar reports?
It would seem that this is is one of the areas of the UFO problem that the
classified aircraft theory would have considerable difficulty in dealing with.

Regards, Herb Taylor
