Yes,

and as I regularly point out much of the information is still classified
although we have a good job of bringing the many issues to the forefront.
There is good evidence and we have been putting out regular information for
some time.

THE BIG MISTAKE that opponents make is suggesting that we are trying to
explain all sightings and in fact the biggest dishonesty is when
"researchers" push this line that "AH, well, you're research cannot explain
this sighting, or that sightings blah blah".

Given that neither I nor anybody else interested in this perspective has
ever claimed that cigar-shapes (clouds, aircraft, god knows) can be
explained by invoking secret military aircraft I suggest that there is no
debate in the first place!!

When you ask for further documentation - assuming that you are aware of the
increasingly impressive array of documents hinting (at least) that we are
in some ways right in our view that flying discs and flying triangles are
of military origin (quite obvious given that many FT sightings are
accompanied by military escort!!) - then we say "Join the club!" because
neither the USAF, NRO, CIA or US Navy are interested in telling us the
truth.

We know they have the documents and in certain cases they have told us as
much - and then gone on to claim "National Security" in defence of their
non-release of vital information on this (50 year old) subject.......

Think about it; what would happen if one/some of the agencies admitted that
there was more in the air than the Avrocar flop? Pandora's Box.......

Tim-

Come, let us reason together.

In your response to my questions:

- who was the contractor?
- where were they built?
- why didn't the Air Force know about them?
- how were they powered? If it was by 1947-vintage jet engines, please
detail their technology.

you said...

"Chance-Vought built some of them...one of the aircraft used Allison
J33's....I have spoken to a
very good witness in terms of this part of the investigation, Thomas C
Smith who worked for Chance-Vought and upon jet-powered pancakes."

Since Chance-Vought was still based in Connecticut in 1947, I assume that
this implies that the saucers of the 1947 wave were built at the Vought
plant in Bridgeport, where the V-173 and XF5U-1 were built and tested.
You mention the Allison J33 engine as a powerplant. And you suggest that the
US Navy was the service branch responsible for funding and operating these
saucers.
It is true that several sources, including the "Aeroplane" article you
mentioned, refer to the idea that the XF5U-1 was intended to be modified to
use a single gas-turbine engine instead of the two Pratt & Whitney R-2000
radial piston engines it originally used, but _even with this engine it
still would have used propellers for propulsion_. The idea that a
1947-vintage propeller-powered aircraft could have reached sustained speeds
of over 500 mph is interesting, and would be news to conventional aero
historians. It's still only one-third of the speeds reported for some of the
1947 UFOs, but we'll let that pass.
Let's take a walk through the "World Encyclopedia of Aero Engines," by top
aero historian Bill Gunston (presumably he can be relied on...). I assume
you know that Vought was a unit of United Aircraft, along with Pratt &
Whitney, the aero engine manufacturer. It seems very reasonable to believe
that P&W, a favorite Navy contractor, would have built the turboshaft engine
the XF5U-1 would have needed, since their engines powered most other Vought
planes. Gunston says that P&W began work on its first shaft-turbine, the
Navy-funded T34, in 1945. Its design was complete by March 1946, it had a
rating of 6,000-7,500 ehp (so far so good), but it took years to develop and
didn't go into service until _1958_. In January 1947 they began working on
another shaft turbine, the Air Force-funded XT45, but it was cancelled in
1948. How about other engine contractors? Allison? Their 2,200 hp T38 (no
improvement over the engines the Flapjack already had) didn't fly until
April 1949. The modified later T40 that was used in the Navy's VTO "Pogo"
and "Salmon" x-planes didn't fly until around 1953. How about GE? Here's a
possibility - the big T31 flew in late 1945, but again only put out about
1,650 hp, no improvement on the F5U's engines. Wright? Their giant XT35 for
the Air Force flew in September 1947 and only 17 were built. Only three
Northrop XT37s existed in 1947 and they were AF-sponsored and far too big to
fit in the Flapjack. Westinghouse, another Navy favorite? No turboprop. In
sum, there were apparently no suitable turboprop/shaft engines available by
summer 1947.

You mentioned the Allison J33 turbojet. Let's think about this. We'll
disregard the fact that the Navy used Westinghouse engines in its first
Vought jet fighter, the F6U Pirate (first flight Oct '46) - the lackluster
J34 (4,100 lb st with afterburner, 3,100 lb military power, 2,600 lb lb
cruise). The J33 was a primitive first-generation centrifugal-flow jet based
on the original Whittle engine. It had a _maximum_ thrust of 4,600 lb, or
5,400 lb for a limited period with water injection. Cruise thrust around
3,000 lb. So obviously, one of these engines could lift something weighing a
little over 4,000 lb, if running at full power, allowing some margin for
acceleration, etc. The XF5U-1 weighed about 13,000 lb empty and
16,000-18,000 lb loaded. So clearly it would have required at least four,
and more likely five, J33s in order to hover, take off vertically, etc.
After modification to house all these engines, there would have been nothing
left of the original XF5U-1 design. And consider fuel consumption. In an
aircraft supported purely by jet thrust, these multiple engines would be
consuming fuel at a tremendous rate. And producing tremendous amounts of
smoke and noise. Fuel is heavy, and four to five engines would need a lot of
it.
The J33 was inadequate for VTOL flight. As you know, two similar Nene
engines were barely capable of lifting their own weight when used in the RR
Flying Bedstead, which first "flew" in 1953. Its performance was hardly
blistering.

For comparison, look at the Hawker-Siddeley P. 1127, the first prototype of
the Harrier VTOL jet, which first hovered in fall 1960, over a decade after
Vought supposedly solved the problem of supersonic VTOL flight. The airframe
weighed only 10,000 lb, the engine barely produced that much thrust, and a
hover could only be achieved when the fuel on board was reduced to 65
gallons, enough for a few _seconds_ of hover!

And in 1947 they could do at least two orders of magnitude better...?

You will no doubt be impatient with niggling little details like the
complete lack of suitable engines for 1947 terrestrial saucers, but really I
think it's the key to the whole thing. The US aircraft industry was in a
crisis in 1947 due to sweeping funding cuts. If a stupendous breakthrough
had been made by an airframe contractor and an engine builder, you would
expect to see them reap big rewards in terms of later contracts. If they had
solved these problems as early as 1947, you would expect to see this
technology show up in unclassified work a decade or so later. Where does
this happen? Who built the engines? Find that out and you have the solution.

One last observation. You said

Christ, even Keyhoe in 'Flying Saucers Have Landed" notes conversations
where he was told about secret military a/c projects!"

I would suggest that it's extremely inadvisable to cite "The Flying Saucers
are Real" to bolster the claim that UFOs are US secret aircraft. The whole
_point_ of Keyhoe's book is a thorough, logical demolition of that notion.
But of course, ufologists are all dupes of the Navy conspiracy, aren't they?

- J Carpenter

Why the great debate about the Vought Saucers? The XF5U be it -1 or -2
might've flown but it didn't get anywhere. After all it would have
deprived the Admirals of big ole carriers to swan about in. Some designer
comes along and says "This'll make big carriers obsolete" Admiral Bigboat
says "Well, we ain't having that" End of XF5U. I believe I put this theory
as applied to the AF bombers in an email to Tim about a year ago. Didn't
use that theory in the book? The air force generals would probably prefer
300 nice big B-52s than a handful of shiney discs. What do the others on
the list think of this theory? Ha! Peer review.

I note that Tim isn't pushing his assertion from his book (I've read it)
that the saucers were German / Canadian? Why is this? been up the road to
Domestos on that one as well? Maybe I misread that chapter.

I've always thought that the reason the aviation historians like Gunston
didn't discuss discs / saucers was that they appreciated the difficulty
involved in getting the run of the mill aircraft to work efficiently,
never mind anything exotic.

When you look at the difficulties involved in hypersonics (my area of
interest) I can't see the saucers being any easier, especially in the area
of propulsion. Engine designers habitually over estimated the performace
of the early jets.

We end up with loads of cigarette packet designs that came to nought. ie
an aeronautical blind alley. Conventional designs were easier to produce
and operate. All the proposed designs for saucers I have seen (not many I
might add) look highly complex pieces of kit to maintain, with multiple
engines and all those flapper valves to operate: a hydraulics engineer's
nightmare. Lots of heavy, complex mechanisms which would hardly be immune
to a 30mm incendiary injection from a Farmer. I suspect you'll be saying
they were fly-by-wire and armour plated with Unobtainium.

All the documentation I have seen shows lovely drawings of saucers.
Where's the hardware? (Don't even think about mentioning Avrocar, I saw
it in the Smithsonian and I'd say some-one has lost a skeet target)
Where's the photos? They wouldn't run these programmes without documenting
them photographically. Of course, the photos are classified, silly me.

I've seen the same type of drawings for hypersonic designs, none of which
came to fruition.

The saucers were extant, but I'd say they were only extant for a limited
period. Any benefit they provided was overtaken by conventional, i.e.
cheap (?!!?), aircraft which could be built and operated in greater
numbers, with ease.

From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>

UFO Research List

As we know, there are two quite distinctive categories of FT
reports.

The first is indicative of a relatively straight-forward top
secret military aircraft; it flies at high altitude and
reports have observed it to be accompanied by other recognised
military planes.

So, what is it, when was it developed and what role does it
serve.

Taking the middle question first, it seems there may have been
triangular-shaped aircraft flying in the early 1970s.

Although anecdotal evidence, there are a number of ostensibly
credible reports. For example, Jay Ward's account:

"In the summer of 1975, I saw a pair of triangular objects
while stargazing with binoculars. At the time, I assumed that
they must have been aircraft. But it's been a long time since
then, and I haven't ever seen any airplanes, or whatever, that
even remotely resemble the objects I saw.

...I was laying on the ground, looking through a pair of 20
power binoculars. My feet were pointed east, and the
binoculars were pointed slightly to the right of straight up,
at about the one o'clock position. Something went through my
field of vision, moving right to left. I caught up to it
quickly, and saw two objects flying in close formation, one in
front, and the other behind, and to the right. They were both
the same size, shaped like equilateral triangles with straight
edges, flying point forward. Their color appeared to be flat
slate gray, against a deep black sky. There were no features,
and I saw no lights, or glow of any kind. They appeared to be
illuminated by the city lights. It looked something like this:

            left (north)
                  -                 .if this diagram doesn't
             -         -            .line up, select a fixed
           -             -          .font (like courier). This
       -                     -      .line should be straight.
   -         .                -     .
  -          /\                -     .
 -          / \                 -    .
 -      / \                  -     .
 - /         \               -     . I've draw this sideways
 - /_________\                      -     . because it was a little
-                .            - top . easier, and the proportions
-                /\           -(west). are more accurate.
-               / \           - .
 -             / \           -     .
 -            /      \       -     .
 -           /_________\            -     .
  -                         -     .
   -                       -      .
     -                   -        .
       -               -          .
         -          -             .
              -                   .
         right (south)

There was something very peculiar about the way they looked as
they flew. The craft in front appeared more steady than the
trailing one, and the distance between them fluctuated
randomly, varying from nearly touching, to a maximum of a
triangle length. When the rear one began to lag, it would
suddenly snap back to a comfortable distance from the front
one. My impression was, that it looked as though they were
being manually controlled by pilots, and as if they had very
high power to weight ratio, and like they were somewhat hard
to control.

I watched them for about 8 to 12 seconds. During that time,
they maintained a due north heading, and covered about 80 to
90 degrees of azimuth. After I lost sight of them, I waited
for several minutes for any sound. I heard nothing.

The binoculars were 20x50, with a field of view of 157 feet at
1000 yards. If you assume that the objects were about 100 feet
long, and took up about one third of the field of view, then
their altitude would be 2000 yards, or 6000 feet, and their
speed would be 568 mph. That seems pretty conventional, but I
think I would have heard jets at that altitude. Furthermore,
what jets have a perfect equilateral silhouette? The closest
thing I can think of, is the B58 Hustler. But my view was
clear enough, that I could have seen the little bit of
fuselage in the front and back of the delta wing.

I probably blew the simple geometry I used for the altitude
and speed calculations, but I've given enough facts that one
could calculate height and speed for any craft of a known
size.

If anyone has any information about similar sightings, I'd
love to hear about it.
[End]


At the time of this report, in 1994, Jay was employed by
Lockheed.

He later corrected the date of the sighting as 1974, not 1975
and in personal correspondence added:

"My sighting was in Campell, CA., which borders San Jose,
about 50 miles south of San Francisco.

[.]

The more I think about the way I calculated the speed and
altitude, the more I think I didn't do it correctly.

The interesting thing here, is that if they were travelling
much faster, then they would be supersonic, and I would
certainly have heard the sonic boom. If they were lower in
altitude, then I should have heard their engines, if they were
jets (I think I should have heard them anyway, but a friend of
mine, who is an F-16 pilot, says not necessarily)".


There's Paul Hamner's 1978 UK account I had further
documented, in which Paul claims to have seen at close range a
large triangular-shaped 'aircraft'.

These are a couple of the more detailed examples. In terms of
the overall evidence, we might have a new claimed sighting.

It comes from Camille, who as I recently mentioned had
responded to my enquiries on an Oregon 'Birders' mailing list
re Kenneth Arnold's report of 25 or so 'brass coloured'
objects which flew like ducks, but weren't ducks because they
flew too fast, etc.

As a complete aside, Camille mentioned the sighting of a
'cigar-shaped' object which her father had documented in his
work for Boeing, a report which had apparently never been
published. More on that later.

In correspondence, adding to the irony of my ornithological
query resulting in an unexpected and intriguing 'UFO' report,
to my surprise, she wrote: "A question: Very fast, black, high
altitude triangle(s) over Utah or Nevada in 1974 or 1975 would
have been a Stealth prototype?"
It was a development which reinforced my belief that 'birders'
are a largely, if not entirely, untapped source of
observational data apropos to 'anomalous' aerial objects.

Few other hobbies or occupations involve scanning the skies
for lengthy periods during daylight and in general always
being attentive to anything 'unusual' appearing.


Camille clarified:

"I'm fairly certain it was in spring of 1975, not '74, late
May, on secondary roads between Beaver & Cedar Breaks Nat
Monument, in the vicinity of Parowan Gap, Utah. We were on the
way to Zion Nat Park, spent the previous night @ Beaver (which
I do not recommend), and I think we headed E. after Parowan
Gap. Parowan Gap is a natural feature near the town of
Parowan. It was between 10 a.m & 4 p.m., mostly clear with
intermittent high altitude clouds, or haze, that developed
into non-productive thunderheads in late afternoon. I don't
recall if it was on the hike to the Gap or another stop, but I
was out of the car without the field glasses, looking for
ravens. The black or dark triangle was travelling in an
apparently straight line S., SE, or SW against 'white' sky.
Difficult to describe size - if I stuck a paper triangle
three-sixteenths of an inch on a side on the upper center of
my left eyeglasses lens it would be about right. It appeared
to be moving very fast. (I currently live under an afternoon
commuter jet route & the triangle was moving faster than they
do @ about 50 miles out). My companion said there were more
than one, but I only saw one. There was never any noise from
it. Definitely not a bird.

In talking about the trip to co-workers who had suggested part
of our route (to look for hotsprings -)a short time later one
of them said she (they?) had seen 'those things' in the same
general area. I don't remember if anyone else concurred.

The object might not have been triangular. A white or very
light colored aircraft of any shape with a triangular dark
area on the underside would have 'disappeared' except for the
dark area because the sky was 'white' - a standard type of
camouflage for many birds & aquatic lifeforms, and something I
didn't know about at the time".


One point which does seem to be resolved, there were no
'stealth' aircraft flying until the late 1970s.

For information, some reports I noted which suggest the
possibility that these 'second category', anomalous flying
triangles, if they do exist, are capable of unusual
manoeuvrability:


"In the early 60's while living in central Texas, I was out in my
folks back yard one evening. The sun had already set and it was a
perfectly clear night. In this area of Texas you have a nearly
horizon to horizon clear view. Now I was only about 10 at the
time but I can remember it as clearly as if it happened
yesterday. Out of the south-east an object moved across the sky
towards my location very fast and dead stopped what I would guess
about 5 miles away at about 2 miles up. It then moves closer to
my location, very fast and dead stopped. This time it was maybe a
mile away so looked to be at about 45deg from the horizon. I
could see that it was clearly a triangular shape. Then I noticed
that there was another craft following the first, mimicking every
move. The first now moved to the east about 3 or 4 miles and
stopped again and the second moved to the location near me. I
noticed then that while they were at rest they seemed to look
more blue and while moving they were more white. The first then
took off at another angle more north east and was out of site.
The second one followed the same path and was gone. I had no
witnesses except my little brother, who was 5 at the time and
today he remembers nothing of it".

"As I remember, what I saw had no fuselage either. They just
looked like fat triangles with rounded edges with no other
features. I think I remember hearing a high pitched crackling
sound that followed their movement, but this may have been added
in my mind later.

I always have felt they were pretty big for airplanes. Maybe 100
to 200 feet across. I know, from having worked around military
aircraft, that they always appear smaller than they really are.

I remember distinctly that the sides were rounded. Like the
things were maybe 20 feet thick and had perfectly rounded sides,
like a 10 foot radius. They were very smooth looking. I don't
remember any thing protruding from the top or anywhere. I always
try to put some sort of cockpit on a saucer in my mind but that's
not what I saw.
Remember, I say these when I was about 10, that was 30 years ago.
I still got all my marbles...but...details do get a little
cloudy. But this I manage to remember quite clearly.

Oh yea, one other thing that should rule out the chance that it
was an early version of the F117...these things DID NOT turn when
they changed direction. They simply stopped, rather abruptly and
then took off in the heading off another point of the triangle.
Now I suppose the things could have rotated their orientation
very quickly, so I couldn't see it, but I never felt they did
that. It's like the things have 3 fronts they could choose from".

Andy Christian.



"The time, i.e. year, is now hard for me to remember but the
events remain as clear as though it was yesterday.

I was living in St. Brides Major, a small village near Bridgend,
South Wales. I was around 16 years old then and keen on
astronomy. This fixes the date somewhere between 1974 and 1976.

[.]

As we both continued to watch, it started to come towards us. As
it got closer two more lights appeared, also red. It became
apparent that whatever it was, was going to pass directly over
our house and quite low at that. We both rushed outside, grabbing
my mother on the way. We stood in the garden and watched this
thing approach our house. As it got closer we could see that the
three lights, all red, were arranged in a triangular
configuration (i.e., at the corners of a would be equilateral
triangle). The lights illuminated the inside of the triangle but
not the outer. They appeared to shine inward, albeit that's how
it seemed. What was illuminated can only be described as
something metallic. It appeared to be a metallic surface that was
dull. It did not shine as there were no light reflections in it.
I say metallic because that what I felt at the time. The material
appeared to be a silvery-grey colour. However, bear in mind that
this was observed under red light. It was one piece, i.e. between
the lights, there appeared to be no joints, rivet lines, beams,
etc., just a flat, dull, metal surface.

[.]

It then abruptly moved to the left. It had made a right 90 degree
turn in a totally dumfounded way - like a ball bouncing off a
cushion in snooker. The lights remained in the exact
configuration and did not change. The whole thing was weird, it
was as though this craft was gliding at a very slow speed. It did
not pause or hover over the house, it went about this direction
change as one fluid movement. When the craft came towards us it
had the point to the front (1 light in front and two behind).
When it made the turn, it moved to the side and it did not
rotate.

This was the thing that really made me think it was something
odd, because things just couldn't move that way".

Steven Suddell.



'TRIANGULAR UFOS AND NOCTURNAL LIGHTS IN SE WISCONSIN'
By Charles Goldman

"Kevin Crump and his Grandmother Betty Barnick own an antique
dealership in the town of Delevan, WI. They travel home by Hywy
12 most often between the hours of 5:00 and 7:30 PM on a daily
basis. On February 4th 1993, Kevin and Betty were returning home
to FT. Atkinson via Route 12 at 5:35 PM. Kevin carries with him
in his car an RCA Camcorder. With it he likes to tape anything
that is newsworthy, plus he makes short, creative videos with his
friends. On the way home at about 5:30 they spotted a fire-engine
and decided to look for whatever was on fire. Both Betty and
Kevin were carefully watching for lights or the fire when Kevin
spotted something in the sky, from the driver's side window. "We
thought at first that it was a low flying plane. Then all of a
sudden it shot out a blue glowing ball from the tail-end of the
craft. It looked like a flame ball from a Roman candle. It shot
out about two inches, in ground to sky distance, with a trail of
twinkling lights. The blue ball just hung in the sky over the old
school to our left." They pulled off the road to get a better
look.

Kevin then got out his video camera and opened the door while
Betty decided to stay in the car. Kevin said, "I looked up and
saw the ship just about directly overhead. I could see a faint
outline of the ship because the moon was above it. The moonlight
reflected off the black metallic surface. It was the shape of an
oblong triangle with a light at each point. A red and a blue
light at the front and a white light at the back". An unusual
feature of this craft is that it traveled with the base forward,
instead of the point first as with most conventional craft.



To anyone concerned:
About one year ago (May 10, 1994 -- it was my husband's birthday,
so it was easy to remember) my husband and I were driving north
on I-25 from Colorado Springs, headed back to Denver and we saw
the most unusual thing:

He usually drives and I look at the sky thru our sunroof and try
not to fall asleep...there is usually some airplane activity and
so I usually don't pay any attention to lights in the sky...but I
noticed what seemed to be a fairly large "plane?" that wasn't
quite in the right place to be approaching any airports that I
knew of....and it was fairly low to the ground (later I realized
it was headed south and it was following the highway (I-25)). My
husband was also looking at it, but neither of us said
anything....we just "blew it off" as an approaching plane.

My side window was down and I expected to hear some kind of noise
since it was moving so low to the ground....at this point is
looked like two very steady lights that appeared larger than
normal for most planes, one light seemed bluish and the other
red...as it approached I could tell that there was a third light
(a round bulb shaped light like the first two), but it was very
dim. It was a dark section of the road, so I could see it very
clearly. It then passed over our car and I looked straight up,
the entire "plane" filled the sunroof and I remember thinking,
gee that pilot is a nut....he's flying so slow and so LOW, he
should be crashing on the ground or something. I remember
thinking, how strange, it was triangular shaped, kinda like a
stealth, with one of the "bulb shaped balls" on each point.

We kept driving in silence (The Air Force Academy was behind us
by about 15 miles and it was probably just a Stealth or something
flying too low (of course, there was absolutely NO noise as it
passed over). About 10 minutes passed and it hit me all of the
sudden...hey most planes like that would fly with a point of the
"triangle" shape to the front...but this "plane" was flying with
the flat-edge leading (with those two "bulbs" lit up) and the
point to the rear. I remarked on it to my spouse and he said,
"Yea, strange that I didn't realize it sooner, but it was!"

Heather Timmons.


I'm sure there are further comparative accounts and I'll see if I
have any on file. Any others which are known about, details would
be welcome.

My question was why do the saucers have to be American? Tim says that a
lot of the interesting documentation on saucer projects has been
destroyed. I do believe all the documentation on SUNTAN was destroyed, yet
there are drawings and at least one photo. All the documentation, tooling
and photos relating to TSR.2 were destroyed on Wilson's orders, yet we
have books full of photos, film footage, complete aircraft and a lot of
documents on TSR.2. All the documents on Station X were destroyed on
Churchill's orders, yet I've just watched a major TV series on the history
of Station X. Projects like Chevaline didn't exist, yet we have the
documents relating to Chevaline. Now we have Camille saying she might have
something in her attic. Looking in the obvious places is easy, but the
chances are some-one has been weeding. That piece of information in
Camille's attic could be crucial.

What you should have realised was that the documents were ordered to be
destroyed but the evidence exists somewhere. It is merely a matter of
finding it. That's why to return to my original argument that kicked off
this entire debate, we cannot exclude an entire knowledge base ie the
UFOlogists. You and I might not agree with them, but they do look at the
subject from a different perspective. What set me on the trail of British
hypersonics was Brian James' letter in the Fortean Times, odd reading
matter for some-one interested in aviation but it provides an excellent,
broad based forum for what is a wide ranging subject. I presume the FT has
knocked back Tim's work as well.

As I have repeated ad nauseum, I don't doubt the saucers exist(ed), but
think some more concrete evidence is required. I'd like to know what their
place in aviation history is, why they failed to see off conventional
aircraft, why have they been kept so secret. There must be a reason for
all this, were they inefficient, dangerous, did they lack payload, lack
range? Proving they exist is not the point, where they fit into the
picture is more important.

As for the Bicester delta, despite asking Tim and Andy Roberts for a
contact for the witness involved, neither have provided a means for me to
correspond with him. I have some drawings I'd like him to look at, but
without being able to contact him, I have to fear the worst. Mind you, I'm
the cynical, secretive and obstructive Chris Gibson. If you are willing to
pass on a letter, let me know.

1989, North Sea. Ten years on, despite fairly vigorous research, despite
Sweetman's and other people's efforts, I'm no nearer to finding out what
it was. I've come to the conclusion that my question will only be answered
when the people in charge decide it should be answered. Definitely the
long game, but I'm a patient chap.

If I had a quid for every drawing of a "SR-71 replacement" that has landed
on my doormat, I'd be a happy chappy. Which SR-71 replacement is it? The
tailed delta with the podded engines at midspan, the double delta, the
delta the compression lift, the Sweetman Mk1 or Mk2, the canard with
winglets or the long wingspan high aspect ratio SR-71 replacement. Ever
consider it isn't an SR-71 replacement? Hypersonics are so useful, but
like the saucers I have to ask, where are they? Remember the F-19? All
sorts of drawings did the rounds, but when the "F-19" turned out to be the
F-117, it looked nothing like the drawings that did the rounds. Over the
years I've come to view the speculative drawings as exactly that,
speculative.

There are no easy answers to this Snark hunt. I fully expect the Snark to
turn out to be a Boojum.

I think my original point has got lost in the mire. If the members of the
list want to pursue this Snark hunt along the lines of the UFOlogists,
carry on, I'll muddle away, bouncing ideas of the boys offshore, rather
than bouncing them off what should be a more learned forum. So far all
that has turned up is a blinkered attitude of a minority. If you want to
do it in a proper historical or scientific manner, a certain amount of
discipline is required. So look at the UFOlogists' output from a different
standpoint. They are as entitled to their opinion as any-one else, but you
might find something useful. It is quite satisfying to find something
where you least expect it.

You'll be glad to know I'm off to do my monthly porridge on Thursday, so I
won't be cluttering your hard disks.

Chris

I haven't read Matthews' book, but if in it there is - again - to be found
the theory that disc shaped devices were first developed by the Nazi's,
then I beg to differ.

Disc shaped devices were already dreamt of in the 1880's (documented). It
is a natural thing in the history of aviation to come up with flying
ciontraptions of all kinds, shapes and sizes. Sometimes disc shaped
devices were even built and test flown, long before darkness descended
over Europe with the coming of the Third Reich.

I have yet to see on scrap of real, hard, historical and verifiable
evidence that yes, those pesky Third reich boys built and succesfully flew
them. And I am not referring here to 2nd hand accounts, 50's newspaper
clippings or later Neo-Nazi pamphlets or Vesco's book, but real,
contemporary evidence. The germans documented almost everything they did,
but on those designs, we find nothing. And I will not take the `yes but
the plans were taken to Russia and the US and kept secret' stuff as an
excuse for lazy, sloppy or bad research in general.

I do think that it is a highly interesting theory that at least some UFO
sightings may be explained by earth technology; but what I want to see is
what I also want to see from the ETH proponents: evidence.

Kind regards,

Theo Paijmans

Some further background on that latter story; in answer to the
question of what position her father held, Camille explained:

"My father was a tech rep before people got degrees in such
things, and was on most of these flights doing assessments. There
were often several passengers on these flights; engineers, reps
from potential customer companies etc. The flying thing was
observed from the cabin, rather than the cockpit, although I
assume the pilot saw & reported as well. This was not a flight
where he was taking surveillance photos as far as I know - I
recall some kind of comments about why the Exacta wasn't with
him.

I've wondered if it was a glider @ an angle which concealed the
wings, or if the US somehow had an intact "V" up in the air. Is
it that unusual for an object like this to match speed & course?
On a low altitude Boeing test flight there's always the
possibility of misperceived aircraft; some of the test flights
out of Moses Lake in the 70s were intentionally @ very slow
speeds - alarming when hiking under one of them!"

She adds, "after years of just assuming that the sky was full of
stuff we either didn't understand, didn't want to admit we had,
or weren't supposed to see (this being just another one of those
'things'), I'm beginning to wonder about it. So I will look,
eventually.

Send me a list of aircraft project names like Have Blue, at some
point, and I'll look for them in the documents when I get into
them. There was a lot of back & forth between the techs @ Boeing,
Lockheed & McDD whether they were competitors or not".


Although 'Have Blue' would be later than the documents in
'Camille's attic', few of us wouldn't like the opportunity to see
exactly what was there.

Commercial high-resolution satellite vanishes after launch

Tuesday's launch
April 28, 1999
Web posted at: 9:52 AM EDT (1352 GMT)


LOS ANGELES (AP) -- A civilian satellite that can take the kind of detailed
photos that previously only spy satellites could produce disappeared shortly
after it was launched Tuesday.

An Athena II rocket carrying the Ikonos 1 satellite roared off a Vandenberg
Air Force Base launch pad at 11:22 a.m., bound for an orbit 400 miles high.

Communications with the spacecraft ended about eight minutes after liftoff,
as planned, but it failed to re-establish contact as expected later in the
flight. Officials could not say whether it remained in orbit.

Space Imaging, the Denver company that planned to operate the satellite, has
already built a spare one. John Copple, the chief executive officer, said he
expects it will be launched before the end of the year.

Ikonos 1, named after the Greek word for "image," has a camera capable of
resolving objects one meter square -- about 10 square feet. That means the
satellite would be able to distinguish between a car and truck, according to
Space Imaging.

Until now, only military satellites have been able to photograph Earth in
such detail. Some experts said they worried that images from Ikonos 1 could
be used by terrorists or enemy governments to plan attacks or spot
mobilizing troops.

The federal government approved the satellite in 1994. Space Imaging, a
privately held company, said it expects its clients to use the images for
urban planning, environmental monitoring, mapping, assessing the scope of
natural disasters, oil and gas exploration, monitoring farmland and planning
communication networks.

John Pike, an authority on space reconnaissance with the private Federation
of American Scientists in Washington, D.C., pointed out that the government
will not allow images of some places to be sold.

"The dilemma that you've got, though, is how do you make sure that Serbia
doesn't know where American troops are while making sure that American news
media is able to cover the war," Pike said. "And we're obviously going to
have a hard time drawing that line."

The satellite was built by Lockheed Martin Commercial Space Systems.
Raytheon built the communications, image processing and other

The U.S. Navy's "White Cloud" Spaceborne ELINT System
[Kosmicheskaya Sistema Radiotekhnicheskoy Razvedki VMS SShA "Uayt Klaud"]
by Major A. Andronov
Zarubezhnoye Voyennoye Obozreniye [Foreign Military Review] (ISSN
0134-921X), No.7, 1993, pp.57-60
translated by Allen Thomson

The US Navy's spaceborne electronic intelligence (ELINT) system, White
Cloud, is based on SSU (Subsatellite Unit) satellites and is intended for
determining the location of warships of foreign states and following them by
the method of taking bearings on the ships' onboard radioelectronic
equipment from several positions. Official Pentagon representatives try not
to attract attention to this system, since it is the principal means of
over-the-horizon reconnaissance and target designation for the US Navy's
weapons systems. In comparison with other American reconnaissance
satellites, (for example, "Keyhole" and "Lacrosse") the SSU satellites are
mentioned comparatively infrequently and have various names: White Cloud,
Classic Wizard, and Parcae.

The last designation more precisely reflects the mission and operating
principle of the system's satellites. The mythological Parcae were the three
daughters of Zeus and the goddess Themida (the SSU satellites are launched
in groups of three and fly relatively close together.) One of the daughters
spins the thread of fate for each mortal (one satellite has a wide
observation swath, but cannot exactly determine the coordinates of radio
emitters). The second daughter measures out a length of thread for each
person (when two satellites get a fix on the shipborne emitters, the
position is obtained, but with some ambiguity). The third sister (Atropos -
"she from whom one may not flee") cuts the measured thread of life (the
third satellite, getting a fix on the emitters' signals, enables their
coordinates to be determined precisely and then transmitted to Navy ships
for weapons employment....

Naval Ocean Surveillance System, also called Parcae

American military ocean reconnaissance system. The first experimental
satellite of this program could be 05678 / 71110A

Whitecloud (1976-1987, 9 satellites)

The NOSS constellation consists of three orbital planes, each containing
four satellites flying in formation; a main satellite and three
sub-satellites. Some believe that the satellites periodically deploy solar
sails to provide the propulsion required to maintain their precise formation
flight.
Another theory says the satellites would be connected by long (several km!)
wires?

Some of the NOSS launches carried a LIPS (Living Plume Shield) subsatellite.
In those cases a jetisonable toroidal plume shield, which protected the
satellite from the exhaust of the Star-37E motor, was fittet with some
solar-cell experiments.
The use of the Star-37E motor for the NOSS launches is somewhat conjectural,
but is performance fits good with the published wights of the NOSS
satellites.

Sighting Report
Occurred : 1/28/1999 06:30 (Entered as : 01/28/99 06:30)

some interesting things in the sky over north Scottsdale in AZ. I
wont speculate on what I saw but I will provide this brief
explanation. The rear balcony of my 2nd story apartment faces
east - north/east overlooking Stone Creek Golf course so I've a
very clear view with little or no obstruction. The other day I
was relaxing on my balcony just enjoying the sky as I am an
amateur astronomer. Then I saw a streak in the sky low on the
horizon about 10 degrees. This streak was black against the
darkening sky, and triangular in shape. The time was around 6:30
pm and the sky was turning a deep low saturation purple as is
does here in the desert. The shape almost reminded me of an
orderly flock of birds but it was clearly not birds as the speed
was way to great and there was no variation in its shape, it was
solid. The object covered at least 45 degrees horizontally in
about 2 seconds. I estimate the object to be approximately 2 to 4
miles distant making it quite large about the size of an f-15 or
larger. At first I thought this is what I must have seen but
there were no lights and no reflected light the only way I saw

no sound and what seemed to be a dark streak or trail behind the
object. I noticed that I could more clearly see the object by not
looking directly at it. As all astronomers know when looking at
very faint objects it is best to not look directly at the object
due to the make up of the human eye, rods and cones. I've a very
clear understanding of aircraft, speed, size and action. Just to
the north east of me is the Scottsdale Airpark, an airport that
can handle many types of jets up to small passenger jets. It is a
very busy airport and at any time you can see 4 to 6 jets on

see it more clearly. This occurred just after the full moon had
cleared the mountains in the distance. Again there was no sound
and the shape was triangular. I saw one and then within a few
seconds another one. I could clearly point at it and follow it
across the sky telling my friends as it crossed various reference
points such as houses and the moon. I'll be watching the desert
skies at dusk in that area everyday now with my camcorder in
hand.
[End]

Following on from comments made by Joel and yourself, I believe
it's now possible, maybe for the first time, to confidently state
that some of the more recent 'triangular UFO' reports can be
explained as exactly that.

One thing noticeable in looking at the NUFORC data was the number
of sightings which came from amateur astronomers who had seen
something 'triangular' moving at high altitude and could not be
equated with a satellite.

Reading through this data with the hindsight of what's been
highlighted here, it's evident that some observations are
consistent with 'triplets' of satellites. The following is a
classic example:

Occurred : 7/3/1998 00:30 (Entered as : 07/03/98 24:30)
Reported : 8/4/1998 00:33
Posted : 11/21/1998
Location : Campbell River (Vancouver Island), B.C.,
Shape : Triangle

I was laying out on my sundeck looking at the stars. It was just
after midnight and the sky was mostly clear with some high
cirrus. As I looked up I saw what I thought was a satellite,
except it seemed to be moving almost twice as fast as the average
satellite. It only took a fraction of a second for me to realize
that there was more than one point of light moving across the sky
(as described above). The three points of light that made up the
main outline of the triangle were a dull reddish-orange colour
and about the same size as most of the smaller stars that make up
the night sky. The two other lights that could be seen from
within the triangle were a white light but were no larger and
only slightly more intense than the outer lights. These two
lights were quite close together and located on either side of a
central axis extending from a halfway point at the base to the
apex and closer to the front of the craft. I could not see any of
the usual running lights associated with typical aircraft ie.
(port and starboard lights and the bright pulsing central light).
As it moved across the sky in a southeast to northwest direction
it seemed to me that there was no substance to this shape, as if
it were held together by strands of wire, with the leading light
pulling the others in tow. The colour within the triangle was
exactly the colour of the night sky, and there was no dark
silhouette, and no reflected light. It did make a slight sound as
it passed overhead but, the sound was not far behind which seemed
odd considering the speed it seemed to be travelling at. It was
not as loud or delayed as even the highest jetliners that fly
over. The best way to describe the size would be to say that
across the base of the triangle it would measure about the length
of an average human thumb extended to arms length, with the two
sides being slightly longer than the base. I was the only one in
my family to see this although my wife and three children were
all sleeping beside me. I tried to wake my wife but the duration
of the event was so short that she never had a chance to roll
over. I am 45 years old and I have been married for ten years I
have three young children and I live an otherwise normal and
routine existence. I have my own design and construction business
and my wife is a recreational co-ordinator. We own our house and
live in a suburban neighbourhood. I would like to know if anyone
else saw this object on this or any other night or if anyone can
give a reasonable or scientific explanation of this sighting.
[End]


Noting that, "it seemed to me that there was no substance to this
shape, as if it were held together by strands of wire, with the
leading light pulling the others in tow. The colour within the
triangle was exactly the colour of the night sky", it's a fair
bet that what was observed within the triangle of lights _was_
the night sky.

Can't explain the 'slight sound' and would have to assume this
was unrelated or inadvertently imagined.

James, Chris, List members -

I have been looking for better information on these triplet
satellites...obviously it's hard to evaluate the accuracy of the data on
things that are as classified as these spacecraft are, but evidently there
are at least two independent systems that use these triad configurations -
NOSS/White Cloud/Parcae being the older system going back as far as 1976.
Drawings and technical details at:
http://www.fas.org/spp/military/program/surveill/noss.htm

The second system is Space-Based Wide-Area Surveillance System, SBWASS:
http://www.fas.org/spp/military/program/surveill/sbwass_n.htm

"Under the unacknowledged program, the first Navy SB-WASS triplet (USA 59 -
1990-50) was launched on 8 June 1990 by the second flight of a Titan 4 from
the Eastern Test Range. The booster was launched at a reported inclination
of 51 degrees, but a significant plane change maneuver placed the spacecraft
into a circular 454 kilometer orbit inclined at 61 degrees. A subsequent
maneuver on 19 June raised the inclination of the orbit to 63.4 degrees, and
following this maneuver three SB-WASS sub-satellites were released.

The identity of these primary payloads was initially unclear, with several
interpretations under discussion, including a possible relationship to the
KH-9 SIGINT sub-satellites.

However, it is clear that both of these launches also included a triplet of
sub-satellites, which were placed into a 63 degree inclination orbit that
would permit them to maintain a stable relative formation in orbit. Thus
these sub-satellites have been interpreted as being probably related to the
NOSS program. Each of these would have a mass of several thousand kilograms,
consistent with the presence of an advanced infrared scanning sensor, such
as was contemplated under the acknowledged program.

A second triplet (USA 72 - 1991-76) was launched on a Titan 4 on 8 November
1991. A third attempted launch ended in failure on 4 August 1993. At least
one more launch is planned to complete the operational constellation. This
occured on 12 May 1996..."

The SBWASS triplet satellites are enormous. C. P. Vick's drawing shows that
the solar panels have 100-foot spans.

A chart at
http://www.fas.org/spp/military/program/surveill/open.htm
shows a timeline for the development of parts of this system. It may be of
interest that the "Bus 1" propulsion system for SBWASS, shown at the bottom
of this page, was apparently proposed at one point as a possible replacement
for the then-delayed Russian FBG propulsion module of the International
Space Station.

Apologies for unnecessary facetiousness in previous posts.

- J Carpenter

Bill Rose has taken at some images of these things, and with his

BEGIN QUOTE
Satellite Formation

During the early hours of April 26 1992, I was making a series of
night sky tests with a new wide aperture 50mm camera lens near to my
home in Eastern England.

As I wound on the film and opened the shutter, I spotted a formation of
what appeared to be three satellites entering my field of view and I
managed to make two 15 second exposures on very fast B&W film.

A couple of minutes later, the three points of light had passed beyond
visual range, although I noticed they were very close to each other and
seemed to be travelling in a highly inclined polar orbit.

I guessed they were probably NOSS (Naval Oceanic Surveillance
Satellites) or perhaps a Russian equivalent, but enquiries (to the
RGO, NASA and BAA's satellite section) failed to track down any launches
which might have been responsible.

The pictures have subsequently been published in several magazines and
there has been some response from other astronomers who have seen similar
formations.

Bill Rose
END QUOTE

I’d like to make a few very quick observations on the way things seem to be
going here on with the discussion of man-made, unconventional aircraft and
their place in the study of aerial phenomena:

I know Joel has spent a good deal of time and effort in researching the
subject, and his comments are based on that body of work. For that
reason, I take his points very seriously.

As far as I'm aware, none of us looking into this area have the answers to
>all< the questions that arise from the man-made hypothesis, so FWIW, I
feel we should exchange information where possible rather than argue.

I know factors like writing books and articles will delay this exchange to
some extent for obvious reasons, but we need to decide which is more
important: getting to the bottom of these things or pushing our own pet
hypotheses.

James has taken the trouble to set up this invitation-only list to keep the
noise level down, isn't it up to us ensure we draw on the
collective experience of those here to generate some meaningful signal ?

Finally, no-one is suggesting that a/c of whatever type are a panecea of
explanation for all UFO sightings, but no-one here would argue that a/c do
generate UFO reports. As we know, the CIA has admitted to early U-2 and
A-12 flights being the cause of many reports. On the grounds of OPSEC, it
seems reasonable to assume , that should classified a/c (operated by
whatever agency) be dimissed as UFOs, it would their owners very well.

David

This may seem off-topic, but it's an example of how you can "read between
the press releases" to get a pretty detailed picture of how open projects
relate to "black" programs. If you went to the reconnaissance agencies and
asked them for details of the propulsion system of the Triplet
reconnaissance satellites you'd be laughed out the door. But with just a
little hunting I found the items below, which give many details on the
International Space Station's Interim Control Module, which was based on the
Triplet's maneuvering engine module. With a little more digging you can get
down to the actual engines used, fuels, etc. IMO, more of this needs to be
done re the alleged FTs.

- J Carpenter

http://www.nrl.navy.mil/pao/rel-97/7-97r.html
NRL Revamping Control Module for NASA Space Station

(Washington, DC · June 1997) -- A spacecraft previously designed and flown
by the Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) on a Titan IV rocket has been
selected by NASA to serve as the back-up Interim Control Module (ICM) for
the International Space Station (ISS).

ICM will be mated with the ISS via the Shuttle, and will reboost the ISS to
higher orbits and provide attitude and guidance control for the positioning
of the spacecraft. ICM may also provide a refueling capability that could
extend ISS operations for up to 3 years. Using this spacecraft in
combination with Clementine- and NASA-derived hardware designs, NRL will be
able to meet NASA's tight schedule for providing a means to control the ISS
during its critical "build-up" stage and keep this major U.S. space program
"on track."

ICM, which was originally designed by NRL's Naval Center for Space
Technology (NCST) in the 1980's to launch on NASA's Space Shuttle, was first
named the Shuttle Launch Dispenser (SLD). It was developed for and funded by
the National Reconnaissance Office.

The SLD program had passed its Phase Two Safety Review at the time of the
Challenger accident in 1986. Subsequently, all Department of Defense
missions were directed to launch on expendable launchers. The SLD had to
launch on the then-new Titan IV, which necessitated that certain
modifications be made. At that time, the instrument was renamed the Titan
Launch Dispenser (TLD). The first TLD was launched from the Eastern Test
Range and therefore, the system has gone through all the field processing
and safety reviews required to load its 12,000 lbs of bi-propellant fuel and
oxidizer.

The TLD program ended in 1996. All residual hardware was retained by NRL for
future potential use. Modifications are now required to change the TLD into
the ICM needed for the ISS. TLD was spin-stabilized and ICM requires
three-axis stabilization.

Propellant management devices will be added inside the propellant tanks and
the attitude control electronics will be changed to a three-axis design. NRL
had previously developed the three-axis Clementine spacecraft and many of
those designs and components will be used on ICM. Clementine also used a
110-lb thrust main engine, which will replace the 900-lb engine used on TLD.
The Command and Data Handling will be changed to make it ISS compatible and
will include communications via tracking and data relay satellite systems.

http://ifmp.nasa.gov/codeb/budget2000/HTML/RPA.htm
The U.S./Russian Cooperation and Program Assurance (RPA), as part one Step
one, was initiated in May 1997. It provided contingency planning funds to
address ISS program requirements resulting from delays on the part of Russia
in meeting its commitments to the ISS program. The first step in the
contingency plan, which was to protect against a potential further delay in
the SM, has been implemented. The ISS program is purchasing an interim
control module (ICM) from the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) to
provide attitude control and reboost functions for continuation of the ISS
assembly sequence in case the Russian SM is launched later than July 1999.
The NRL’s ICM is currently being prepared to support a March 2000 launch to
back up any shortfall of Progress fuel resupply vehicles. The Program is
also maintaining an option to attach it to the back of the Russian-built
functional cargo block (FGB), should the Russian Service Module slip
considerably beyond its scheduled launch in July 1999.
Step One of NASA’s RPA contingency plan had two primary components. First,
modifications were done to the Zarya, an element purchased from Russia and
owned by the U.S, to enhance the Zarya’s propulsion control capabilities and
make it refuelable. The Zarya was launched on November 20, 1998. Second, the
development of an interim control module (ICM) is being pursued to ensure
that sufficient attitude and reboost capability is available if required in
the assembly sequence. The Zarya modifications and the ICM addition will
enable the on-orbit build to continue even without the Russian Service
Module, although not as planned due to the loss of the Service Module’s
habitation resources...

http://www.marquardt.com/products.htm
 In the early 1960s – the dawn of the space age – Kaiser Marquardt developed
and produced man-rated high performance 100 lbf earth storable liquid rocket
engines for the Apollo Service Modules and Apollo Lunar Modules. Subsequent
man-rated engines produced by Kaiser Marquardt included the 870 lbf Primary
and 25 lbf Vernier thrusters for the Space Shuttle Orbiter. The most recent
application of Kaiser Marquardt’s 100 lbf and 25 lbf engines are for the
International Space Station Interim Control Module.

110 lbf (490 NEWTON)
LIQUID BIPROPELLANT ROCKET ENGINE
Model Number R-4D

Technical Description

The Model R-4D rocket engine is a pressure fed liquid bipropellant
configuration providing a nominal thrust of 110 lbf (490 Newton) at a
minimum inlet pressure of 210 to 235 psia (15 to 16 bar). The demonstrated
operating thrust range is 60 to 135 lbf (270 to 600 Newton). The engine
design incorporates radiation and fuel film cooling and a C-103 (niobium)
combustion chamber material operating at 2350ºF (1300ºC). The engine is
capable of operation at electrical pulse widths from less than 0.050 second
to 45,000 seconds of steady state on time. Solenoid valves provide positive
isolation of the nitrogen tetroxide oxidizer and monomethylhydrazine fuel
during non-operating periods. The engine has also demonstrated more than 2
hours of firing time using hydrazine fuel at specific impulse levels of 317
seconds.

Dr Dennis P. Gordon fron the National Institute of Water &
Atmospheric Research, near Wellington, New Zealand, wrote:

"The fire salp Pyrostremma spinosum (Pyrostoma) achieves lengths
of 20 m. Photographs were published in 1971 of giant colonies
(with a diver entering one end) in New Zealand waters (see
references below). Divers described the organism as a looking
like a giant sock. Their powers of propulsion are limited but I
presume they may appear to accelerate if affected by the
underwater wake of a passing vessel.

References :

Baker, A.N. 1971: Pyrosoma spinosum Herdman, a giant pelagic
tunicate new to New Zealand waters. Records of the Dominion
Museum (Wellington) 7(12): 107-117.

Grace, R.V. 1971: Giant pyrosoma seen in New Zealand seas.
Australian Natural History 17(4): 118-119".


Gustav Paulay, from the Marine Laboratory, University of Guam,
also responded:

"The pelagic tunicates known as pyrosomas fit the shape,
luminescence and even approach that size, but not the speed".


If the reported speed of the object was actually within
parameters for Pyrostoma, then this explanation seems a
reasonable conclusion; the luminescence especially, I would have
thought was a significant clue.

It can't be proven of course, however, am I correct in assuming
this conceivable explanation hasn't previously been considered?



James.

Brad,

For general information and appreciating this may be known, there
are two comparative films to the Trementon footage which were
shown on 'Sightings'.
One source of these is a video, 'UFOs Over Mexico', available
from UFO Magazine (UK). It's a recording of the presentation
given by Santiago Yturria Garza on 8 September 1996 at the Quest
International conference.

I've had a look at this again and amongst the footage shown by
Santiago are two films, one shot in Monterrey, Mexico on October
27, 1992 and the other attributed to South Korea, September 1995.

Some of the 'Sightings' segment is included, featuring the almost
obligatory analysis from Jim Dilettoso, plus the Trementon
footage. The comparison between all three films is highlighted
and the similarities are quite striking.

Do they depict birds spiralling in a thermal...

Unfortunately, all were filmed from considerable distance,
however, the Monterrey and South Korean films seem to show an
initial compacted cluster of bright or reflective objects which
then slowly disperse and are descending, not ascending.

It's suggestive of a balloon cluster, or something along these
lines, which have been released at altitude.

If either of the more recent films could be explained, it would
probably resolve the other, although I'm not sure how this might
equate with the Trementon footage, taken some 40 years
previously.

I would, however, suggest the least likely source is small,
reflective 'alien spaceships' with nothing better to do and I'm
sure the actual explanation is attainable.

Anyway, something I had noted to mention.

Are we dealing with three films which show the same, as yet
unidentified, objects?


James.

James,

I'm not familiar with the Mexico and Korean footage so I can't comment on
possible similarities to the Tremonton (not "Trementon"), Utah, film of July
2, 1952.

One point I might add is that on the C-E or 1947 List someone rebutted that
Dr. Robert M. L. Baker had done a simulation of the Tremonton film with a
movie camera. However, it turns out that Baker did his experiments in
Southern California using stationary painted targets instead of actual flying
or soaring birds, and he does not specify the make and model of movie camera
in the report I have (1968 House Symposium on UFO's).

Baker himself recommends, " However, actual movies of birds in flight would
have to be taken to completely confirm this conclusion." (p. 140) Baker had
concluded that the images did not conform to what would be expected for
birds.

Brad

Hello All -

Just a note to let those interested in the Trementon footage that I
had the opportunity to speak to Newhouse in the 1970s. He told
me then, as he told others earlier, that he and his wife had seen
the objects close at hand. By the time he got the car stopped and
his camera out and began filming, the objects had moved off a long
way.

The Blue Book files, as well as Ruppelt's book suggest that Newhouse
told others that the object had a specific shape and that as they flew
over the car, he was unable to identify them. Unfortunately his film
provides us with few real clues.

Date: Wed, 12 May 1999 19:51:42 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: Fu-Go Balloons

UFO Research List

* LIST ONLY *

A historical topic, specifically relevant to the PROJECT-1947
mailing list and cross-posted from there for information.


James.

_____

I recently came across a book called 'Secrets and Stories of
the War' published in 1963 by the Reader's Digest.

It contains an insightful article about the Fu-Go (Fugo)
balloons and I thought it might be of further interest:

JAPAN'S LAST SECRET WEAPON - BALLOONS
By Brigadier-General W. H. Wilbur
(Formerly Chief of Staff, US Western Defence Command)

The first bombing of Tokyo, on 18th April 1942, hit the
Japanese right in the middle of their pride. Casting about for
a means of reprisal, they conceived the first transoceanic
automatic-balloon campaign in history. It took them two years
to get ready, but in the six months following 1st November 1944
they turned loose 9,000 ingeniously contrived gas-bags,
engineered to drop incendiary and fragmentation bombs on
American forests, farms and cities.

These new weapons, thirty-three feet in diameter, were
designed to travel across the Pacific at an altitude of 30,000
to 35,000 feet, where prevailing air currents move towards
America at the rate of 100 to 200 miles an hour. Although no
human hand exercised any control over the balloons - even by
radio - after their release, it is conservatively estimated
that between 900 and 1,000 of them reached the American
continent.

They appeared everywhere, from Alaska to Mexico. Nearly 200
more or less complete units were found in the north-western
United States and western Canada. Fragments of seventy-five
more were picked up on land elsewhere or fished out of the
coastal waters of the Pacific, and flashes in the sky
indicated to observers that at least 100 exploded in mid-air.
Efforts have been made to belittle this attack. The fact
remains that it marked a significant development in the art of
war. For the first time, missiles were sent overseas without
human guidance, and the threat of damage was very real.
Fortunately winter snows eliminated the forest-fire hazard. If
the balloon assault had continued into the dry summer, when
America's vast western forests were like tinder; if the
Japanese had maintained their March 1945 rate of launching an
average of 100 balloons a day; and if they had equipped them
with hundreds of small incendiaries instead of a few large
ones - or with bacteriological agents - they would have
wrought havoc.

The Japanese made their first mass balloon tests in the spring
of 1944, setting loose 200 trial gas-bags. None of these
reached American shores. The first successful ocean-spanning
balloons were released on 1st November 1944, and on 4th November
the first report of them was received. That day a navy patrol
craft spotted what looked like a large fragment of tattered
cloth floating on the sea. A sailor tried to drag the fragment
aboard and discovered a heavy mass attached to it. Unable to
lift it, he slashed it off with a knife, thus permitting the
undercarriage of gadgets and explosives to sink. All that was
salvaged was the envelope; it bore Japanese marks, however,
and revealed the fact that something mysterious has been
introduced into the struggle of war.

Date: Thu, 13 May 1999 07:50:10 -0400
From: James Easton <pulsar@compuserve.com>
Subject: List 'Housekeeping'

UFO Research List

These are the simple 'housekeeping' rules:

1. The 'UFO Research List' is intended to provide a focused
forum for any related topics which recognise the need for a
scientific and evidential foundation.

It's that twilight zone which is devoid of abject nonsense
and where objectivity replaces resolute 'religious', or
sceptical, dogma.


2. The list is also primarily intended to enable secure
discussions and as subscribers may request feedback on new
data or privately debate controversial, sensitive issues,
etc., ALL contributions are therefore 'LIST ONLY - IN
CONFIDENCE' unless otherwise denoted.

If it appears on this list, it shouldn't be seen anywhere
else without the originator's permission.


3. Archives of messages posted to the list can be viewed on
the ListBot server, at URL:

http://www.listbot.com/

Log in as a list member under:

contents - log in - list member

You will require the password provided by the list server
when you subscribed.

If that's been mislaid, use the 'Lost yours?' link above the
password field.


4. You can also use the member log-in to:
- unsubscribe
- change your password
- change the e-mail address where you wish mail to be sent
(very useful and this can be done regularly)
- add e-mail aliases, i.e., provide additional addresses you
might send mail from
- update your member profile, i.e., any information you may
have provided when you joined the list.


5. The list address for mail is:

UFORL@listbot.com


6. With some e-mail software, using 'reply' may not send a
response to the list, it will be sent ONLY to the address
shown in the 'From' heading, which is the person who sent
the mail. Using 'reply to all', as recommended by the
ListBot notes, may send a reply to both the list and the
person who sent the mail, if that's required.

It's recommended that the destination of your reply is
therefore checked before sending and should always be:

UFORL@listbot.com


7. The standard mailing list code applies and messages
should be no more than 65 characters in length.

If replying to mail, only the relevant section(s) should be
quoted, not the entire original message.


8. The list software also requires that each posting is no
larger than 100k in size.


9. Strict 'Netiquette' rules apply and all postings are
expected to be cordial, ensuring the list is always a
pleasant environment.

For further information see:

http://www.pbs.org/uti/guide/netiquette.html


10. Any related problems or queries should be addressed to:

UFORL-owner@listbot.com


James.
E-mail: pulsar@compuserve.com

Expanding on some 'housekeeping' items:

"With some e-mail software, using 'reply' may not send a
response to the list, it will be sent ONLY to the address
shown in the 'From' heading, which is the person who sent
the mail. Using 'reply to all', as recommended by the
ListBot notes, may send a reply to both the list and the
person who sent the mail, if that's required.

It's recommended that the destination of your reply is
therefore checked before sending and should always be:

It's strongly recommended that instead of using the 'reply'
function (unless you know this works fine with list mail),
you send all list mail, including replies, as new messages
to:

UFORL@listbot.com


"If replying to mail, only the relevant section(s) should be
quoted, not the entire original message".

Please check that you're reply isn't trailing the entire
original message!


"The list software also requires that each posting is no
larger than 100k in size".

This is a new and significant enhancement, the previous
limit was 10k.


"Strict 'Netiquette' rules apply and all postings are
expected to be cordial, ensuring the list is always a
pleasant environment".

Some initial, 'heated' viewpoints were expected and although
a few comments were noted as less than congenial, I trusted
that would all settle down.
As it looks like this list is here to stay and it's intended
to expand the membership to over 100 subscribers in the near
future - for example, a number of recognised scientists who
are known to have an objective interest in the subject
matter are being invited to join - that period of leniency
has expired forthwith.


One of the advantages of having this list is that people can
be invited to subscribe, even for a short time.

Similar to an on-line conference, someone who has e-mail and
was agreeable to answering questions, perhaps discussing
their research, encounter, experience(s) etc., could be
subscribed for a brief period.

Any suggestions along these lines?


There's also no reason why current subscribers can't invite
others to join the list, providing of course any new
subscribers fully understand the list's objectives.

Those interested in subscribing can write to:

UFORL-subscribe@listbot.com

They will then be sent the standard 'verification' message.

Following on from comments made by Joel and yourself, I believe
it's now possible, maybe for the first time, to confidently state
that some of the more recent 'triangular UFO' reports can be
explained as exactly that.

One thing noticeable in looking at the NUFORC data was the number
of sightings which came from amateur astronomers who had seen
something 'triangular' moving at high altitude and could not be
equated with a satellite.

Reading through this data with the hindsight of what's been
highlighted here, it's evident that some observations are
consistent with 'triplets' of satellites. The following is a
classic example:

Occurred : 7/3/1998 00:30 (Entered as : 07/03/98 24:30)
Reported : 8/4/1998 00:33
Posted : 11/21/1998
Location : Campbell River (Vancouver Island), B.C.,
Shape : Triangle

I was laying out on my sundeck looking at the stars. It was just
after midnight and the sky was mostly clear with some high
cirrus. As I looked up I saw what I thought was a satellite,
except it seemed to be moving almost twice as fast as the average
satellite. It only took a fraction of a second for me to realize
that there was more than one point of light moving across the sky
(as described above). The three points of light that made up the
main outline of the triangle were a dull reddish-orange colour
and about the same size as most of the smaller stars that make up
the night sky. The two other lights that could be seen from
within the triangle were a white light but were no larger and
only slightly more intense than the outer lights. These two
lights were quite close together and located on either side of a
central axis extending from a halfway point at the base to the
apex and closer to the front of the craft. I could not see any of
the usual running lights associated with typical aircraft ie.
(port and starboard lights and the bright pulsing central light).
As it moved across the sky in a southeast to northwest direction
it seemed to me that there was no substance to this shape, as if
it were held together by strands of wire, with the leading light
pulling the others in tow. The colour within the triangle was
exactly the colour of the night sky, and there was no dark
silhouette, and no reflected light. It did make a slight sound as
it passed overhead but, the sound was not far behind which seemed
odd considering the speed it seemed to be travelling at. It was
not as loud or delayed as even the highest jetliners that fly
over. The best way to describe the size would be to say that
across the base of the triangle it would measure about the length
of an average human thumb extended to arms length, with the two
sides being slightly longer than the base. I was the only one in
my family to see this although my wife and three children were
all sleeping beside me. I tried to wake my wife but the duration
of the event was so short that she never had a chance to roll
over. I am 45 years old and I have been married for ten years I
have three young children and I live an otherwise normal and
routine existence. I have my own design and construction business
and my wife is a recreational co-ordinator. We own our house and
live in a suburban neighbourhood. I would like to know if anyone
else saw this object on this or any other night or if anyone can
give a reasonable or scientific explanation of this sighting.
[End]


Noting that, "it seemed to me that there was no substance to this
shape, as if it were held together by strands of wire, with the
leading light pulling the others in tow. The colour within the
triangle was exactly the colour of the night sky", it's a fair
bet that what was observed within the triangle of lights _was_
the night sky.

Can't explain the 'slight sound' and would have to assume this
was unrelated or inadvertently imagined.
