Now I have some rather technical questions (you can guess that I
am an engineer) Some of them are to check the veracity of other
sources, while others are to refine my understanding of the
process used:

- Was there any indication on the scope of signal strength, or
  was it clipped, so they got a yes/no indication?

- Was any other means of measuring signal strength (an s-meter or
  the like) used?

- Was there any form of AGC on the ELINT?

- Was it possible on that ELINT for the contacts to stick in such
  a way that BOTH dishes received at the same time?

- Were the characteristics of ship radars then in use checked?

- What was the frequency range of the equipment?

- If the frequency range was wide, how did they get a sharp focus
  at all frequencies used? I know a parabolic dish works better
  than any other antenna, but even those have anomalies at
  some frequencies.

- Was initial signal detection done broadband, by automatic
  sweeping of the tuning, or manually tuning through the band?

- How was the frequency of the signal determined?

- Could a very strong signal blast its way through the open relay
  contacts? If so, it's possible to fake a signal moving upscope
  and particularly one orbiting the plane with a transmitter on
  the ground.

- For that matter, could a strong interfering signal have entered
  the receiver in stages after the tuner?

- Since there were several units, could they have been
  interfering with each other only when set a certain way?

- Did all of the ELINT consoles work off the same antenna pair ,
  or did each one have its own antennas

- Was the rotation of the sweep on the display actually
  produced by rotating a transformer coil, as Klass depicted?
  If so, then how was the sweep limited to one quadrant (since
  transformers don't pass DC)? Or was the deflection coil
  actually rotated (and Klass's drawing is misleading)?

- Was the amplitude of the sweep driven by a sweep oscillator (as
  it is in RADAR), or by the incoming signal?
- Was there a RADAR set on the plane?

- Could someone have been covering up sloppy maintenance (like
  leaving a tube shield off) to avoid demerits?

One case this might explain and which immediately leaps to mind
is Paul Hamner's 1978 encounter which I documented. The full
account is on my web site at:

http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/paul_h.txt

Paul stated:

"In March 1978, I was working on such an assignment in my
home county of Lincolnshire, UK. One Thursday night, I finished
work at about 10.30pm and drove a colleague home to the village
of Alford.

My route home took me up a hill on the A1104 towards Ulceby
Cross. Part way up the hill, at around 11:00 p.m., I was dazzled
by what I took to be the undipped headlights of an oncoming car.
I flashed my own headlights and slowed. To my astonishment, the
oncoming lights slowly "took off" from the road and gracefully
flew to my right. Excitedly, I stopped my car, wound down the
driver's side window and peered out. The sight that greeted me
will stay in my memory forever.

I saw that the lights were coming from a massive, beautiful
aircraft which had now turned, was flying at a height of about 50
feet and was now heading towards the coast directly over my car!
The craft was shaped like a delta, very similar to the Vulcan
bombers based in Lincolnshire at the time.

However, it was about four times the size of a Vulcan, flew
extremely slowly and was absolutely silent! All leading edges of
the delta were beautifully rounded - there were no sharp
protuberances such as a tailplane. The underside of the craft was
coloured sky blue. It just glided over me and headed towards the
coast - no noise, no smoke, no vibrations, no smell - just an
aircraft of sheer gargantuan beauty.

It was very real; from the A16 I was able to watch this craft
making its slow, majestic way south towards Boston until I lost
sight of it just past Spilsby. I'd love to know what it was. It
seemed too real to be extraterrestrial. However, its immense
size, its low speed and above all, the sheer silence made it
unlike any aircraft known to me!"

Asked `how wide and how deep was the object?', Paul told me:

"Other than the craft itself, and a few small trees,
I had sight of no other structure by which I could gauge it.
However, I could compare it to the Vulcan bombers with which I
was familiar (the Vulcan squadron was based at RAF Waddington,
Lincoln at the time.) I would say that the area of the delta was
about four times that of the Vulcan. The depth of the delta was
about the same as the cabin section of a Boeing 747. As far as I
can recall, the depth was the same throughout the delta.


Paul seems confident about the size difference and when also
asked, "Were there any markings of any kind, even the smallest
detail like a different coloured section, which you can recall?",
replied: "No markings at all. Just an even light blue underbody.
No roundels or numbers or logos!".

Wouldn't there have been some markings visible on a Vulcan?

I suppose it depends on how good the visibility actually was. At
10:30 in March, Paul would have been driving in the countryside
in the dark of night and it would surely have been difficult to
be certain of any observations.
Could also maybe throw size perspectives way off.


Paul notes that Vulcans were stationed at RAF Waddington in 1978.
Would they possibly still be flying night ops then?

How feasible is it that Paul witnessed a Vulcan which was gliding
at such low altitude - maybe coming in to land?


James.

From: Andy Roberts <Brigantia@compuserve.com>
Subject: Ufology fiddles whilst Max Burns

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

I note with great interest the recent posts about Max Burns being
found guilty of serious drug supply charges. Many people have
been bored to tears over the past two years by the Max Burns
saga and the 'war' which has taken place between him and
other UFO researchers keen to promote the truth. It has
diverted valuable time, money and resources from real
UFO research.

Yet if Dave Clarke, Tim Matthews, Martin Jeffry and myself had
not challenged Burns at every turn ufology
and the public would be more duped than they have been.
We defend our actions and will happily do it again the next time
a charlatan rears his/her head in the subject.

No doubt we will learn of his sentence at the appropriate time
but for the moment there are some useful points to be
considered.

Max Burns appeared suddenly on the UFO scene a few years
ago, claiming a long standing interest and research in the
subject. He stated on many occasions that he was
looking for 'fame' and 'money'. His 'big chance' came with the
alleged 'Sheffield UFO Crash', promoted as an ET event
exclusively by Burns and which has been closely intertwined
with his criminal activities ever since.

Many things could, and will, be said about Burns' involvement
with ufology and I think we have a right to say them now that
his case is almost at an end. Here's a few..............

*     At the 1997 BUFORA Conference Burns stated, in
front of several witnesses, that he had bribed a key witness
to the Sheffield case with marijuana.

*      When challenged about this he ranted and raved,
saying he had never used drugs in his life and was going to
take legal action against me for libel. The facts have turned
out somewhat different and Max is guilty of drug dealing.
I repeat my statement again - that Max Burns bribed a key
witness to the 'Sheffield' case with marijuana. The fact that
this witness has disappeared into the woodwork notwithstanding,
this incident is an excellent example of just one of Burns' lies and
manipulations of truth to fit his own fantasy prone view of the
Sheffield 'UFO Crash'. I trust any researcher stupid enough to
subscribe to Burns' views on this case will read these words
carefully.

*      The British UFO Research Association (BUFORA)
were major supporters of Burns throughout this time. He was
in communication with several council members and active
members of BUFORA (Steve Gamble, Judith Jafaar, Malcolm
Robinson, Richard Conway and many others according to emails
Burns sent to me) eventually persuading them he had a right to spout
his lies on a BUFORA lecture platform. BUFORA Council members
were made fully aware of the nature of Burns' evidence and of his
involvement with drug dealing and yet, incredibly, gave him a
platform to speak - taking his word over that of their Press Officer,
Journal Editor and many other key personnel and investigators.
BUFORA were also fully aware that many of the 'facts' Burns'
used in his presentation were imagined, untrue or unverifiable.
This did not deter them and, in some bastardised version of
promoting 'free speech' they allowed Burns to manipulate their
organisation and membership.

BUFORAs Council's grip on ufology in the UK, reality in general,
and their understanding of ethical practice within the subject must
be called into question over their sponsorship of both Burns and
his interpretation of the Sheffield case.

The facts appear to be that BUFORA will sink to any level to
produce 'infotainment' with which it can fool its' membership.
And that once again the elite ruling body on Council will have its'
way despite any representation from other officers or its
membership.
Democracy? I think not.

Perhaps BUFORA should make a public statement as to whether
they now supported a convicted drug dealer and his lies about the
Sheffield case?

Of course the deluded and the nutcases in ufology will not take
heed of the Max Burns affair. Some will believe he is innocent and
has been set up by 'UK intelligence', as he puts it. I only wish this
were the case - he might have been stopped sooner.
Others will continue to believe there is an extraterestrial element
to the Sheffield case. All permutations of stupid believes will
abound but the plain and simple facts are that ufology in the UK
was taken is - yet again - by a huckster.
And that - yet again - BUFORA gave its support to something it
knew nothing of but thought it could make ufological capital and
money from.

If ufology in the UK ever wishes to be taken seriously by the
establishment it needs to learn the lessons of the Burns farrago.
I very much doubt it will as long as its leaders are more interested
in profit and promotion over hard fact.

I leave you with two thoughts:

*    A careful reading of Burns' court case makes it plain that
not only was he a drug dealer but that he was intent on passing
ordinary amphetaine off as Ecstasy. Therefore he cannot even
claim any ideological reason for his drug dealing - this was ripping
people off purely for financial gain.

*      Burns, on many occasions accused myself and Dave
Clarke of working for the government and being part of a plot to
infiltrate and set-up ufologists in the UK. Isn't it therefore extremely
strange, to say the least, that Max Burns' trail and sentencing
comes in the same week as Dave Clarke leaves his post at the
Sheffield Star and moves on to other things. As he said to me the
other day 'my work here is done'. Quite!

I hate to say we told you so...............................

Happy Trails

Andy

Bruce & List,

I agree with your renewed challenge to James Easton to "DRAW A MAP." In lieu
of a map, as we discussed a month or so ago, I've deduced that the only way
Easton's theory can even have a ghost of a chance given a 110+ mph airplane
which would easily overtake 30-35 mph pelicans is if Arnold's plane ORBITED
THE FLOCK OF BIRDS at a distance of about 1-3 miles. That way roughly the
same distance would be kept and Arnold would not overtake the birds -- unless
he chased them. But Arnold would have to keep the "bird" UFO's off to HIS
RIGHT THE ENTIRE TIME, viewing them through his passenger side window
instead
of watching them cross his front windshield -- which is a major discrepancy
for this bird-orbit theory.

In order for this orbiting or circling maneuver to keep the birds projected
towards Mt. Rainier and then Mt. Adams as Arnold reported for the UFO's,
Arnold would have had to be heading NNW at first, then turning to the right.
It is true that Arnold reported making a 180- or 300-degree right turn over
the town of Mineral just before or perhaps during the first "flashes" he
sighted (there is a discrepancy in Arnold's accounts as to the size of the
turn and exactly when he first saw a "flash"). At the end of the circling,
Arnold's plane would have had to be headed nearly due East towards Yakima in
order for the birds to be projected past Mt. Adams to the southeast. And he
was indeed heading for Yakima. So these are points in favor of the
bird-orbit theory. But according to Arnold he was heading to Yakima
virtually the ENTIRE TIME OF THE SIGHTING, and he says nothing about
watching
during a turn, nor anything about having to view them off to his right
instead of crossing directly in front of him.

But how could Arnold be unconscious of the fact he was in a turn the entire
time? How could he not realize he was circling around the birds on a short
1-3-mile radius? He might have to bank at an angle to do the turn and
possibly might not be able to see objects near the horizon from the passenger
side window if so tilted. How could he perform the turn and at the same time
release the aircraft controls to use the cowling tool to measure the angular
size of the objects as he reported he did? Seems awkward if not downright
dangerous. How could he briefly turn his plane to open his window to see the
objects if he was ALREADY IN A TURN? Couldn't Arnold have simply chased the
birds and overtaken them in just about one minute's time? He says he
deviated from course to measure the five-mile length of Goat Ridge right
after the sighting so he should certainly have been willing to do so in order
to investigate the mysterious objects if he thought he could catch up with
them -- but obviously he didn't, they were much too fast.
Regards,

Brad Sparks

Now I have some rather technical questions (you can guess that I
am an engineer) Some of them are to check the veracity of other
sources, while others are to refine my understanding of the
process used:

- Was there any indication on the scope of signal strength, or
  was it clipped, so they got a yes/no indication?
COMMENT: ECM/ELINT Operator No. 2, Maj. McClure told the Condon
Committee it
was a strong signal comparable in signal strength to that of the ground
radars he picked up at the same time and then tuned out in order to focus on
the UFO signal.

- Was any other means of measuring signal strength (an s-meter or
  the like) used?
COMMENT: Don't know. Possibly ECM No. 1 Provenzano's APD-4 did and it also
continuously recorded, too. Records kept in highly classified storage, no
one has succeeded in locating or getting released.

- Was there any form of AGC on the ELINT?

- Was it possible on that ELINT for the contacts to stick in such
  a way that BOTH dishes received at the same time?
COMMENT: Don't know.
- Were the characteristics of ship radars then in use checked?
COMMENT: Yes.
- What was the frequency range of the equipment?
COMMENT: I think McClure's covered 1,000-5,000 MHz.
- If the frequency range was wide, how did they get a sharp focus
  at all frequencies used? I know a parabolic dish works better
  than any other antenna, but even those have anomalies at
  some frequencies.
COMMENT: They tuned into a narrower band.
- Was initial signal detection done broadband, by automatic
  sweeping of the tuning, or manually tuning through the band?
COMMENT: I believe it was manual.
- How was the frequency of the signal determined?
COMMENT: AN/APR-9 signal analyzer.
- Could a very strong signal blast its way through the open relay
  contacts? If so, it's possible to fake a signal moving upscope
  and particularly one orbiting the plane with a transmitter on
  the ground.
COMMENT: Doubtful.
- For that matter, could a strong interfering signal have entered
  the receiver in stages after the tuner?
COMMENT: Doubtful. Other ground radars in the same S-Band range were
displayed normally, concurrent with the UFO signal.
- Since there were several units, could they have been
  interfering with each other only when set a certain way?
COMMENT: Doubtful. Nothing like this ever occurred again (or before) on the
same plane. McClure was on it for 4 years.
- Did all of the ELINT consoles work off the same antenna pair ,
  or did each one have its own antennas
COMMENT: I believe each had their own antennas. Provenzano and McClure had
their own for sure.
- Was the rotation of the sweep on the display actually
  produced by rotating a transformer coil, as Klass depicted?
  If so, then how was the sweep limited to one quadrant (since
  transformers don't pass DC)? Or was the deflection coil
  actually rotated (and Klass's drawing is misleading)?
COMMENT: You'll have to ask Klass.
- Was the amplitude of the sweep driven by a sweep oscillator (as
  it is in RADAR), or by the incoming signal?
COMMENT: Don't know.
- Was there a RADAR set on the plane?
COMMENT: Yes, a navigation radar, APS-23 I think.
- Could someone have been covering up sloppy maintenance (like
  leaving a tube shield off) to avoid demerits?
COMMENT: Doubtful. This was thoroughly checked back at the home base,
Forbes AFB, afterward.

Philip Klass writes:

"You are welcome to share following with UFORL...

I visited Socorro in late 1966 and tape-recorded interviews with
all of the principals. However, where I quote Zamora (below),
same is based on interview with Zamora, conducted several hours
after the (alleged) incident by FBI Agent J. Arthur Byrnes,
acting in an UNOFFICIAL capacity. Byrnes chanced to be in Sgt.
Chavez office when the latter received a call from police radio
operator Lopez saying that Zamora wanted Chavez to come to the
"site." Prior to my visit to Socorro, I obtained a copy of the
complete Project Blue Book files on the case, including prints of
pix taken shortly after the incident, showing the odd-shaped
"landing pad prints."

The map of the area contained in my first book "UFOs--Identified"
does show the location of the airport. In my 2nd book, the map
was "shortened" a bit (cutting out the airport location) to make
room for the lengthy caption. Can provide you with a copy of the
original (via airmail) if you wish.

Following comments are numbered for your convenience if you wish
to respond. Although I am convinced the incident was a hoax,
inspired by Major Bursom to attract tourists, I will refer to
"UFO" or "object" as IF Zamora's tale were true.

(1) Zamora reportedly was chasing a speeding car headed south on
a rough (noisey road when I drove it in 1966) when he claimed
his attention was attracted by a "ROAR" and a "flame in the sky."
Assuming Zamora was driving 60 mph. to try to catch speeder, the
"roar" would have had to be quite loud to hear above ambient road
noise. Zamora said he initially suspected an explosion of the
Mayor's dynamite shack near the UFO.

(2) Zamora reported that he had an (estimated) 20 seconds for
close-up viewing of the UFO when he parked 100-200 ft. away from
it. He seemingly had a sufficiently close look to (reportedly)
see a symbol on the "egg-shaped" object. If true, surely Zamora
would recognize that the object was some kind of a balloon--even
if he had NEVER seen one or a picture of same.

(3) Surely he would have seen one/two balloonists in their
basket. Yet Zamora reported that "the persons [he allegedly saw
briefly from a distance of about 800 ft.] were NOT seen when I
got up to the scene area. But Zamora reported seeing TWO LEGS
extending from the object.

(4) Zamora reported being terrified when the UFO took off with a
very loud roar." Hot air balloon launches do NOT create "a
very loud roar."

(5) Zamora reported the UFO flew off in a SOUTHWEST direction,
passing over the dynamite shack--(and Highway #60)--NOT Due SOUTH
towards the airport. (If headed for the airport, object would
have passed over/near Felix Phillip's house.)

(6) Altho the alleged incident occurred around 5:45 p.m., THERE
WERE NO OTHER WITNESSES--other than Opal Grinder's ALLEGED
tourist--which is a "tall tale" exposed in a White Paper of mine.
Copy on request. If there had been ANY OTHER witnesses, surely
they would have come forward during the next several days when
there was a widely publicized investigation by White Sands Capt.
Holder, by Dr. Hynek, by Blue Book chief, and great media
interest nation-wide.

(7) As Dr. Hynek stated in his report to Project Blue Book, after
his first 1-day visit, this incident was "one of the major UFO
sightings in the history of Air Force consideration of this
subject." (Based on Hynek's recommendation, the USAF sent
letters of inquiry to many major and minor aerospace/defense
companies asking whether they had built an experimental craft and
tested same in vicinity of Socorro on April 24, 1964. None had
nor could they offer a possible explanation or hypothesis.)

Question #1: If Socorro incident involved a hot-air balloon
landing, why did the balloonists opt for a scrubby, dangerous
aroya instead of landing 1/2 mile south at the Socorro airport?
IF landing site was result of an emergency--say a malfunction of
balloon's heater-burner, what a curious coincidence that they
were able to fix the problem in only a couple minutes that it
took for Zamora to drive to the site. How curious that the
balloonists did not greet Zamora and explain why they had been
forced to land on the aroya.

Question #2: Why didn't the balloonists promptly come forward
and explain their role in the widely publicized UFO incident--
explaining the emergency landing. At worst, they might have been
fined $25 for tresspassing on Mayor Bursom's desert property
without his permission.
[End]

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 1999 09:56:45 +0100
From: John Burtenshaw <jburtens@bournemouth.ac.uk>
Subject: Re: Night Flights

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/


>Any chance you could scan the Vulcan photograph and make it
>available?

>replied: "No markings at all. Just an even light blue underbody.
>No roundels or numbers or logos!".
>
>Wouldn't there have been some markings visible on a Vulcan?

The colour is interesting. Vulcans went through a number of camo changes
from anti-flash gloss white in the 60's, green/grey upper camo and white
undersurfaces to all over green/grey wrap around camo. Never seen a sky
blue undersurface, but it could be reflection from the white. At one point
the all RAF aircraft lost their underwing serials and the roundals became
very small. The current fashion is light grey with toned-down markings
which are very hard to see.


>I suppose it depends on how good the visibility actually was. At
>10:30 in March, Paul would have been driving in the countryside
>in the dark of night and it would surely have been difficult to
>be certain of any observations.
>
>Could also maybe throw size perspectives way off.

Could be I've confused a bizjet with a bigger airliner when it was landing
at dusk...

>Paul notes that Vulcans were stationed at RAF Waddington in 1978.
>Would they possibly still be flying night ops then?

I would think so - I'll check to what Sqn was based there and what they
were tasked with.

>How feasible is it that Paul witnessed a Vulcan which was gliding
>at such low altitude - maybe coming in to land?

According to my pilot friend, a Waddington landing began with an approach
from 50,000ft over Carlisle (they need such a long one to bleed the speed
off). It was a GCA (Ground Controlled Approach) e.g a talk-down by
Waddington as the Vulcan was not ILS equipped. The normal approach was to
reduce power at the start and let the speed bleed off during descent (the
Vulacn had no flaps). It was basically a glide approach with full power
only applied if a go around was required. A Vulcan landing was a
High-Alpha landing with the wing being used to aerodynamically slow the
aircraft on landing e.g the pilot kept the nose high until the speed
dropped and nose wheel touched the runway when the chute was released.

So it could have been a landing Vulcan.

Cheers

John

Bruce wrote:

>problem of explaining why Arnold first saw the objects north of
>Rainier (from his MOVING persepective) and last saw them seeming
>to go past Mt. Adams, yet, at all times they were far enough
>from his plane that he couldn't see the wings flapping and
>thereby identify them as birds. This essentially means that at
>their closest they were a mile or so away.

Bruce,

It means nothing of the kind.

As I've pointed out before, there are no `scientific formulas'
which can be applied to an observer's perceptions at a given
point in time. All things are possible, there aren't any `no
ways'.

You can't apply maths in people's ability to judge, reason,
understand, become overexcited etc., especially when they could
face the exact same situation on other occasions and respond
differently each time.

It's called human nature and often it's just incomprehensible.

Like... how someone like Kenneth Arnold could have a second
encounter with even more `UFOs'.

Although he noted how their flight characteristics were so
similar to the nine unfamiliar objects previously observed,
Arnold experienced that this formation of... how did he describe
it again... "a cluster of twenty-five brass coloured objects that
looked like ducks", flew at a speed which outstripped his
airplane.

Many rational folks would conclude these were ducks and Kenneth
Arnold's perception and conclusions were somehow,
incomprehensibly, consummately mistaken.


We'll never know what Arnold observed in any of his numerous
sightings and and can't prove if he was correct in his reading of
situations, or, whether he made judgmental errors, as can clearly
be evidenced seems a reasonable possibly.

His June 24th report is a singular witness testimony and aside
from a great story, will always be open to interpretation. For
all we know, the accounts(s) he gave are completely inaccurate.

As I've said before, the `believers' will believe and the
sceptics will `disbelieve'. No amount of debate, only proof, will
ever change that.


>Just because Easton was supremely confident in his explanation
>doesn't mean he was right.

I don't think I've ever been that confident it was the actual
explanation!

I had increasing confidence in the possibility that a formation
of birds was a reasonable, logical conclusion.

That's all.


Presumably the astronomer you refer to is Dr Jacqueline Mitton,
the Royal Astronomical Society's Public Relations Officer. I have
on tape Dr Mitton's recent appearance on UK Breakfast TV. She
clarified how Arnold's sighting did not involve `flying saucer'
shaped objects and his most widely-known sketch was of a bird-
like object. Dr Mitton then explained how birds can be highly
reflective and under certain conditions could take on the
appearance of `UFOs'.

Both these comments are of course correct.

Her conclusion that Arnold observed a flock of birds seems to
have been reached independently of anything I have published,
although she will shortly be aware of what I have published and
why.

Maybe she will see it as an endorsement to learn of Capt. Moore
and his co-pilot's sighting of nine "big round disks weaving
northwards" on 12 July 1947 in the Cascade mountain range. These
flying disks were, as you know, identified as a formation of nine
pelicans.

What she makes of it all is up to Dr Mitton, although I'm sure
she will find the background research to be interesting.


James.

only see flashes from the objects, not the objects themselves.

of the sun from ground objects which are not themselves
distinguishible (e.g., glint from the windshield of a car
when at an altitude of 35,000 ft; you can't see the windshield
or the car, but you can see the glint).
Unless you can produced "polished pelicans with alumnum
covering" or some such, there is "no way" the pelicans could
reflect light from the sun like a metal surface.

From: RB47Expert@aol.com
Subject: Re: Re: Arnold again?Cc: brumac@compuserve.com
UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Bruce, James & List,

I must chime in with my agreement with Bruce. For the bird theory to work it
has to explain most or all of the facts of the sighting, and those that it
doesn't explain must be clearly set out and a satisfactory explanation given
for the failure of the bird theory on those points. I especially appreciate
Bruce's points about "sensor physiology" and the fact that Arnold had the
presence of mind to conduct an "angular size resolution test" DURING the
brief sighting, not just reconstructing it from memory afterwards. This was
a very SCIENTIFIC procedure that Arnold carried out, along with timing the
objects, and opening his window to view them. Arnold should be credited for
carrying out scientific experiments so to speak on a real-time UFO
observation. Few have ever done that in the decades since.

The linear path Arnold reported, of objects appearing to the north of Mt.
Rainier and disappearing south of Mt. Adams, is an absolutely fundamental
aspect of the Kenneth Arnold sighting. Have we forgotten that he made his
famous CLOCKING of the objects' travel from Mt. Rainier to Mt. Adams????
This MUST be explained.

As I have pointed out, the only way Arnold could see birds projected into the
distance towards Rainier and then Adams is if he ORBITED the birds in his
plane from a distance or radius of about 1-3 miles. But then he would always
see them off to his right, through the passenger side window, and never
crossing his front windshield as he reported. Arnold was indeed in a
180-300-degree turn just before or at the beginning of the sighting and at
the end of the turn he was headed east towards Yakima exactly as he would
need to be in order to see the birds off to the south past Mt. Adams. All
these could be points in favor of the birds, except that it prohibits Arnold
from ever seeing the objects cross in front of him or from briefly turning
the plane so he could open his window for an unobstructed view -- which he
reported. And as Bruce rightly points out, the brightness of birds is
insufficient. Arnold reported ARC-LIGHT brightness of the "flashes" so
intense it LIT UP HIS PLANE -- the intensity was so great he thought he was
in a near-collision with another aircraft reflecting sunlight directly at him
from close range. None of Easton's eyewitness reports of birds "flashing" in
the sun or appearing "metallic" in sheen can match Arnold's uniformly
reported sun-like BRIGHTNESS. I've never seen a sunlit bird even from close
range that could blind me with its reflected light.

Notice we're giving the bird theory every benefit of a doubt by not arguing
SHAPE or extreme DISTANCE (Arnold distinctly reported the objects passing
behind certain mountain peaks which would put minimum distances at 20+ miles
far beyond bird visibility).
Regards,

Brad Sparks

described had he seen birds. This is a logical procedure,.
And then you fail to take the crucial logical step and demonstrate
that the grossest detail of Arnolds sighting, that he first saw
them north of Mt. Rainier and last saw them passing Mt. Adams
(from his persective) can be explained by th bird hypothesis.
Until you make this final proof it is illogical to accept the
bird explanation as consistent with the sighting.

>That's all.


>Presumably the astronomer you refer to is Dr Jacqueline Mitton,
>the Royal Astronomical Society's Public Relations Officer. I have
>on tape Dr Mitton's recent appearance on UK Breakfast TV. She
>clarified how Arnold's sighting did not involve `flying saucer'
>shaped objects and his most widely-known sketch was of a bird-
l>ike object. Dr Mitton then explained how birds can be highly
r>eflective and under certain conditions could take on the
>appearance of `UFOs'.

>Both these comments are of course correct.

Of course? I have pointed out to you (and to her) that
the initial sighting was at such a distance that Arnold could
only see flashes from the objects, not the objects themselves.
This is a characteristic of highly reflective materials. Anyone
who flies in airplanes a lot can occasionally see bright glints
of the sun from ground objects which are not themselves
distinguishible (e.g., glint from the windshield of a car
when at an altitude of 35,000 ft; you can't see the windshield
or the car, but you can see the glint).
Unless you can produced "polished pelicans with alumnum
covering" or some such, there is "no way" the pelicans could
reflect light from the sun like a metal surface.

Subject: Re: Re: Arnold again?Message-id: <a3f39db3.251c5f92@aol.com>

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

James & List,

The case you cited of the ad plane reported as a saucer was recited entirely
without quantitative data and without reasonable error margins on the
numbers. This would be like analyzing the Arnold case but without his
clocking, no angular size measurement, no references to known landmarks and
measured distances, no mentions of estimated altitudes and altitude
variations. Al Hendry has a page of drawings of ad planes looking like
classic saucers and reported as UFO's (UFO Handbook p. 92). On pp. 94-96
Hendry shows how he resolved UFO-like behavior in many of these cases.
Interestingly, when Hendry explains these cases he usually introduces
specific quantitative data.

To me, a UFO case without reliable quantitative data is worthless. That's
why as minimal initial screening criteria for UFO Best Evidence I require a
minimum of TWO WITNESSES each of whom gives detailed accounts covering
necessary data (it's no good to have only one witness report and just say "oh
there were 20 others who saw it too"), the duration must be at least 1 MINUTE
of continuous observation by each witness and of an object of at least FULL
MOON (0.5 deg) angular size during the minimum 1 minute. This won't
eliminate all IFO's but it will help prevent a total waste of time spent on
marginal cases. I haven't developed screening criteria yet for photo, radar
and other instrumented or physical trace cases.

But under my initial screening criteria I would never include the
essentially-single-witness Arnold case in a Best Evidence list (independent
witness Fred Johnson on Mt. Adams does not have a duration or angular size).
The Socorro case would not pass either if it had no landing traces, but since
it does I can't technically eliminate it yet based purely on screening rules
(but it could be eliminated if the hot-air balloon theory proves out). The
point is that I use the screening criteria so as to not waste valuable time.
Certain cases that are "classics" command extra attention but for other
reasons than the quality of the case.

Brad Sparks

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

John Burtenshaw's observations on the markings on recent military aircraft reminded
me of the "black helicopter" syndrome afflicting many a UFO witness / investigator.

The Fortean Times was due to publish an article on black helicopters, but it seemed to
have been pulled for some reason. I was rather looking forward to it. Anyway, here
we go...

Being an old hand at recognition, mention of black, unmarked helicopters always
makes me smile. Why?

1) Almost any aircraft in flight will be seen as a silouhette against the lighter sky, ie
black

2) No markings will be seen on a sillouhette, ie appears unmarked

3) Most frontline military helicopters are matt dark green or dark grey to reduce their
chances of being seen from above by fighters, or against the landscape as they operate.
The very dark paint also has some IR signature reducing properties.

4) The US Army applies very small, low contrast ("toned down" is the term)
markings to their choppers. These are very difficult to make out at a distance and
especially against a lighter background such as the sky. Even if they are seen in good
lighting conditions they will appear unmarked.



What about these silent ones though, eh Chris?

A variant of the MH-6 was a specially developed version of the McDonnell Douglas
(nee Hughes, now Boeing, I think) Defender possesing several stealth characteristics,
one of which was acoustic signature reduction. The method was to reduce the rotor
rpm. The same company also developed the NOTAR (NO TAil Rotor), again
reducing the acoustic signature.

Nothing sinister then? Has anyone done any research into the black helicopters and if
so what was the conclusion?

Chris

That, of course, depends on the relative distances of the pelican
and the mountain. For example, if a pelican is one mile distant,
an airplane is 15 miles distant, and a mountain is 30 miles
distant (do we have the figures on this?), there are a lot of
differences:

 1. Different amounts of light scattering in the path of vision.
 This causes different maxima in contrast, with closer objects
 having more contrast.

 2. Different real sizes for the same subtended angle.

 3. Different perceptions for an object of the same real
 brightness.

 4. Different speeds for the same angular velocities.

But that depends on how far away the mountain is from you,
compared to the small plane. You are saying that the climber is
ON the mountain. The pelican theory says that the pelicans are
much CLOSER than the mountain is. Halation (see below) would also
tend to mask a dark climber on the white background.

@Kathleen Andersen

There is another mechanism that night be at work here: Halation
in the retina of the eye. Halation is the scattering of strong
light within the retina itself. It makes bright objects appear to
be larger and more rounded than they are. I cite an example from
experience:

One day in 1974, I was in northern Indiana, and I saw a large
silver sausage come from behind a tree. It glittered in the sun.
Since I had never seen anything like it (except maybe the
Goodyear blimp), I watched it closely. I wondered if this was
what others were seeing and reporting as UFOs.

Suddenly, it dimmed and shrank to about a third of its thickness
and about 5/6 of its length. I then immediately recognized it as
a DC-3. Halation strikes again. BTW, video and film cameras react
the same way to bright sources of light.

It is possible that Arnold saw objects that would have been below
the resolution of his vision except for halation.

***

I tend to think that (rather than pelicans) Arnold saw a flight
of propeller-driven predecessors to the YB-49 flying wing. I
can't remember the designation of these, but they were mostly
wing, with a ovoid fuselage in the middle, four pusher
propellers, and round vertical fins at the ends of the wings.

A footnote on this: I modified some nightscopes in 1984 for use
in scientific experiments. As a test, I took one of them out at
night and looked around. Just as was reported in the Rendlesham
case, I saw a house that appeared to be on fire. But without the
nightscope, the house looked normal.

The nightscope really sees infrared light. Since the infrared
frequency chosen includes the black-body-radiation frequency of
body temperature, people walking down the street glowed, as did
the warm air rising from that house, which had poor insulation.
Some windows glowed, even when there were no lights on inside,
and a flashlight I put on the sidewalk looked like a burning
torch after a minute.

This could explain the path the men took to the farmhouse. Before
they got there, they were using the nightscope, and homed in on
the infrared leaked from the house.

It is also probable that the objects seen on the second day were
fire balloons, since their characteristics matched distant fire
balloons. They tend to make their appearance immediately after a
UFO sighting becomes publicized.

From: TPrinty@aol.com
Subject: Re: Atmospheric effects on star observationMessage-id:

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

In a message dated 09/24/1999 6:21:56 PM Hawaiian Standard Time,
brumac@compuserve.com writes:

<<
You can seen twinkling of distant ground lights under some conditions...
but whether this is "bad" or not depends upon what you are seeing or
trying to see. Any object which subtends an angle of about 0.1 degree
(1/5 the moon diameter) will not generally be affected by turbulence.
(It can be affected greatly by atmospheric transparency, of course.) >>

I disagree with this statement and as an amateur astronomer, I have
seen stars affected by atmospheric effects quite often. Stars twinkle
because of the earth's atmosphere and therefore ARE affected by
atmospheric turbulence. The degree of twinkling is very indicative of
atmosheric conditions and many planetary observers will refrain from
photography when stars are twinkling too much.

Quoting from McGraw-Hill Enclyclopedia of Science and Technology
we find out why stars "Twinkle".

"High-altitude winds and local air currents carry atmospheric irregularities
across the line of sight. Because the entrance pupil of the human eye is
much smaller than the characteristic size of atmospheric irregularities,
any twinkling that is visible to the unaided eye is caused primarily by the
modulation of the light intensity and not by the deflection of the light
waves. Modulation is best understood as an interference phenomenon acting on
adjacent light waves. Like random waves in water, sometimes the waves
add constructively, causing the star to brighten, and other times the waves
add destructively, causing the star to dim.Stars experience a process called
scintillation which is common under atmospheric conditions of turbulence."

Scintillation is a common effect that fools many inexperienced observers.
I have sat out and watched the star Sirius vary in brightness, intensity, and
color. People, who have never seen this often feel that the star is an
airplane with landing lights when they see it low to the horizon. Here in
Hawaii, I see Sirius do this almost every night. Probably due to the
atmospheric conditions around the islands. Looking at Minneart, we
find out why the colors change (p.67):

"The colour changes are to be ascribed to slight dispersion of the
normal terrestrial ray curvature, so that the rays from the star travel
along slightly different paths in the atmosphere, according to their
colour. For a star at a height of 10° above the horizon we compute
distance between the violet and red rays to be as much as
11inches at a height of 1.25 miles, and 23 inches at 3 miles.
The air striae are, on an average, fairly small, so that it may often
happen that the violet ray passes through a striation and is
deflected, whereas the red ray passes on without deviation. The
moments when the light of a star becomes brighter or feebler as
a result of scintillation are, therefore, different for the different
colours… Colour changes never occur, apparently, at altitudes
of more than 50° , but frequently below 35° . The most beautiful
scintillation of all is that of the bright star Sirius, which is visible
in the winter months rather low in the sky."

Then there are many cases of stars being misidentified as UFOs.
The Condon committee and Hendry were quite familiar with the effect.
Even Dr. Hynek was aware of how stars can be misidentified by an
observer. In Michigan, during the UFO flap in the '66,
Dr. Hynek accompanied several police officers in viewing one UFO
which turned out to be Arcturus. He also described how the star Capella
fooled one pilot who was trying to chase it 1952. It appears that the
effects of scintillation played a significant factor in this case.

Additionly, it does not take much for autokinesis to set in and make a
star appear to jump back and forth or appear to approach and recede.
Coupled with color changes induced by scintillation and the observer can
feel that the star is moving and flashing landing lights or signalling the
observer. Atmospheric effects DO affect how stars appear to the naked
eye observer.

Tim Printy

Force Combat Control Teams, and have logged more hours than I
care to recall in helicopter varients. Being involved in CCT's,
there were many reasons to use helicopters, and different
varients using different color schemes were used for different
scenarios.

Yes, there are black helicopters. And there are olive helicopters
and sub-dued olive and sub-dued black helicopters. There are deep
blue helicopters and light blue helicopters and white helicopters
and silver helicopters. There are orange helicopters and there
are yellow helicopters. The point is, pick a color and the
military could probably pull one out of inventory somewhere and
give you a reason for the odd color.

researchers" then it does for camoflauge and radar concerns.

to "conspiracy" but rather for up close and personal air and on
ground identification. I do not deny that there are helicopters

> 0.003 ft = 0.036 inch approx. I think Arnold also stated the objects were
> about 100 feet in size if at 23 miles, which is about the same angular
size
> 0.8 milliradian approximately.)

The DC-4 is really the calibration, isn't it? His eyesight was very good if
he could resolve the outboard engines on a DC-4 15 miles away. Or possibly
it was closer than that?

From: RB47Expert@aol.com
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Arnold again?Cc: ufx@mindspring.com
UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Joel,

Because Arnold didn't give us the dimensions on his "zeus fastener or cowling
tool" or the distance he held the tool from his eyes, we must use his size
comparison based on the DC-4 that was simultaneously visible and trust he did
his calculations correctly and that he estimated the 15-mile distance
correctly (in his ca. July 10, 1947, letter to the AAF). He gave differing
figures for the distance to the DC-4, such as 20 miles (AP Pendleton, Ore.,
June 26, in Boise Statesman, June 26).

Arnold did NOT say he actually SAW the engines on the DC-4, only that he was
comparing the UFO dimensions to the separation distance of the DC-4 engines,
"if" the object was placed over the DC-4 what "would" the spacing have been
(Idaho Statesman, June 28, 1947). Since he was familiar with the appearance
of DC-4's he would not need to see the engines to know how to compare their
spacing.

Yes, 1/30th of an inch is small but engineering rulers are routinely
graduated down to 1/64th inch. I can see even the 1/64th graduations at 4
feet. That's 0.33 milliradian or 1 arcminute (the full moon is about 33
arcminutes diameter). It's at the limit of visual acuity.

However, I think there is another serious problem for the accuracy of
Arnold's angular size estimate and visual acuity for the details he reported:
 The objects were in motion at a high angular rate of at least 1 deg/sec.
Moving objects present less contrast than stationary ones (the contrast is
spread out over a larger area).

BTW, I noticed an AP story from Seaside, Oregon, datelined June 28, 1947
(from Twin Falls Times News June 29) which mentioned that "A recent issue of
Mechanix Illustrated said that the navy [sic] has developed a plane
designated the XF5U1, 'a queer, saucer shaped object' capable of well over
500 [sic] miles an hour." If the magazine article came out BEFORE Arnold's
sighting, using the words "saucer shaped," maybe Arnold read it and it
suggested those words to use in his account, leading to decades of
misconceptions about the actual shape.

Regards,

Brad

strikes me that someone sees a UFO and a chopper flies nearby, its a black helicopter,
a part of the UFO conspiracy. How common are choppers around population centres?

not spooky.

1) Black helicopters exist

3) It's just a coincidence they turn up with UFOs

Date: Sat, 25 Sep 1999 17:49:41 -0700
From: Greg Long <greglong@nwmyst.com>
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Re: Arnold again?

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Brad, Joel, Bruce, and Kathleen,

I've been finding the recent discussion regarding Kenneth Arnold's sighting
of June 24, 1947, very interesting. It appears that the latest analytical
result indicates that the objects Arnold saw were not more than glints or
flashes, quite tiny actually, in the very far distance. Of course, such
glinting objects suggest a meteor, or meteors, or a fragmented(ing) meteor
moving in a straight-line. These multiple objects were moving from north to
south, and although seemingly low in altitude, would not preclude a
low-flying meteor. Hell, if a meteor can crash to earth (which they do),
then they can travel at low altitude.

I had an experience while on the top of Mary's Peak one night. The peak is
in western central Oregon, 1,400 feet. My wife and I were stargazing and
looking for a repeat of strange lights we had seen on two previous nights.
Suddenly we saw a bright object plummet at about a 60-degree angle from the
north to the south, in a straight line, as if heading toward the apex of
the mountain that we were standing on. The object was quite bright, a
phosphorus white, and generally heel-shaped, similar to Arnold's
description. It also had a flat, one-dimensional appearance. I recall a
faint streak behind it. Of course, we all know that it is nearly impossible
to calculate distance of lights at night, and precise location is near
impossible. The sighting lasted about a second, but the object weas quite
clear and definite.

One solution to the Arnold mystery is to do something rather simple and
obvious. And that is to rent two aircraft. One of them would be Arnold's
plane, which resides in a museum I think in Wyoming, and the other would be
a plane the estimated size of the objects Arnold saw. Two pilots would fix
these aircraft at their approximate locatons on June 24, 1947. This would
be done under very similar weather conditions, perhaps in late June. From
here, the experiment is fairly simple. Can "Arnold" in his plane west of
the sighting location see the aircraft or not? Mr. Maccabee can generate
the necessary experimental parameters; video tape or film can be involved;
blah blah. Why no one in the UFO field has ever done this is a puzzle.
Well, actually, not a puzzle. It costs money and takes time; and ufologists
are famous for just reading paper reports. Few, if any, EVER do any actual
field work or observation. I may be wrong, but I think Mr. Maccabee
"analyzed" the hoaxer Ed Walters "photos" over the phone, and instructed
Walters to set up some type of stereo-camera system, again by phone. It's
always easier to do research by mail or phone than to get of one's butt and
go to the scene, and especially to do all the necessary character checks,
etc.
In addition, I am appalled (well, actually, pretty accepting now) at how
so-called ufologists have refused to, or just didn't care, to actually dig
into every aspect of Arnold's character, personality, personal history,
values, beliefs, profession, and so forth, to thoroughly evaluate his real
observational abilities and his analytical expertise. I have attempted to
do this myself by reading everything in his personal files. I found it very
interesting that his book Coming of the Saucers was really very poorly
written, and that when you study the government documents and all the
material available on the Tacoma Incident (Maury Island) you discover that
Arnold's mindset in the summer of 1947 was charged with anxiety and
paranoia. This was, of course, the result of the fear and fascination
gripping part of the American populace during the 1947 wave, and the
extraordinary impact Arnold's sighting had on him starting soon after the
sighting of June 24. Arnold may have observed accurately on June 24, but
did he, suddenly thrust into the limelight and under the intense scrutiny
of journalists and the focus of military investigations, actually maintain
a clear head as he continued to repeat and recite his sighting over and
over again to reporters?

Most interestingly, how did the glints and flecks of white light he saw on
June 24, 1947, take form as a sharp crescent-shaped "wing" with a black
circle on it in the painting that he had commissioned after the sighting?
Also, can someone tell me what were the actual names of the mountain peaks
that his nine objects weaved in and out of? This purported motion of the
nine objects is absolutely critical to an understanding of what he saw.
Even from my vantage point of Bellevue, Washington, and from Interstate 5
looking east, for the life of me I cannot see any of these peaks, only the
immensity of Mount Rainier. I look to be enlightened on all these matters.

Greg (The Huge Person--Six Feet Eight Inches Tall and Now a Massive 300
Pounds of Flesh) Long

Just because you night scope detected infrared doesn't mean theirs
did. There are "starlight scopes" which use photoemissive cathodes that
are not sensitive to infrared but which are VERY sensitive to lo light from
starlight (and other souces of visible light).

Incidently, the typical home video camera, and I presume the digital
cameras, are sensitive to "near infrared" which is light that is "too red"
to make an impression on your eyeball, but yet which is not
the infrared generated by "warm bodies."

under such conditions and this will be readily seen by a naked eye observer.

Subject: ARNOLD: FLASHES IN THE DISTANCE

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Brad wrote:
>
You are right to point out the ambiguity in Arnold's use of the DC-4 size
comparison as to whether it was relative or absolute. His 100-foot figure
comes from the 1977 Fate Symposium.
And you are especially right in pointing out the objects were "tiny glints"

<

This brings up an interesting point: the brightness of a flash of light
from a
mirror surface 100 ft in diameter at 100,000 ft (simple aproximations to
true
size and distance). As I have pointed out before, reflection of the sun
from a FLAT
mirror is is like looking directly at the sun. If the angular size of the
mirror is
larger than that of the sun (say 0.008 radians approx), then you will see
the
WHOLE brightness of the sun (if 100% reflective). If the mirror is
smaller
in angular size, then you see a fraction of the suns brightness given by
(ignoring diffraction effects important for really small reflectors)
(D mirror)^2 / (D sun)^2. In this case I pick D mirror = 100/100000 =
0.001 rad
(1 milliradian or 1 mr). THe sun is about 8 mr. Hence the brightness of
a
FLAT (circular) reflector of 1 mr angular size (oriented correctly to give
a
reflection, of course) is (1/8)^2 = 1/64. The sun is so bright that even
1/64th of
its brightness is brighter than the surrounding sky.

I posted the following message way back in November 1997 (yes, this
argument has been going on a LONG time) (edited slightly
to make it relevant to today):

ASSUME the initial sighting by Arnold was when the objects were
50 miles away. He said he could see the light flash on his plane. At
this
 point it is necessary to determine what Arnold meant by a "flash
 on his plane" Was it so bright that he actually saw light reflected off
 his plane and ten into his eye?
 I doubt it since this was full daylight and the objects were
 very distant.
 On the other hand, if meant that light was reflected TOWARD his
airplane and the light entered his eye directly it could be quite
 bright IF THE OBJECTS REFLECTED LIKE MIRRORS, which is
 what Arnold seemed to imply. When you look at a mirror reflecting
the sun you are actually looking
at the sun(!), just from a different direction than directly toward the
sun.
If the angular size of the mirror is smaller than the sun's angular size
(i.e., less than about 8 milliradians or about 1/2 degree), then you are
looking at a piece of the sun. Suppose we imagine a roughly circular
object sufficiently flat and shiny to appear as a mirror and let its
diameter be 80 ft. Then at 50 miles the angle is 0.3 milliradians.
The fraction of the sun which this small angle represents is about
(0.3 mr/8mr)^2 = 0.0014. (Squared because it is the area of the
mirror divided by the area of the sun's disc that determines the
 reflected solar "flux.") So you get roughly 0.14% of the sun's light
\being reflected (0.00014).
(Note: no spherical divergence here since the surface was assumed
to be flat; if a curved surface then the fraction must be reduced
 somewhat).
Now, the solar disc is about 1 to 2E5 times brighter than the sky (for
 experts: B = luminance = (1 to 2)E9 cd/m^2 for sun, and B = 1E4 cd/m^2
 for bright sky near the horizon; these numbers change with atmospheric
 conditions and the elevation of the sun and are approximate.
  E# represents 10 raised to a power, 10^#).
  Hence 0.0014 of the solar disc is still more than a hundred times
 brighter than the sky. Although one does not know the exact conditions
of sky brightness, nor the exact reflectivities of these objects, this
 calculation does suggest that the reflection would be easy to see
even over a distance of 50 miles.
.......
If one assumes the surface was curved, all bets are off as far as
calculating is concerned without knowledge of th radius of curvature.
However, that fact that Arnols reported these flashes at a distance
so great tht he couldn't see the objects themselves implies that the
curvature was not great (the radius of curvature was large).

Date: Tue, 28 Sep 1999 03:19:23 +0100
From: James Easton <voyager@ukonline.co.uk>
Subject: Everything You Think You Know...Message-id:
<008101bf0957$e1ed6720$88c828c3@cis.compuserve.com>

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

The following news release could be of interest:

Kathleen Burton
NASA Ames Research Center, Moffett Field, CA
(Phone: 650/604-1731 or 650/604-9000)
kburton@mail.arc.nasa.gov

Sept. 24, 1999

NOTE TO EDITORS: 99-58

NASA RESEARCHER FINDS EVIDENCE THAT THE UNIVERSE
MAY BE YOUNGER THAN PREVIOUSLY THOUGHT

Dr. Eyal Maoz of NASA Ames Research Center, Moffett Field, CA,
and astrophysicists from a variety of U.S. and Canadian
institutions have found evidence suggesting that the universe may
be younger than scientists had previously thought, and that it is
expanding faster than expected. Their findings are reported in
the Sept. 23 issue of Nature magazine.

Current estimates put the age of the universe at about 15 billion
years. Maoz' research indicates the universe may be as young as
12 billion years, nearly the same age as its oldest stars. This
implied relatively low age of the universe revives an old paradox
in the field of astrophysics that the universe seems to be
younger than some of the stars in it. The finding suggests that
a revision of the cosmological model may be required.

Maoz and his team used the Hubble Space Telescope to observe the
pulsing of giant stars called 'Cepheid variables' in the galaxy
NGC4258. Researchers used a standard "Cepheid measurement"
technique that allowed them to measure the distance from Earth to
the galaxy. However, this measurement was different from another
independent, highly accurate distance determination to that
galaxy made using masers (the microwave equivalent of lasers),
which are located at the galaxy center and orbiting a
supermassive black hole.

A revision of the standard Cepheid measurement method would mean
that estimates for the age of the Universe would have to be
revised downwards by 10-15%, experts say.
Measuring galactic distances using Cepheid variables has been a
standard since 1929. They are useful because their rate of
pulsation is closely linked to their brightness. This means that
a galaxys' apparent brightness can be used to gauge its distance
from Earth

Maoz and his colleagues used the Cepheid method to estimate the
distance from Earth to the benchmark NGC4258 galaxy as 8.1
megaparsecs (Mpc), significantly farther than the geometric
estimates derived by recent estimates. (One Mpc is equivalent to
approximately three million light years.)

"We discovered a considerable discrepancy between the maser-based
and Cepheid-based distance," Maoz said. "The bottom line is that
it seems that galaxy distances may have been consistently
overestimated by about 12%. This would imply that the universe is
expanding faster than expected, and the age of the universe is
lower by a similar factor."

-end-

To receive Ames press releases via email, send an email with the
word "subscribe" in subject line to:

ames-releases-request@lists.arc.nasa.gov

The NASA Ames Public Affairs Home Page is at URL:

http://ccf.arc.nasa.gov/dx
[End]

Indeed they are loud, especially on take-off (as all aircraft are) when max
power is used to get airborne. Even light aircraft make a hell of din on
take-off, but almost glide in for landing. I've seen many at my local
airport with props just about turning!! In the trade its called "the flare"
and the whole point of the exercise is to make the aircraft do what it is
was design not to do - that is stop flying :-)

>As usual, we'll probably never know. I suppose if a Vulcan was
>landing at that time, there might be still be a record of this
>'somewhere'.

All take-off's and landings should be logged by the tower, but how long the
records are kept by the RAF is anyone's guess.

BTW at that time Waddington was using its Vulcans in the maritime
reconnaissance role so night flying would probably have been involved. I
believe it was in support of Operation Tapestry (sp?).

Wednesday September 29 12:15 PM ET

CIA Sets Up Venture Capital Firm
By TOM RAUM Associated Press Writer

WASHINGTON (AP) - The CIA, not wanting to be left behind in the Internet age
or be outsmarted by tech-savvy adversaries, is teaming up with Silicon
Valley entrepreneurs to invest in companies developing computer technologies
that could assist in intelligence gathering.

Forgoing its usual clandestine ways, the agency has set up its own venture
capital firm - with money appropriated by Congress - with offices in
Washington and Palo Alto, Calif. It will invest in promising new start-up
hi-tech companies.

The CIA picked a fanciful name for the new company: In-Q-It. The ``In''
stands for intelligence. The ``It'' stands for information technology. And
the Q? That's the code name of the James Bond character who comes up with
all the gadgets that the fictional British spy uses.

``We do have a sense of humor,'' Central Intelligence Agency spokesman Bill
Harlow said today, confirming the existence of the new company.

Harlow said the venture capital company ``is clearly tied to us, but they
make a big point of being independent.''

The venture, first reported by The Washington Post and The New York Times in
today's editions, was actually set up last February as a nonprofit
organization.

But it is just now getting organized, with its own board of directors,
according to the new chief executive officer, Gilman Louie.

Louie said in an interview that the company would be small, with about 20 to
25 employees, and is being started with $28 million appropriated by Congress
last year as part of the classified budget for the agency.
Both Louie and the CIA said the venture capital company would work only on
unclassified projects.

Mainly, In-Q-It will invest in some high-tech companies and form joint
ventures with other ones where the companies are working on promising
technological projects that could benefit the CIA.

This includes ways of helping the CIA to use the Internet more effectively
and securely.

It also will try to find promising technologies that will help the CIA
better use the information it already possesses in a variety of forms, from
paper to computer files.

He cited the May 7 bombing of the Chinese embassy in Yugoslavia - a target
picked by the CIA - as ``the manifestation of the worst result that could
happen if you don't have all your information lined up.''

Louie, 39, founded his own electronic game company - MicroProse Inc. - that
was later bought by Hasbro. At Hasbro, Louie has been an executive with the
toy company's online business group.

He said he has no experience in espionage ``and I want to keep it that
way.''

The company's board of directors includes John Seely Brown, director of the
Xerox Corporation's Palo Alto Research Center; Norm Augustine, chairman of
Lockheed Martin; William Perry, the former defense secretary; and Jeong Kim
of Lucent.

Date: Sat, 02 Oct 1999 15:18:16 +0200
From: "Luis R. Gonzalez Manso" <lrgm@arrakis.es>
Subject: Linda Cortile's abduction Jerome Clark <jkclark@frontiernet.net>, Antonio
Huneeus <huneeus@idt.net>,
euroufolist@oasi.asti.it
UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Dear colleagues,

Let me quote from Hopkins' last book (Witnessed, paperback edition, Pocket
Books):
p. 23: "The episode in which she apparently spoke in an "alien tongue" was
something I had never encountered before"
p. 129: "Until Linda's hypnosis session I had never heard of an abductee
being temporarily "taken over" by the UFO occupants and behaving as if he or
she were in complete sympathy with the aliens, wholly accepting their goals
and techniques",
p. 219: "this discovery of the aliens' interest in studying human
relationships and eventual sexual "bonding" from childhood through maturity
is one of the most important contribution of the Linda Cortile case"
Apart from the spectacular abduction in the middle of Manhattan on November
30th 1989, these were (according to Hopkins) the main novelties offered by
Linda Cortile, specially the third.

I had finally obtained (and READ) a copy of a thriller published in April
1989 (BEFORE the alleged abduction). I would summarize its story as follows:

In fact, aliens are time travellers, coming from our future. They were
genetic engineered Earth soldiers send to fight an interstelar war that they
won. Their genetic stock comes from a very small group of survivors after
almost all the life on Earth was destroyed by a ¿solar flare? So they had to
come to their past with a double strategy: a) establish a sexual “bonding”
from childhood between those who are to survive; b) collect genetic material
from the rest of humanity in order to replenish their stock. They tell each
abductee what he wants to hear, and some of them are in complete sympathy
with the aliens. One of the main characters even speak their “alien tongue”.

(As a curiosity, the portrait of the only ufologist to appear is not
pleasant: he takes advantage of his female abductees and he is really an
abductee and an ally of the aliens, covering their mistakes when he pretends
to investigate. Finally, he dies aboard a UFO deceived until his end)

This is too much of a coincidence. The three main points in Linda Cortile’s
abduction were written several months before the alleged abduction. This is,
at least, a clear evidence of a sociological influence or, in the worst
scenario, proof of a hoax.

That, being important, is not the main point of this message.

As some of you may have already guessed, I am referring to “Nighteyes” by
Garfield Reeves-Stevens, the novel that Stefula, Butler & Hansen suggested
as “a possible literary basis for elements of Linda’s abduction”.

Let me, once again, quote Hopkins (IUR March/April 1993 p. 12):

“Now the truth is that apparently no one except Butler finds any similarity
between the novel and Linda’s account (...) As is typical of its genre,
“Nighteyes” contains literally thousands of details (...) Apparently Butler
sat down at this lurid smorgasbord and picked whatever details he thought
might fit the case and ignored all the rest. But the biggest hole in his
arguments is, as I’ve said, the complete absence in the novel of the core
events of the Cortile case”

Of course, in a simple way, it is truth that the similarities between both
accounts depend on the level of detail. For instance, Richard and Dan are
security and intelligence agents but the characters in the novel are FBI
agents. Is that a suspicious parallel? It depends on who is reading.

But what should have been evident both to sceptics and believers, if they
really READ the novel, is the unavoidable coincidences not between events
but between the novelties, the discoveries, offered by Linda Cortile and the
main elements of the plot story. After reading the novel (with its
interesting suggestions about memory-erasing gas, forensic investigations,
etc.) nobody can legitimately deny that the “never-before-heard-of
contributions” of Linda case were already an important element in the plot
of a mass-market thriller.

Let me put it more clearly. The most amazing point made in Hopkins’ book,
the cornerstone of Linda Cortile’s case, was how the aliens had orchestrated
the lifes of two abductees in order to reunite them one night in lower
Manhattan for an apocalyptic message. The main surprise of Nighteyes’ plot
(besides the aliens being humans) is when two apparently independent
abductees met again, in order to become the founders of a future race. How
can anybody miss the paralelism?

If the trees do not let them see the forest, Mr. Hopkins (and the other
colleagues who agree with him after reading the novel) are not good
investigators. But if they did see the forest but preferred not to say so,
that is even worse.

My conclusion: Beware of personal opinions! Try to evaluate the raw data by
yourself. Please, do not even believe me. Read the novel and reach your own
conclusions. To me the precedent is obvious.

Luis R. González Manso

Voyager Newsletter - Issue No. 8

* Nick Pope - The Ministry of Defence Respond *


On 7 August, 1999, I published the following:

'An Open Letter to Nick Pope'

Dear Nick,

In the July issue of 'NICK POPE'S WEIRD WORLD', you wrote:

"Over the past few months I'd been becoming more bullish in my
response to certain people within ufology who'd been sniping at
me over the years. Nobody likes criticism, and I'd been getting a
fair bit - little of it constructive in nature. If people were
criticising my views on, say, Roswell, then fine. I wasn't there,
and so my view probably counts no more or no less than anybody
else who's followed the case with a reasonable degree of
interest. But it rankled when outsiders who'd probably never even
visited MOD Main Building started casting doubts on my knowledge
about - and access to - government and military UFO files. I've
worked for the MOD for over fourteen years now, and three of
those were spent researching and investigating UFO sightings,
alien abductions, crop circles, animal mutilations and any other
weird and wonderful reports that came my way".


I trust I'm not one of the aforementioned 'critics' and perhaps
you can help clear up some of the confusion which surrounds a
number of claims.

To recap; your appointment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD) was
as an Executive Officer. To clarify for the 'uninitiated' (I'm a
former Civil Servant), the standard grading hierarchy is clerical
assistant - clerical officer - executive officer - higher
executive officer - and upwards.

Although your affirmation clearly gives the impression of being
HM Government's full-time investigator of "UFO sightings, alien
abductions, crop circles, animal mutilations", etc., I understand
that was not the situation.
Weren't your duties varied and 'UFO etc. reports' only one
aspect? In possibly the first 'promotional' interview you gave,
to 'UFO Magazine' (UK) on 5 May, 1996, it was stated:

UFO Magazine: When did you join this office, and indeed, were you
aware of its function?

Nick Pope: I've been in the Ministry of Defence since 1985. We
are just 'posted around' every two or three years to acquire
experience. I had just finished various duties associated with
the Gulf War and it just so happened that there was a vacancy
which cropped-up. Also in this office was a chap I had worked
with quite closely with Gulf War duties and he offered me the
job. I was aware that UFO research was one of its functions.

UFO: Was this the reason you switched departments?

Nick Pope: I was certainly interested, it sounded fascinating,
but I was quite keen to get out of my old job.
[End]

As you said, "UFO research was one of its functions".

Can you please clarify what the job title was and its other
functions?

What percentage of your appointment was actually spent on 'UFO
etc.' related matters?

Was it, for example, a situation where the 'UFO etc.' duties took
up, approximately, 75 percent of your time, 50 percent, or did
they only perhaps demand a few hours per week, maybe even, over a
period of three years, average a few hours each month?

It's obviously of interest to know how much emphasis our
government put on this and whether it continues to do so.


On the question of any 'cover-up', you helpfully confirmed and
have maintained this had no substance whatsoever. Typical of your
response was the one given to Michael Lindemann, editor of 'CNI
News', on November 17, 1996, during a 'UFO conference' at
Blackpool.

Lindemann asked, "This seemingly irrational denial of significant
UFO events could be interpreted as evidence of a deliberate
cover-up. What are your views on that?".

To which you replied, "I found no evidence to support a cover-up
in Britain. I think, without trying to sound too arrogant, that I
would have gotten a few hints in three years if there had been
someone doing my job but on a covert basis, not least because the
one thing they would have needed beyond anything else was access
to the raw data of the witnesses, and never once in three years
had any witness complained that I had sent someone around to the
house".

PRESS RELEASE

'Operation Thunder Child'
by Nick Pope

Although ostensibly a techno-thriller, the Ministry of Defence
insisted on seeing the manuscript and making some changes. They
had the book for three months - longer than for most of the books
written by former SAS soldiers - before giving it final clearance
to publish.

Nick Pope has dipped into the 'real x-files', and packed the book
with references to formerly classified UFO events investigated by
the MOD.

Many of the events are thinly disguised versions of the real
events. Fictionalisation is the only way that MOD official Nick
Pope can talk about some of the more controversial incidents.

Examples of reality disguised as fiction include:

1 The Rendlesham Forest incident, which appears in the prologue,
inspired some of, and reflects, what Nick Pope was told by United
Nations Air Force officers.

2 The alleged downing of an RAF Lightning by a UFO in 1970, which
inspired some of the aerial battles that appear throughout the
book.
3 The UFO briefing that the Minister receives in chapter four is
based on a brief Nick Pope gave to a Defence Minister in 1982.
All the incidents described actually occurred.

4 The potential biological hazard from extraterrestrial contact
as described in chapter nine was an issue that Nick Pope raised
with his MOD bosses while on the UFO desk.

5 The descriptions of the shape and capabilities of the UFO's,
and the physical description and behaviour of the aliens are
based on actual UFO reports and alien abduction claims
investigated by Nick Pope as part of his official MOD duties.

Many scenes give insights into 'spin-doctoring' techniques,
showing how Governments manipulate Parliament and the public, and
manage the media.

Nick Pope has worked for the Ministry of Defence for fourteen
years. As well as a tour of duty spent researching and
investigating UFOs he has been involved in highly classified work
on the Gulf War, Bosnia and Kosovo.

This book contains a wealth of authentic detail about rules of
engagement, weapons systems and tactics although some details
have had to be changed for national security reasons.

Nick Pope will be appearing at KULTURE SHOCK on Sunday 10th
October 1999, from 12.30 when he will be talking about his work,
answering questions and signing copies of his books.

Advance booking is advised!

Contact DAVID for further details
[END]
