How? Our email site is a mainframe accessable only by Pine.


I was refering to ONLY the 2000 (10 pm) sighting in my above
remarks, although a gray background was also reported on an
earlier flight.


I did a detailed study of this case. There were actually 9
different events on 3/13/97:

#1. A flight of lights was seen in the Paulden area from 2000 to
2016.

#2. A flight of lights in the Prescott area. 4-5 lights in a
rough triangle moved slowly over the area, from 2015 to 2020.

#3. A flight of lights over the Phoenix area, including Chandler.
5-7 lights in a rough vee, from 2023 to 2035. The lights went out
one by one. This was the flight where a transparent object was
seen behind the lights.

#4. A flight of lights over the Tucson and Saddlebrook area.
These were seen from 2045 to 2100. They were in a straight line
as seen from Tucson, but a diamond shape was seen from
Saddlebrook.

#5. Another flight of lights over the Chandler area (south of
Phoenix) from 2050 to 2100. 7 lights in a row with another light
following it.

#6. Another flight of lights was observed in the Ahwatuckee area
from 2130 to 3135.

#7. A line of ten lights was seen south of Scottsdale at 2200.
This is the flight that was taped, and was identified as the
flare drop exercise.
#8. One light to the west of Phoenix at 2200 was chased by 3 jets
from Luke AFB, and also observed from the ground. Another was
seen toward the northeast.

#9. A large cluster of lights was seen to the north from Kingman
just before midnight.



Notice these facts:

A. The lights seen in Paulden disappeared just as the Prescott
area started seeing lights.

B. The Prescott lights had disappeared before the Phoenix area
started seeing lights.

C. The lights seen in Phoenix (group 3) went out one-by-one WHILE
the lights were still visible in Tucson. They did not go below
the horizon. This means they WERE NOT the same lights.

D. ALL of the lights moved south, including the flare drop.

E. The flare drop establishes the wind direction.

F. No reports came from intervening towns.

G. The Hale-Bopp "UFO" had just been revealed.

H. Heavensgate was in the news.

I. Spring break was in progress at many college campuses.

J. None of the individual lights did anything inconsistent with
fire balloons, EXCEPT the lights identified as the flare
drop. What about the jet chase? The "Gorman effect" explains the
maneuvers reported nicely.

K. None of the objects appeared on RADAR.

L. Previous flare drops had already been seen from Ahwatuckee on
the 10th, 11th, and 12th, and reported as a UFO in the media.
That's why people were ready with their video recorders.

M. It is amazing the number of fire balloons that appear in an
area after a major UFO event ispublicized. I counted 7 cases of
confirmed fire balloons (some with multiple objects), plus 1
probable fire baloon case (plus who knows how many cases too
tenuous to identify), plus 1 case of people dressed up in foil
suits, all in Indiana during the 1973 UFO wave.
The following scenarios present themselves:

1. A group of students (probably all members of the same
fraternity house) on spring break decided to create a sensational
UFO sighting. They stationed groups of people at various points
along a straight line and had them sequentially release fire
balloons according to a schedule they worked out. Later, more
balloons were released in the Phoenix area.

This sounds similar to an frat initiation project that happened
here in Bloomington Indiana in the 1970s, when Bigfoot tracks
started appearing in the snow everywhere around campus. Since the
tracks were flat (made by boards cut to shape and strapped to
boots), the hoax was obvious to any serious investigator. The
story did not go beyond the student newspaper.

2. Members of the Heavensgate cult planned and released the fire
balloons, intending this sighting to be coupled with the "earth
ship takeoff" the same month.

3. The military released lighted balloons, in an effort to keep
the rabid UFOzos busy while they were doing something in Area 51.
This is much less likely than the other two possibilities.

4. Somebody else did it. The two isolated fire balloons aloft
during the jet chase were probably launched independently of the
others.



Other information needed.

The plastic bag aerostats of the fire balloons explain the
"yellow moon" effect.

A falling candle fits the reported "LASER beam effect." This is a
common occurrance in fire balloon cases, and is one of the
identifying features of a fire balloon.

The Gorman effect is named after pilot George Gorman, who on
10/1/48 had an aerial dogfight with a UFO over Fargo ND. He
reported that as he tried to identify the UFO, it repeatedly made
ramming attacks on him, and turned tighter than he could. This
was the first report of this kind. The UFO was identified as a
lighted weather balloon released from the base, but not until
1/26/53, when the same thing happened again in New Mexico.

The pilot (anonymous) in the New Mexico case insisted he had NOT
chased a balloon. His commanding officer decided to do an
experiment: The next night, he ordered the pilot up again, and
then had a lighted balloon released. The entire episode happened
again! After that, they were all convinced that the original
object was the station weather balloon released shortly before
the "dogfight." The solution was then applied to the Gorman case.

This illustrates dramatically the fact that, against the night
sky, NOBODY with unaided eyes can find the size, distance, or
speed of an unfamiliar object that is farther away than 30 feet.
In this case, the pilot grossly overestimated the size of the
object. That distorted his distance and speed estimates in a way
that made him experience ramming attacks by the object. The light
was really almost stationary, and the entire ramming effect was
caused by the speed of the pilot's own airplane, coupled with his
overestimate of its size.



Again, there is nothing (other than the flare drops) in the
3/13/97 Phoenix case that can NOT be explained by a series of
flights by fire balloons. The estimates of size, distance, and
speed were distorted by the unexpectedly small sizes of the
objects there too.

How? Our email site is a mainframe accessible only by Pine.


I was referring to ONLY the 2000 (10 pm) sighting in my above
remarks, although a gray background was also reported on an
earlier flight.


I did a detailed study of this case. There were actually 9
different events on 3/13/97:

#1. A flight of lights was seen in the Paulden area from 2000 to
2016.

#2. A flight of lights in the Prescott area. 4-5 lights in a
rough triangle moved slowly over the area, from 2015 to 2020.

#3. A flight of lights over the Phoenix area, including Chandler.
5-7 lights in a rough vee, from 2023 to 2035. The lights went out
one by one. This was the flight where a transparent object was
seen behind the lights.

#4. A flight of lights over the Tucson and Saddlebrook area.
These were seen from 2045 to 2100. They were in a straight line
as seen from Tucson, but a diamond shape was seen from
Saddlebrook.

#5. Another flight of lights over the Chandler area (south of
Phoenix) from 2050 to 2100. 7 lights in a row with another light
following it.

#6. Another flight of lights was observed in the Ahwatuckee area
from 2130 to 2135.

#7. A line of ten lights was seen south of Scottsdale at 2200.
This is the flight that was taped, and was identified as the
flare drop exercise.

#8. One light to the west of Phoenix at 2200 was chased by 3 jets
from Luke AFB, and also observed from the ground. Another was
seen toward the northeast.

#9. A large cluster of lights was seen to the north from Kingman
just before midnight.



Notice these facts:

A. The lights seen in Paulden disappeared just as the Prescott
area started seeing lights.

B. The Prescott lights had disappeared before the Phoenix area
started seeing lights.

C. The lights seen in Phoenix (group 3) went out one-by-one WHILE
the lights were still visible in Tucson. They did not go below
the horizon. This means they WERE NOT the same lights.

D. ALL of the lights moved south, including the flare drop.

E. The flare drop establishes the wind direction.

F. No reports came from intervening towns.

G. The Hale-Bopp "UFO" had just been revealed.

H. Heavensgate was in the news.

I. Spring break was in progress at many college campuses.

J. None of the individual lights did anything inconsistent with
fire balloons, EXCEPT the lights identified as the flare
drop. What about the jet chase? The "Gorman effect" explains the
maneuvers reported nicely.

K. None of the objects appeared on RADAR.

L. Previous flare drops had already been seen from Ahwatuckee on
the 10th, 11th, and 12th, and reported as a UFO in the media.
That's why people were ready with their video recorders.

M. It is amazing the number of fire balloons that appear in an
area after a major UFO event is publicized. I counted 7 cases of
confirmed fire balloons (some with multiple objects), plus 1
probable fire balloon case (plus who knows how many cases too
tenuous to identify), plus 1 case of people dressed up in foil
suits, all in Indiana during the 1973 UFO wave.


The following scenarios present themselves:

1. A group of students (probably all members of the same
fraternity house) on spring break decided to create a sensational
UFO sighting. They stationed groups of people at various points
along a straight line and had them sequentially release fire
balloons according to a schedule they worked out. Later, more
balloons were released in the Phoenix area.

This sounds similar to an frat initiation project that happened
here in Bloomington Indiana in the 1970s, when Bigfoot tracks
started appearing in the snow everywhere around campus. Since the
tracks were flat (made by boards cut to shape and strapped to
boots), the hoax was obvious to any serious investigator. The
story did not go beyond the student newspaper.

2. Members of the Heavensgate cult planned and released the fire
balloons, intending this sighting to be coupled with the "earth
ship takeoff" the same month.

3. The military released lighted balloons, in an effort to keep
the rabid UFOzos busy while they were doing something in Area 51.
This is much less likely than the other two possibilities.

4. Somebody else did it. The two isolated fire balloons aloft
during the jet chase were probably launched independently of the
others.



Other information needed.

The plastic bag aerostats of the fire balloons explain the
"yellow moon" effect.

A falling candle fits the reported "LASER beam effect." This is a
common occurrence in fire balloon cases, and is one of the
identifying features of a fire balloon.
The Gorman effect is named after pilot George Gorman, who on
10/1/48 had an aerial dogfight with a UFO over Fargo ND. He
reported that as he tried to identify the UFO, it repeatedly made
ramming attacks on him, and turned tighter than he could. This
was the first report of this kind. The UFO was identified as a
lighted weather balloon released from the base, but not until
1/26/53, when the same thing happened again in New Mexico.

The pilot (anonymous) in the New Mexico case insisted he had NOT
chased a balloon. His commanding officer decided to do an
experiment: The next night, he ordered the pilot up again, and
then had a lighted balloon released. The entire episode happened
again! After that, they were all convinced that the original
object was the station weather balloon released shortly before
the "dogfight." The solution was then applied to the Gorman case.

This illustrates dramatically the fact that, against the night
sky, NOBODY with unaided eyes can find the size, distance, or
speed of an unfamiliar object that is farther away than 30 feet.
In this case, the pilot grossly overestimated the size of the
object. That distorted his distance and speed estimates in a way
that made him experience ramming attacks by the object. The light
was really almost stationary, and the entire ramming effect was
caused by the speed of the pilot's own airplane, coupled with his
overestimate of its size.



Again, there is nothing (other than the flare drops) in the
3/13/97 Phoenix case that can NOT be explained by a series of
flights by fire balloons. The estimates of size, distance, and
speed were distorted by the unexpectedly small sizes of the
objects there too.

From: James Easton <voyager@ukonline.co.uk>
Subject: 'Triangular' UFOs Outwith the USMessage-id:
<008f01bf4cff$632c91e0$981486d4@voyager>
References: <199912211636_MC2-9202-29FB@compuserve.com>

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

A new UK magazine called 'Destiny', is essentially a
'horoscope/fortune telling' etc. publication.

However, the first issue also contains an article on the
'Bonnybridge triangle', namely 'UFO' reports from that area in
central Scotland.

The article was mentioned to myself by someone who thought it may
be of interest. I wondered if it might contain any accounts of a
'triangular UFO' - having by now come to expect this in any
contemporary 'flap'.

One story featured is the following:

Christine Grimley, 40, is typical of many of the residents of
Falkirk. The busy mother of two didn't believe a word of what she
had read in the papers until she saw a UFO with her own eyes
three years ago. To this day she is aghast at what she saw, and
is desperate for an explanation.

"On January 20, 1996, I went to bed at about midnight. At around
2 a.m., my 14-year-old-son, John, was distressed and woke to tell
me he could see strange lights in the sky."

Christine got out of bed and saw the pulsating and indigo lights,
too. At first, she thought they were from an aeroplane, but then
something strange happened. The lights dropped to ground level,
zigzagged across the sky, then hovered above houses in the next
street.

Terrified, Christine grabbed some binoculars and made out the
silhouette of an arrow-shaped vessel, to which the smaller lights
seemed to attach and detach at random. Then, to her utter shock
and amazement, they started coming towards her house.

Running into the front garden, the Grimleys saw the craft hover
over the house in complete silence. "It was massive - bigger than
any aeroplane I've ever seen," remembers Christine with a
shudder. "It's hard to explain, because I've never seen anything
like it before, but I could tell it definitely wasn't a normal
aircraft."
Once over the house, the UFO shot diagonally into the sky and,
Christine claims, straight into the path of an aeroplane. Her
family stood huddled together, thinking they were about to
witness a disaster. Christine's daughter, Jenna was so terrified
she began hyperventilating.

"And then suddenly it disappeared," says Christine, still amazed.
"To this day, I don't understand why nobody on the plane reported
seeing it flying towards them. I honestly can't believe they
didn't see it."
[End]


If 'arrow-shaped' might equate with something seemingly
triangular, this tale has classic ingredients of many other
'triangular' UFO sightings - the 'object' was first perceived to
be distant lights, it then apparently 'approached' the observers,
was 'massive', hovered in silence and departed somewhat rapidly.

The article includes a photograph of Christine and her children,
which at least appears to indicate the story isn't a magazine
fabrication.

Ideally, we could see individual sketches of what they recall -
pity these and detailed testimonies weren't taken soon as
possible.


Does the 'arrow-shaped' description support my contention that
what _we_ categorise as 'triangular UFOs' still isn't a hyped
'UFO' shape?

There are a couple of possible examples in the National UFO
Reporting Center data (spelling uncorrected) previously
mentioned:

Occurred : 8/16/1996 20:15 (Entered as : 8/16/96 20:153)
Reported : 12/3/1998 01:34
Posted : 12/15/1998
Location : Santa Barbara, CA

My wife and I were walking towards our car through the back
parking lot of Andreas Restaurant after dinner. I was looking
towards the direction of where the car was parked when I noticed
with my right field of view, a very large dark object that was
moving from East to West just above tree top. The event happened
so fast that I could barely point fast enough with my hand (while
yelling Look..Look!) towards the object, hoping to get my wife's
attention. Even though black in color, it had dimly glowing light
along all the bottom edges and the sihlouette of the object was
easily distinguished as a large silent triangle. The scene was
fairly quiet and I was able to clearly hear in the background the
motor noise of a small plane, during and well after the event
took place. I was so shook up with my heart pounding that I could
hardly breathe.

[...]

I noted that from the perspective that I saw it dissapear behing
the trees, it looked more like a wide arrow head but was flat
across the back.

[...]


Occurred : 7/1/1978 22:00 (Entered as : july, 1978 10:00 pm)
Reported : 1/18/1999 12:00
Posted : 2/16/1999
Location : Monsey, NY

My boyfriend and I saw a triangular shaped object spinning in
circles, lights rotating..It jut across the evening sky within
the stars in different directions e.g. stop - go- lights
spinning-jut-stop -go -jut- spin- in different directions almost
like the arrow of a computer mouse until it left our sight. I'll
never forget it. It was the most amazing thing that I had ever
witnessed. We thought we were looking at a satellite, until we
were informed that satellites are constant... do not spin nor
jut.

The object was triagular. It must have been huge, because we
could see it vividly within the stars. It had lights all around
it that only shined around it when it was stopped. When the
U.F.O. moved, the arrow heard would point into the direction it
was travelling to-then jut to that position. Stop -spin-lights
also spinning- point into another direction ..then jut to that
position. It did this until it was out of our focus range.
[End]


Incidentally, the above account seems to be another which
features the 'skipping' or 'snapping' motion recently discussed.


Re the 'Grimley' case, I suppose it all comes back to the same
'logical' conclusion; that if it is an accurate report, there's
really no way it can be rationalised as a 'black' aircraft.

What evidence have we seen which indicates any comparative report
can realistically be absorbed as a 'secret' aircraft, utilising
technology which we seem to conclude has no evidential 'paper
trail'. For example and by comparison, 'stealth' technology is a
well documented and natural development from ongoing research.


Just another of them 'UFO' reports?

By default, yes.

Although... it has to be said that this apparent 'housewife'
account of an 'arrow-shaped vessel' with lights that reportedly
left and reattached, which "was massive" and maybe hovered "over
the house in complete silence", originating from central Scotland
is, considering our overall perspective, intriguing.

I know it's not the only conceivable 'triangular UFO' case from
there and separately recall a TV interview with local and
relatively well known UFO researcher Malcolm Robinson, when he
had some of his files open and I noticed they contained sketches
of 'triangular shaped' objects.

If anyone can provide contact details for Malcolm, it would be
appreciated.


James.

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Hi Larry,

NORAD cannot and does not hide ALL spy satellites -- most DO get
cataloged/located and there is an amateur community tracking such satellites and
supplying orbital element sets (elsets). By international treaty all satellite launches
must be registered with COSPAR and given an International Designation (such as
1999-13C). The trick is when there are multiple satellites released from an unmanned
mission or from a Space Shuttle. The "hidden" satellites are from these piggyback
flights. Still, some of these are eventually found out from detection of signals or
optically (there are reportedly some "sleeper" sats with no transmissions, painted with
Stealth absoptive coatings etc. but then these DON'T MAKE SETI SIGNAL
PROBLEMS EITHER).

This still doesn't change the fact that SETI astronomers can observe telltale Doppler
shifts of a satellite. If in Near Earth Orbit it is obvious when the Doppler shifts
approach orbital velocity of 8 km/sec.

What cases are there of NORAD hiding spy satellites from Gemini astronauts who
saw them? This would be LIFE THREATENING and dangerous. NORAD and
NASA have an agreement whereby NORAD is required to warn NASA of any close
approaches of ANY orbiting object to a manned NASA space mission. Since NASA
can and does handle classified information there wouldn't be a problem with
disclosing some spy satellite, especially since all NORAD needs to do is give a
NORAD Catalog Number and the close approach parameters, not identify the
satellite's classified mission.

This sounds to me like a desperate effort to explain away Gemini UFO cases which
even Jim Oberg never resorted to.

Brad Sparks

Date: Wed, 29 Dec 1999 18:05:42 -0500 (EST)
From: RB47Expert@aol.com
Subject: Re: SETI signals?Message-id: <0.d1a33f8a.259bedc6@aol.com>

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Most spy satellites are SIGINT (signals intelligence) satellites for eavesdropping on
communications, radar transmissions and other electronic emissions. Photorecon sats
are fewer in number than SIGINT and very few make film drops -- most send
digitized images. Many SIGINT sats are in geosynchronous orbit in order to provide
continuous 24-hour coverage. Many are in lower orbits for better reception.

Anyway, the point is that SETI astronomers would have to be brain damaged if they
could not see a Doppler shift of 8 km/sec and figure out it is an Earth orbital satellite
just from the characteristic 8 km/sec velocity alone (the geosynch spy sats would have
much smaller Doppler shifts but then there are other clues see NEXT -->). Then there
is the ENCRYPTED DIGITAL SIGNALS which should be pretty obvious. And if
they can't figure it out from the DOPPLER or the ENCRYPTED SIGNALS they
could get INTERFEROMETRY which could triangulate the location as in Earth orbit.

Brad Sparks

From: Jacques Poulet <jpoulet@chucara.com>
Subject: Abductions & Aliens

UFO Research List - http://web.ukonline.co.uk/voyager/

Abductions & Aliens : What 's Really Going On?
By Chris A. Rutkowski
Dundurn Press

The first books I bought when I started reading about UFOs, were books on
abductions. "Intruders" fascinated me. Soon after reading "Communion", I
went to hear Budd Hopkins at a local conference, here in Montreal.

I later learned of the MJ-12 affair and tried desperately to find answers
to both subjects. Finding elements contrary to what I had recently read,
and heard, I quickly realised that no one could be entirely believed in
ufology. You have to verify everything yourself or be very confident in
those you accept to trust.

The MJ-12 theory was full of holes and no one really knew what was
happening to abductees. I decided that I would not get involved in either
of them. I kept informed but that's all. The few TV shows on those subjects
and the information I saw on the net were enough.

When I heard that Chris Rutkowski had written a book on abductions, I
couldn't believe it. Here was a highly respected ufologist, with a solid
scientific background, writing about a subject full of controversy (much
worse than UFO sightings themselves) and with much less physical evidences
than mainstream ufology. I though it was time for me to read another
abduction book.

What a refreshing read. Those who wants to believe in "alien abducting
people" will not like it. The same with those "nay-sayer" called skeptics.
But if you're looking for answers, you must read this book. You wont find
any. What you'll find is information that popular abduction researchers
aren't telling you.

Chris Rutkowski has written a "must read" with lots of information. With a
touch of humour, he present abductions as a phenomenon that no one really
understand yet. In doing so, he points flaws in current pet theory of
leading researchers (they wont like you!). His logical thinking bring the
subject back to what it really is: a mystery. At the same time, he shows
compassion for those abductees who trusted him with their stories,
acknowledging that what they experienced can not be catalogue, simply, as
being "all in their head".

Well done! I highly recommend this book to those who would want a summary
of current state of alien abduction research. You'll get it as it is, pro
or con.
Chris, I have to tell you that, contrary to some rumours you may have
heard, the popularity of Star Trek is not waning.

As Brad knows well, Gemini 11 had a visual/photographic sighting of an
unknown which NORAD initially identified as a piece of orbiting debris
(Proton 3 booster) . Oberg published several articles with this
identification. These publications came AFTER Brad and I independently
proved that the Proton booster was about 3000 miles behind (and to the
right) of the GT-11 craft and could not have been the object which appeared
at their left and seemed to pass jus below them. The duration of th
sighting (many seconds to minute?) indicates that the GT-11 and the unknown
were on nearly parallel tracks: the object moved a distance of a couple of
kilometers or so (estmate) transverse to the travel path of the GT -11
while the GT-11 traveled perhaps as far as 500 km along its track (at
about 8 km/sec). Hence the angle between the paths was on the order of (1
to 2)/500 ...
Een NASA agreed thatthe object was unknown. Oberg eventually admitted
that he couldn't identify it.... yet left it "open" as to whether or not it
could have been some unknown satellite (either a very large satellite...
or several obects i close association).

> followed "space age folklore" with fascination all my life. I've written

> links from my home page), from a sympathetically skeptical point of view, and
> have researched many reports deeply.
>

> it's one of those incidents that most deeply puzzles me, as a "UFO skeptic".
> I've known and respected John Schuessler (not "John Husler" as the script
> writer erred!!) for many years through our work for NASA. I am less convinced
> that Ms. Hill's symptoms are all that characteristic of 'radiation
> poisoning', however, and her pre-encounter medical records -- which might
> cast more light on the post-encounter symptoms -- have been inexplicably but
> staunchly kept secret by pro-UFO investigators.
>
> I do feel that you gave far too much credence to factually-suspect assertions
> by Whitley Strieber, even though many claims -- ranging from the phantom
> "object" in his ear lob
>
> For example, when Strieber calls the STS-80 space shuttle dots "the best
> piece of UFO video I know of", he's advertising how little he really knows
> about real space flight. I've looked at this case very closely because of my
> decades of work in Mission Control, and it's clear to me that the dots are
> exactly what Story Musgrave (who was on that flight) said they were:
>
> "Washers, screws, chips of ice -- they all rotate at their own velocities. So
> it's really marvelous that after they get far enough away from you, all the
> lights are just on and off like blinking lights, as they reflect -- their
> reflective surfaces rotate in the sun."
>
> The STS-80 "UFO case" (and a similar famous case on STS-48) occurred just at
> sunrise, as the shuttle moves into sunlight while the Earth's surface remains
> dark. Sunlit nearby debris shows up as tiny dots, often pulsating. Some other
> pieces are still close enough to the shuttle that they are in its shadow, and
> only appear suddenly as they drift out into the sunlight. This happened
> against the cloud background on STS-80, against the horizon on STS-48, and
> against deep space on STS-63 and other missions from which I've collected
> video. With a little bit of real research (something that ufologists as a
> rule tend to avoid lest they "ruin" useful stories), dozens of cases of other
> similar views which are clearly shuttle-derived debris can be found.
>
> Yet this normal spaceflight visual phenomenon. It dates all the way back to
> John Glenn's first flight and the "fireflies" he spotted -- snowflakes off
> the external evaporative cooler). It is widely misrepresented, in Strieber's
> books and elsewhere, with a collection of false "facts" and with a careful
> avoidance of explanatory facts that might "confuse" the target audience that
> ufo buffs are trying to persuade and/or entertain.
>
> In my opinion, Steve Bassett's comments were particularly inane. There was
> his promotion of a hoax story of Gordon Cooper's "Mercury Sighting" ("Cooper
> was ordered to keep silent" -- a patent falsehood, since he's an outspoken
> advocate of the reality of UFOs and talks widely about his own earthside
> encounters). The story was actually a hoax exposed decades ago, literally,
> but still to this day carefully nurtured in the mainstream 'UFO literature'.
> Then there was the assertion that "the DoD is NASA's boss", a plainly stupid
> lie.
>
> Robert Kiviat, once bitten by the "Alien Autopsy" hoax (what does that show
